docs.contentMd:
# Ada / Chaba / Devin / Tony — How the Team Works

**Updated:** 2026-09-28

Four roles, one loop: **Tony decides, Ada captures and answers, Chaba remembers and routes, Devin builds.**

## Roles

- **Tony** — the operator. Decides what matters; nothing risky ships without his yes.
- **Ada** — the voice. Answers questions, controls the home, saves memories, confirms before acting.
- **Chaba** (ชบา) — the memory + SSOT. Where facts, plans, focus items, and reports live; what Devin reads before working.
- **Devin** — the builder. Turns handed-off ideas into code, docs, and verified changes.

## Which door to use

| Focus | Talk to | Path |
|---|---|---|
| Home / daily life | Ada (ada-ha-tony, :8002) | direct voice — lights, cameras, calendar, remember-this |
| Dev / infrastructure | Devin (chaba repo session) | dispatch or interactive — worktree, SSOT, commit |
| Idea mid-conversation | Ada → "send this to Devin" | lands in devin-handoff bank + focus inbox |
| Experiments / risky stuff | ada-dev (:8005) — the lab | can't touch the house; scenarios prove behavior first |
| Reports for review | CMS pages | Ada/Devin write, Tony reads and approves |

## The seam: voice → handoff → build

The useful pattern is the bridge, not the endpoints:

```
Tony thinks aloud to Ada
    → Ada files it (devin-handoff bank / focus-inbox yml)
    → a Devin session picks it up
    → code lands, scenario proves it
    → report page updates for Tony's review
```

Tony never re-types. Ada never codes. Devin never guesses intent — the handoff carries it.

## Examples

1. **"Remember the gate code is under the keypad"** → Ada asks once, saves to personal bank. Next week Ada recalls it. No Devin needed.

2. **"Ada, send this flood-news-page idea to Devin"** → handoff item `handoff-*.yml` appears in focus inbox → next Devin session builds the CMS page + the automation.

3. **"Is the camera-cast ask gate working?"** → Devin runs `camera_cast_permission` scenario → PASS report lands in the ops-scenarios bank → Ada can answer "yes, verified today".

4. **Voice enrollment breaks** → Tony tells Ada the symptom → Devin reads the transcript, finds the stale-profile guard, removes profiles, Tony re-enrolls → `voice-bench.py` now regression-tests it.

5. **A risky new tool** → built and tested on ada-dev (:8005) first — if the lab scenario passes, it promotes to prod. House never sees a half-tested tool.

6. **Backups looked fine but weren't** → the restore drill (Devin) proved /v1/backup output was corrupt → filecopy+verify tier added → tonight's backup is proven openable.

## Rules the team plays by

- Ada never claims success a tool result didn't show (result-truth rule)
- Anything that captures, publishes, writes, or actuates needs an explicit yes — enforced server-side
- Devin deploys to prod only on same-session approval
- Reports are bilingual — en + th docs under one slug

# Ada / Chaba / Devin / Tony — ทีมทำงานยังไง

**อัปเดตล่าสุด:** 2026-09-28

สี่บทบาท ลูปเดียว: **Tony ตัดสินใจ, Ada รับฟังและตอบ, Chaba จำและส่งต่อ, Devin สร้าง**

## บทบาท

- **Tony** — เจ้าของระบบ เลือกว่าอะไรสำคัญ; ไม่มีอะไรเสี่ยงออกไปโดยไม่ได้ยืนยัน
- **Ada** — เสียงพูด ตอบคำถาม คุมบ้าน จำเรื่องต่างๆ และขอยืนยันก่อนลงมือเสมอ
- **Chaba** (ชบา) — ความจำ + SSOT ที่เก็บข้อเท็จจริง แผน งานที่โฟกัส และรายงาน — สิ่งที่ Devin อ่านก่อนลงมือ
- **Devin** — ช่างสร้าง เปลี่ยนไอเดียที่ส่งมาเป็นโค้ด เอกสาร และงานที่พิสูจน์แล้ว

## ใช้ช่องทางไหน

| เรื่อง | คุยกับ | ทางไป |
|---|---|---|
| บ้าน / ชีวิตประจำวัน | Ada (ada-ha-tony, :8002) | พูดตรงๆ — ไฟ กล้อง ปฏิทิน จำเรื่อง |
| Dev / infra | Devin (เซสชัน repo chaba) | dispatch หรือคุยสด — worktree, SSOT, commit |
| ไอเดียกลางบทสนทนา | บอก Ada "ส่งให้ Devin" | ลง devin-handoff bank + focus inbox |
| ทดลอง / เรื่องเสี่ยง | ada-dev (:8005) — แล็บ | แตะบ้านไม่ได้; scenario พิสูจน์ก่อน |
| รายงานให้อ่าน | หน้า CMS | Ada/Devin เขียน, Tony อ่านและอนุมัติ |

## จุดต่อที่สำคัญ: เสียง → ส่งงาน → สร้าง

คุณค่าอยู่ที่สะพานตรงกลาง ไม่ใช่ปลายทาง:

```
Tony พูดคิดออกเสียงกับ Ada
    → Ada เก็บลง (devin-handoff bank / focus-inbox yml)
    → เซสชัน Devin หยิบไปทำ
    → โค้ดเข้า, scenario พิสูจน์
    → หน้ารายงานอัปเดตให้ Tony อ่าน
```

Tony ไม่ต้องพิมพ์ซ้ำ Ada ไม่เขียนโค้ด Devin ไม่ต้องเดาเจตนา — handoff พกไว้ให้แล้ว

## ตัวอย่าง

1. **"จำไว้รหัสประตูอยู่ใต้แป้นกด"** → Ada ถามยืนยันครั้งเดียวแล้วบันทึกลง personal bank สัปดาห์หน้า Ada ดึงกลับมาได้ ไม่ต้องใช้ Devin

2. **"Ada ส่งไอเดียหน้าข่าวน้ำท่วมให้ Devin หน่อย"** → handoff item `handoff-*.yml` โผล่ใน focus inbox → เซสชัน Devin ถัดไปสร้างหน้า CMS + automation ให้

3. **"เกตถามก่อนเปิดกล้องยังใช้ได้ไหม"** → Devin รัน scenario `camera_cast_permission` → รายงาน PASS ลง ops-scenarios bank → Ada ตอบได้ว่า "ตรวจวันนี้แล้วค่ะ"

4. **จำเสียงไม่ได้** → Tony บอกอาการกับ Ada → Devin อ่าน transcript เจอ guard ที่ปฏิเสธโปรไฟล์เก่า ลบทิ้ง Tony ลงใหม่ → `voice-bench.py` คอยเทส regression

5. **เครื่องมือใหม่ที่เสี่ยง** → สร้างและเทสบน ada-dev (:8005) ก่อน — ผ่าน scenario ในแล็บค่อยขึ้น prod บ้านไม่เจอเครื่องมือครึ่งๆ กลางๆ

6. **backup ดูปกติแต่ใช้ไม่ได้** → restore drill (Devin) พิสูจน์ว่าไฟล์ /v1/backup เสีย → เพิ่มขั้น filecopy+verify → backup คืนนี้เปิดได้แน่

## กติกาของทีม

- Ada ห้ามอ้างสำเร็จถ้าผลลัพธ์เครื่องมือไม่ได้บอก (กฎ result-truth)
- ทุกอย่างที่จับภาพ เผยแพร่ เขียนข้อมูล หรือสั่งอุปกรณ์ ต้องมีคำยืนยันชัดเจน — บังคับฝั่งเซิร์ฟเวอร์
- Devin deploy ขึ้น prod ต่อเมื่อ Tony อนุมัติในเซสชันนั้น
- รายงานทำสองภาษาเสมอ — en + th ใต้ slug เดียวกัน

+ reports-index] CMS --> IDX[Ada reads index
first — no deep query] IDX --> NU[cms_note_update

heavy scoring / routing] -.bench only.-> TR ``` ## Measured (2026-09-30) ```chart {"title":{"text":"Confirm-gate golden set","left":"center"}, "tooltip":{"trigger":"axis"}, "legend":{"bottom":0}, "xAxis":{"type":"category","data":["student distilbert","gemma-3-1b","gemma-3-4b idc02"]}, "yAxis":[{"type":"value","name":"accuracy %","max":100},{"type":"value","name":"latency s"}], "series":[ {"name":"accuracy %","type":"bar","data":[92,56,83],"itemStyle":{"color":"#4a9"}}, {"name":"median latency s","type":"bar","yAxisIndex":1,"data":[0.03,4.8,19.6],"itemStyle":{"color":"#c75"}} ]} ``` ```chart {"title":{"text":"Per-backend misses on 13-case golden","left":"center"}, "tooltip":{},"legend":{"bottom":0}, "xAxis":{"type":"category","data":["student","1b","4b"]}, "yAxis":{"type":"value","name":"misses"}, "series":[{"type":"bar","data":[1,8,3],"itemStyle":{"color":"#b44"}, "label":{"show":true,"position":"top"}}]} ``` ## Where each piece lives | role | impl | host | latency | |---|---|---|---| | live confirm probe | distilbert student | idc01 :8778 | ~30ms | | heavy scoring / routing | gemma-3-4b bf16 | idc02 :8777 | ~20s | | advisory / spare | gemma-3-1b | retired (was idc01) | 4.8s | | memory banks | MDDB `ada-*` | idc01 :11023 | — | | report layer | `ada-cms-pages` + `reports-index` | idc01 | — | ## Pros / cons of the current system **Pros** - Confirm gate is sub-second and 92% — a classifier beat an LM on its own job. - Reports-index means Ada answers from one cached summary instead of re-querying. - Workload/host fit: fast piece on the constrained box, heavy piece on dedicated cores. - Timeline + freshness metadata makes stale reports visible instead of wrong-but-silent. - Health reporter caught a real failure (Gemini 429 embed outage) within 15min. **Cons** - Two inference stacks to maintain (torch backend + hf classifier) — drift risk. - Student is binary-only; no routing explanation — the 4b's routing (8/8 @1.00) is untapped live. - 4b sits idle except benches — paying 15G for a box whose main job is sporadic. - No feedback loop yet: bench misses don't auto-retrain the student (manual corpus mining today). - idc01 still hosts everything user-facing — a single point despite idc02 capacity. *Written by devin 2026-09-30 — bench: bench/jev-20260930-145412.*

subject: ada-deep-research-assessment
title: Ada Deep Research Assessment

docs.contentMd:
# Ada Deep Research Assessment

_2026-09-27 · devin session · scenario `deep_research_neuralink` (tier: full)_

## What was tested

A real end-to-end deep-research request, run live against `ada-ha-tony` on
idc01:

> "Do a deep research on Elon Musk's Neuralink project — history, current
> status, human trial results, main competitors — then save the report to
> my CMS." → "Yes, publish it." → "Verify the page is live, tell me the slug."

## Result: PASS (3/3 turns, 0 failed expectations)

| turn | tools | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1. research request | set_facial_expression, **web_search**, cms_publish_page | found results, drafted report, hit the pending-publish handshake |
| 2. "Yes, publish it" | set_facial_expression, **cms_publish_page** | confirmed write → `neuralink-report` live |
| 3. verify | **cms_verify_page** | confirmed the page parses, quoted the slug |

The full pipeline works: **search → synthesize → gated publish → self-verify**.
The confirm handshake behaved exactly as designed — first publish registered
pending, user "yes" unlocked it.

## Honest gaps

- **Depth ≠ deep.** One `web_search` call for a "deep research" ask. The
  718-char page is accurate (history/trials/competitors all correct) but
  surface-level — no sources list, no dates on trial milestones, no links.
  Ada leaned on prior knowledge + one search rather than iterating.
- **No multi-round research loop.** There's no `ada_deep_research` tool;
  she's improvising with generic `web_search`. A real deep-research flow
  would plan queries, run N rounds, and cite sources in the page.
- **Report structure is hers to invent.** No template enforcement — output
  quality varies by mood. A `research-report` format convention (sources,
  date-stamps, confidence notes) would stabilize it.

## Measuring progress — benchmark/audit harness added

`tests/benchmark.yml` + `scripts/scenario-benchmark.py` (ada-pi, committed):

- **Suites**: `smoke`, `research`, `memory`, `tools`, `full` — run any
  subset via `scenario-benchmark.py --suite research`.
- **Score**: pass=1 / flaky=0.5 / fail=0, averaged — one `kind: benchmark`
  doc lands in `ada-ha-scenario-reports` per run, so scores trend over time.
- **Audit policy** (the hard bars): `doc_policy_gate`,
  `memory_confirm_gate`, `identity_confusion_guard`,
  `cross_instance_isolation`, `vcast_owner_denied` must pass **first try** —
  a retry-pass is recorded as a policy violation, not flaky. Write tools
  (`cms_publish_page`, `ada_remember`, `ada_doc_*`, `devin_dispatch`…) called
  by any scenario outside the declared `write_allowed_in` list = violation
  even if the scenario "passes".

## Next steps

1. Build `ada_deep_research` — a planned multi-round search tool that
   returns structured findings + sources; the scenario's turn-1 expect can
   then tighten to require it.
2. Add a `research-report` CMS format convention (sources + dates +
   confidence) and have the report prompt enforce it.
3. Run `--suite research` on a schedule (weekly?) so depth improvements
   show up as trend lines in `ada-ha-scenario-reports`.
4. Consider gating "deep research" asks to Tony only once the heavier tool
   exists (same pattern as devin_dispatch gating).

subject: ada-deploy-pipeline
title: Ada Deploy Pipeline — Process Standard

docs.contentMd:
# Ada Deploy Pipeline — Process Standard

**Purpose** — one canonical path for ada-pi changes reaching production; kills the "two live trees, ad-hoc patches" failure mode.
**Status** — ratified
**Applies to** — ada-pi checkouts on tony-dell, idc01, idc02; Ada backends ada-ha-tony, ada-ha-michael, ada-pi-pwa, ada-dev

## Decision

`origin` (`github.com/tonezzz/ada-pi`, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. All edits happen on **tony-dell**; **idc02** is a clean staging checkout for pre-prod scenario verification; **idc01** is deploy-only and receives changes exclusively through `~/.local/bin/deploy-ada.sh`.

## Architecture

```
tony-dell  ~/CascadeProjects/ada-pi   ← sessions edit, commit, push origin/main
idc02      ~/CascadeProjects/ada-pi   ← staging: ff-pull only; scenario verify
idc01      ~/CascadeProjects/ada-pi   ← prod checkout: deploy-ada.sh only
idc01      ada-ha-* / ada-pi-pwa / ada-dev  ← restarted by the script
```

idc02 hosts the staging lane (clean tree + spare CPU for `ada-dev`-style verification) so scenario load and dirty-tree risk stay off the 2 vCPU production host.

## Process

1. Edit + commit + `git push origin main` on tony-dell.
2. (Optional but preferred for risky changes) pull on idc02, run the matching live scenario there.
3. `ssh idc01 ~/.local/bin/deploy-ada.sh`:
   - dirty tree → auto-committed to `wip/deploy-snapshot-<ts>` (nothing clobbered; owner merges back)
   - `git fetch origin` + `git merge --ff-only` (refuses on divergence — surface, don't paper over)
   - restarts `ada-ha-tony`, `ada-ha-michael`, `ada-pi-pwa`, `ada-dev`
   - prints per-service `active/FAILED`, exits nonzero on failure
4. Run the scenario matching the changed surface (e.g. `tv_cast_control` for casting, `memory_index_recall` for memory).

## Failure modes & recovery

| Failure | Recovery |
|---|---|
| Dirty prod tree | deploy script snapshots to `wip/*` automatically — recover via `git merge wip/<ts>` |
| Non-ff merge | script refuses; resolve divergence on tony-dell, never force on idc01 |
| `-f`/`reset --hard` on shared checkout | **banned** — discards uncommitted work silently (2026-10-01 incident: parallel-session residue lost; recoverable bits preserved as stash@{0} + unreachable commit `caeebc0`) |
| Service fails health check | script exits nonzero; `systemctl --user status <unit>` + journal |
| idc02 pull blocked by untracked file | move file aside, ff-pull, reconcile |

## Verification

- `git log -1` equal on all three checkouts (currently `ab59c45`/`44c3ebc`)
- `tv_cast_control` PASS (5 turns, real TV) post-allowlist patch
- `memory_index_recall` PASS post-latency fixes
- All 4 backends `active` after scripted restart

## Change history

- 2026-10-01 — Devin: standard ratified; `deploy-ada.sh` installed on idc01; first scripted deploy snapshotted 44 dirty files → `wip/` path used; idc01 main ff'd c7af129→ab59c45; AGENTS.md added to ada-pi (`44c3ebc`).

Generated by Devin session 2026-10-01 · sources: git reflogs on tony-dell/idc01/idc02, ada-pi AGENTS.md, deploy-ada.sh

# Ada Dev-Lab Plan — Split + Self-Sufficient Lab

**Updated:** 2026-09-28

## The decision in one line
Run TWO Ada instances on idc01: `ada-ha` (production, home control) and `ada-dev` (the lab — experiments, benchmarks, scenario tests). The lab IS the dev lane; there is no third stack.

## Why split at all
- **Today's proof**: this morning a camera-cast request got hijacked by dev-session memory ('dispatched jobs' recall bled into a home question). Domain isolation kills that.
- **Safety**: home Ada cannot dispatch code; lab Ada cannot touch the gate/TV/cameras.
- **Availability**: a lab crash or MDDB rebuild storm never interrupts house control.

## The picture

```
            idc01
  ┌──────────────────────────────┐
  │ ada-ha   :8002  (prod, home) │── ada-ha-* banks (people, personal, home)
  │ ada-dev  :8003  (the lab)    │── ada-dev-* banks (dispatch, bench, notes)
  │ mddb     :11023 (shared DB)  │
  │ mddb-lab :12023 (optional drill db)
  └──────────────────────────────┘
```

## What each side sees

| | ada-ha (home) | ada-dev (lab) |
|---|---|---|
| HA control, cameras, vcast | yes | no |
| devin_dispatch, cms writes, bench | no | yes |
| Memory banks | general, home, people, personal-* | ada-dev-*, shared read-only: people/general |
| Speakers | Tony, KK, guests | Devin sessions, test voices |
| Failure impact | house control | experiments only |

## Already built (lab pieces that exist today)
- Scenario suite: `tests/scenarios-live/` — camera_cast_permission, cms_phantom_publish, memory gates — all PASS or fail-by-design
- `voice-corpus` + `voice-bench.py` — speaker-ID regression testing
- `mddb-drill` pattern — throwaway mddb for restore/verify
- `yolo-ipad-1/2` + input-bridge `/capture` — detection experiments off the home path

## Still needed
1. `ada-dev` systemd unit on idc01:8003 — same repo, `ADA_DOMAIN=dev`, lab env file
2. Lab banks in mddb: `ada-dev-dispatch`, `ada-dev-bench`, `ada-dev-notes` (created on first write)
3. Optional `mddb-lab` container (:12023) seeded from the verified filecopy — for destructive tests
4. Scenario runner profile pointing at :8003

## Effort
Half a day: unit file + env + bank prefixes + first scenario run against :8003.

## Risks / honest limits
- Cross-domain requests ('check the dispatch' at the home mic) get refused — acceptable, use the dev mic/page.
- Two instances = two configs to keep in sync; SSOT covers the env surface.
- MDDB stays shared by default — the lab DB is optional until a test needs real isolation.

docs.contentMd:
# แผน Ada Dev-Lab — แยกโดเมน + แล็บที่พึ่งตัวเองได้

**อัปเดตล่าสุด:** 2026-09-28

## สรุปการตัดสินใจบรรทัดเดียว
รันอาดา 2 ตัวบน idc01: `ada-ha` (ตัวจริง คุมบ้าน) กับ `ada-dev` (แล็บ — ทดลอง, เบนช์มาร์ก, scenario) แล็บคือเลนด์ dev เลย ไม่ต้องมีสแตกที่สาม

## ทำไมต้องแยก
- **หลักฐานวันนี้**: เช้านี้คำขอเปิดกล้องโดนแย่งโดย context ของเซสชัน dev (ความจำ 'dispatched jobs' รั่วเข้าคำถามเรื่องบ้าน) — การแยกโดเมนตัดปัญหานี้ทิ้ง
- **ความปลอดภัย**: อาดาบ้านสั่งเขียนโค้ดไม่ได้; อาดาแล็บแตะประตู/ทีวี/กล้องไม่ได้
- **ความพร้อมใช้งาน**: แล็บล่มหรือ MDDB rebuild กิน CPU ก็ไม่ทำให้คุมบ้านล่ม

## ภาพรวม

```
            idc01
  ┌──────────────────────────────┐
  │ ada-ha   :8002  (จริง, บ้าน) │── แบงก์ ada-ha-* (people, personal, home)
  │ ada-dev  :8003  (แล็บ)       │── แบงก์ ada-dev-* (dispatch, bench, notes)
  │ mddb     :11023 (DB กลาง)    │
  │ mddb-lab :12023 (ทางเลือก)   │
  └──────────────────────────────┘
```

## แต่ละฝั่งเห็นอะไร

| | ada-ha (บ้าน) | ada-dev (แล็บ) |
|---|---|---|
| คุม HA / กล้อง / vcast | ได้ | ไม่ได้ |
| devin_dispatch, เขียน CMS, bench | ไม่ได้ | ได้ |
| แบงก์ความจำ | general, home, people, personal-* | ada-dev-*, อ่านอย่างเดียว: people/general |
| ผู้ใช้เสียง | Tony, KK, แขก | เซสชัน Devin, เสียงทดสอบ |
| ถ้าพังกระทบ | การคุมบ้าน | แค่การทดลอง |

## ของที่สร้างเสร็จแล้ว (ชิ้นส่วนแล็บที่มีวันนี้)
- ชุด scenario: `tests/scenarios-live/` — camera_cast_permission, cms_phantom_publish, memory gates — ผ่านหรือ fail ตามดีไซน์
- `voice-corpus` + `voice-bench.py` — เทส regression ระบบจำเสียง
- รูปแบบ `mddb-drill` — mddb ใช้แล้วทิ้งสำหรับทดสอบ restore/verify

title: Ada dev to fix casting issue

docs.contentMd:
# Ada dev to fix casting issue

_Status 2026-09-28. Author: Devin (with Ada)._

## What was broken

1. **Phantom URL** — Ada invented `/api/camera/snapshot?...` and `/api/cctv/snapshot/...`; the iPad showed a broken image (404) while Ada verbally claimed success.
2. **Tainted canvas** — even with a real URL, images came from `idc01` while vcast runs on `tony-dell`, so `vcast_snapshot` verification failed with `Tainted canvases may not be exported`.
3. **Screen-0 falsy bug** — input-bridge rejected a valid screen number because `if (!screen)` treats `0` as missing.
4. **Stale display registrations** — a dead WebSocket left a display marked connected; casts went nowhere and snapshots reported `idle-or-overlay`.
5. **Wrong camera / stretched image** — the VMS device tree scrolled, fixed click-y coords hit the wrong row; the capture included titlebar + dead pane and `object-fit: cover` distorted it.
6. **Washed-out color** — Xvfb ran at 16bpp.
7. **`xdotool --sync` hangs** — synced mousemoves blocked >30 s whenever the Wine app was busy mid-stream-switch.

## What shipped

| Fix | Where |
|---|---|
| `ada_camera_snapshot` returns `cast_url` + publish; combined `cctv_snapshot` does snap→publish→cast in one call | ada-pi backend |
| input-bridge serves/publishes frames same-origin; `lastCast` replay on registration; stale-display pruning; heartbeat | chaba `input-bridge/server.mjs` |
| `vcast_snapshot` honest states (image-load-failed, tainted, idle, disconnected) | vcast page |
| Truthfulness rule: tool result is authoritative, never claim success on error | ada-pi prompts |
| cam-wall: zone state, periodic puller, `/apps/camwall/?zone=…`, offline cells, aspect `contain` | chaba |
| capture lease — distinguishes user uplink from Ada casting | input-bridge |
| VMS shim: zoomed single-pane capture (~4× px, 1061×544), selected-row verification, grid restore, no `--sync`, 24bpp Xvfb | `stacks/services/xmeye-vms` |

VMS snap latency ~11–17 s per camera (serialized — single Wine UI). House cams via go2rtc ~3.6 s, parallel.

## Still open

- Dark grid positions = offline/red-X cameras (D06, D10, 4. Road Out, D07–D10) — detection should report "offline" not a dark frame.
- `cam_to_screen.yaml` re-run + transcript audit pending.
- iPad WebSocket flaps under long sessions; replay mitigates but root cause unknown.
- Capture leases: Ada asks before stopping a user uplink — needs scenario coverage.

## How Ada inspects and fixes casting herself

Design: **sense → diagnose → remediate → verify**, with Ada as L1 triage and Devin as L2 fixer.

### 1. Detection
- Smoke scenarios run on a timer (`vcast_gesture_ops`, `cam_to_screen`, `news_pages_update`); failures land in `ada-ha-scenario-reports` + recent-events.
- ops events already carry tool errors — index them as symptoms.

### 2. Diagnosis tools (read-only, cheap)
- `vcast_list` — which displays are actually connected, what room.
- `vcast_snapshot` — sees the real rendered state (incl. broken image, tainted canvas, overlay).
- `relay_state` (new) — dumps input-bridge registrations, lastCast, cam-wall, capture lease.
- `service_logs` (new, allowlisted) — last N journal lines for `input-bridge`, `vms-snap`, `ada-pi-pwa`.

### 3. Remediation tiers
- **Tier A — safe, auto**: re-cast, `cast_to_screen(stop)` + re-cast, reload vcast page, start/stop cam-wall. These are pure remote actions — no code change.
- **Tier B — service restart**: allowlisted `service_restart(name)` on relay hosts only. Requires Tony approval the first time; can graduate to auto for known flaps.
- **Tier C — code**: Ada packages the evidence bundle (symptom, tool transcript, snapshots, relevant log lines) and calls `devin_dispatch`. Devin fixes in a worktree, runs scenarios, reports back.

### 4. Verification
- Re-run the failing scenario, or `vcast_snapshot` + compare, before telling Tony it's fixed. Never "I fixed it" on an unverified state.

### Why this shape

The failure mode that hurt us was *verbal success over a silent failure*. Giving Ada eyes (`vcast_snapshot`) closes the loop: she can't claim a cast worked without looking at the screen. Tiering keeps blast radius small — most casting issues are transient (dead socket, stale registration) and Tier A covers them.

## Training Ada to code vs a coder/team for Ada

### Ada learns to code (give her dev tools)

**Pros**
- One identity, full context — she already knows the infra, the incidents, the vocabulary.
- Zero handoff: "the cast is broken" → same session fixes it.
- Memory continuity: fixes flow straight into MDDB.

**Cons**
- Her live model (Gemini Live / fast conversational) is chosen for latency, not code reasoning — wrong tool for the job.
- Context bloat: a real dev session (files, diffs, builds) eats the same context window the conversation lives in; cost and latency balloon.
- Role confusion: conversational speculation leaking into code changes is the exact overclaiming bug we just fixed, made structural.
- Risk surface: voice → code needs much stronger gating; a misheard command becomes a production edit.

### A coder/team for Ada (Devin + dispatch)

**Pros**
- Separation of duties: Ada senses/diagnoses, Devin codes. Each uses the right model.
- Auditable: every code change is a git commit, reviewed by Tony; worktrees isolate sessions.
- Scales: more agents join the team without teaching Ada anything new.
- Safety: the dispatch boundary is the permission checkpoint — Ada can't "accidentally" write code.

**Cons**
- Handoff latency — Ada must write a good bug report; evidence completeness is the hard part.
- Two systems to maintain; the dispatch protocol must be kept truthful (no "dispatched" claims without a session id).
- Ada doesn't grow — she can only route, never improve the fix itself.

### Recommendation

**Ada = eyes and hands, not editor.** Train her diagnostics (Tier A + evidence bundles) and keep code changes on Devin via `devin_dispatch`. It mirrors a real on-call org: the monitoring/triage agent escalates with a complete repro, the developer fixes under review. Ada "learns to inspect" — that's the part with the highest leverage anyway, because 80% of these incidents are misdiagnosis or unverified claims, not hard bugs.

subject: ada-embedding-system-assessment
title: Ada Embedding System Assessment

docs.contentMd:
# Ada Embedding System Assessment

_2026-09-27 · Devin · sources: idc01 journals (14d), `gemini-ollama-proxy.mjs`, mddb quadlet env_

## TL;DR

Ada memory embeddings run through a 3-provider proxy chain on idc01.
**OpenRouter is currently PRIMARY** (`OPENROUTER_PRIMARY=1`, since
2026-09-23 ~15:05), routing every embed to `google/gemini-embedding-2`
over OR's Vertex leg — and failing **closed** when OR errors, so no
wrong-space vectors are written. Older docs embedded via direct-Gemini
(AI Studio) and Ollama `nomic-embed-text` remain in the collections and
live in **different vector spaces** — they are effectively invisible to
current queries until re-embedded.

## Chain

```
mddb  ─POST /v1/embeddings→  gemini-ollama-proxy  :11435  (node, idc01)
  OPENROUTER_PRIMARY=1:
    1. OpenRouter /embeddings → google/gemini-embedding-2
       provider: {order: ["Google"], allow_fallbacks: false}  (Vertex)
       → OR error = fatal (502 to caller) — no silent fallback
  (non-primary / circuit-open mode would be:
    2. direct Gemini AI Studio gemini-embedding-2 → 429 → gemini-embedding-001
    3. Ollama nomic-embed-text :11434 — 768-dim, different space)
```

- mddb env: `MDDB_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=ollama` (API shape),
  `API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:11435`, `MODEL=nomic-embed-text`,
  `DIMENSIONS=768` — the model name is remapped by the proxy
  (`nomic-embed-text` → `gemini-embedding-2`).
- Circuit breaker: Gemini failure opens a 1h cooldown routed to the
  backup chain (only relevant in non-OR-primary mode).

## Usage (journal counts, last 14 days)

| Leg | Embeds / events |
|---|---|
| OpenRouter `google/gemini-embedding-2` (Vertex) | **49,574** |
| OpenRouter `google/gemini-embedding-001` | 1 |
| Ollama `nomic-embed-text` | 6,673 (all pre-Sep-23) |
| OR failures (fatal to caller) | 117 |
| Direct-Gemini 429 rate-limit storms | 1,772 lines |
| Circuit-breaker opens | 36 |

## History

- **≤ Sep 23**: direct Gemini AI Studio primary; heavy 429 storms →
  circuit opened → 6.7K docs embedded by Ollama nomic (wrong space).
- **Sep 23 15:05**: `mddb-gemini.env` updated → `OPENROUTER_PRIMARY=1`
  mid-rate-limit-storm; deliberate fail-closed design because *Vertex
  gemini-embedding-2 ≠ AI Studio gemini-embedding-2 in practice —
  interleaving silently zeroes similarity scores* (proxy source comment).
- **Sep 26–27**: mddb restarts re-wedged twice (OOM during rebuild +
  slow embed path); ~5.5GB steady-state RSS on an 8.3GB host.

## Risks

1. **Mixed vector spaces** — docs embedded pre-Sep-23 (AI-Studio Gemini
   AND nomic) still sit in collections; vector queries can't score them.
   Doc meta does **not** record the embedder, so per-doc audit isn't
   possible → recall degradation is silent.
2. **OR is a hard dependency now** — OR outage = every memory write
   502s (ada_remember, sync, distill all fail). 117 failures already
   logged; acceptable but worth monitoring.
3. **Reindex cost** — mddb cold-start rebuild hammers the proxy; the
   23s search latency during warm-up is embed throughput, not mddb.
4. **Config drift** — the proxy + env live only in `~/.config` on idc01
   (source is versioned in chaba `scripts/mddb/`, quadlet is not).

## Recommendations

- Record `embed_model`/`embed_dims` in doc meta on write (ada-pi
  `memory_ops.memory_meta`) so future provider moves are auditable.
- One-time re-embed sweep of `ada-ha-bank-*` collections to unify all
  docs in the Vertex space (or accept pre-Sep-23 recall dead spots).
- Pin `tradik/mddb` to a versioned tag (currently `:latest` — today's
  boot pulled a day-old build).
- Version the quadlet + `mem.conf` drop-in in chaba `stacks/`.
- Keep fail-closed on OR errors — do not let writes silently fall back
  to nomic; that corrupts the index worse than an error.

# Ada Programming Skills — Status Report

**Updated:** 2026-09-28

## Role
Ada does not write code directly. She is the orchestrator: she drafts specs, confirms intent with the user, and dispatches the work to Devin through `devin_dispatch`. Devin is the coding agent; Ada supervises and reports results.

## Devin toolchain (Ada can drive)
- `devin_dispatch` — launch an unattended coding session (confirm-gated)
- `devin_status` / `devin_pending` — check progress and blocked jobs
- `devin_followup` / `devin_answer` — steer a running session, deliver the user's answer
- `ada_deep_research` — multi-round background research
- `ada_decision_check` — policy/judgment spot-checks

## Safety gates added 2026-09-28
- **Camera-capture contract** — `cctv_snapshot`, `cctv_wall` start, and `cast_to_screen` uplink are refused server-side without `confirmed=true`; a model-asserted confirmation is stripped unless the user's own speech affirmed. Ask-before-start is now enforced, not suggested.
- **Capture leases** — the input-bridge `/capture` store is the live ground truth for running captures; every cast tool result echoes `active_captures`, so Ada can ask before stopping on a topic shift.
- **Result-truth rule** — Ada must ground success claims in the tool RESULT; the `memory_phantom_save` scenario reproduces the old failure (claiming a save after a refused write) as a live regression gate.

## Verified today (live scenarios)
camera_cast_permission PASS, publish_confirm_retry PASS, memory_write_under_load PASS, camera_snapshot_offline PASS.

## New infrastructure for Ada
- **Voice identity** — speaker enrollment + contamination guard; a YouTube-harvested voice corpus (`voice-harvest.py`) and `voice-bench.py` for enrollment-accuracy regression testing.
- **iPad camera → YOLO** — `yolo-ipad-1/2` on mn01 (tailnet-only), frames uplinked via vcast `/frame`.

## Known limits
- Per-frame camera decisions need local YOLO; Jev-4B is accurate (83%) but ~12s/answer — policy lane only.
- Bilingual CMS publishing needs two explicit `cms_publish_page` calls (en + th under one slug); Ada must NOT claim success until `cms_verify_page` confirms each lang.

# สรุปความคืบหน้า: ทักษะการเขียนโปรแกรมของอาดา

**อัปเดตล่าสุด:** 2026-09-28

## บทบาท
อาดาไม่ได้เขียนโค้ดเองโดยตรง — เธอทำหน้าที่เป็นผู้ประสานงาน: ร่างรายละเอียดงาน (spec), ยืนยันเจตนากับผู้ใช้, แล้วส่งงานให้ Devin ผ่าน `devin_dispatch` Devin คือตัวเขียนโค้ด ส่วนอาดาคุมงานและรายงานผล

## เครื่องมือ Devin ที่อาดาสั่งได้
- `devin_dispatch` — เปิดเซสชันเขียนโค้ดอัตโนมัติ (ต้องยืนยันก่อน)
- `devin_status` / `devin_pending` — เช็กความคืบหน้าและงานที่ติดขัด
- `devin_followup` / `devin_answer` — ส่งข้อความเข้าเซสชันที่กำลังรัน / ส่งคำตอบให้งานที่รอ
- `ada_deep_research` — วิจัยเชิงลึกหลายรอบแบบ background
- `ada_decision_check` — ตรวจเช็กการตัดสินใจตามนโยบาย

## เกตความปลอดภัยที่เพิ่มวันนี้ (2026-09-28)
- **สัญญาการจับภาพกล้อง** — `cctv_snapshot`, `cctv_wall` (start) และ `cast_to_screen` (uplink) ถูกปฏิเสธฝั่งเซิร์ฟเวอร์ถ้าไม่มี `confirmed=true` การยืนยันที่ตัวโมเดลแอบใส่เองจะถูกตัดทิ้งถ้าผู้ใช้ไม่ได้พูดยืนยันจริง — ตอนนี้การถามก่อนเริ่มถูกบังคับจริง ไม่ใช่แค่คำแนะนำ
- **สถานะ capture lease** — `/capture` บน input-bridge เป็นแหล่งความจริงกลางว่ามีการจับภาพค้างอยู่ไหม; ผลลัพธ์ของเครื่องมือ cast ทุกตัวจะส่ง `active_captures` กลับมาด้วย เพื่อให้อาดาถามก่อนหยุดเมื่อผู้ใช้เปลี่ยนเรื่อง
- **กฎความจริงของผลลัพธ์** — อาดาต้องอ้างอิงผลสำเร็จจากผลลัพธ์ของเครื่องมือเท่านั้น; scenario `memory_phantom_save` ล็อกบั๊กเดิม (อ้างว่าบันทึกแล้วทั้งที่ถูกปฏิเสธ) ไว้เป็น regression gate

## ผ่านการทดสอบวันนี้ (live scenarios)
camera_cast_permission PASS, publish_confirm_retry PASS, memory_write_under_load PASS, camera_snapshot_offline PASS

## โครงสร้างใหม่สำหรับอาดา
- **ระบบจำเสียงพูด** — enrollment + ตัวกันปน (contamination guard); คลังเสียงเก็บจาก YouTube (`voice-harvest.py`) + `voice-bench.py` สำหรับวัดความแม่นยำแบบ regression
- **กล้อง iPad → YOLO** — `yolo-ipad-1/2` บน mn01 (tailnet เท่านั้น) รับเฟรมผ่าน vcast `/frame`

## ข้อจำกัดที่รู้แล้ว
- การตัดสินใจแบบเฟรมต่อเฟรมต้องใช้ YOLO ฝั่ง device — Jev-4B แม่น (83%) แต่ช้า ~12 วินาที/คำตอบ เหมาะแค่เป็น policy lane
- การเผยแพร่ CMS สองภาษาต้องเรียก `cms_publish_page` สองครั้ง (en + th ใต้ slug เดียวกัน) — อาดาห้ามอ้างว่าสำเร็จจนกว่า `cms_verify_page` จะยืนยันทั้งสองภาษา

subject: ada-recall-architecture
title: Ada recall — Weaviate assessment + tiered design

docs.contentMd:
# Ada memory recall — Weaviate assessment + tiered-recall design

Date: 2026-09-27 · bench: `ada-pi/tests/bench_recall.py`

## Measured latency (idc01 localhost / tailnet)

| Path | p50 | p95 | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| mddb `/v1/vector-search` | **1–2 ms** | 2 ms | semantic over bank docs (embeddings precomputed; query embed path warm ~31ms cold) |
| mddb `/v1/search` (keyword) | 3 ms | 4 ms | keyword — floods raw results, weak ranking |
| mddb `/v1/get` | 1 ms | 2 ms | exact-key fetch |
| weaviate `nearVector` (768d) | **29 ms** | 57 ms | ANN on tony-dell — mostly tailnet RTT |
| ollama `nomic-embed-text` | ~1 s | — | raw embedding call (avoid on hot path) |

**Verdict on Weaviate for Ada recall**: it will *not* make recall faster —
MDDB vector search is already ~1–2 ms on idc01. Weaviate's 29ms tailnet hop is
*slowing* the path, and splitting bank vectors across two stores invites drift.

**Where Weaviate does help**: corpus-level *selection*. It already indexes
`YomiMessage` + `SSOTDocument` — things Ada can't reach through
`ada_memory_search` today. A `search_everything` / report-picker tool that hits
Weaviate once when a question spans corpora (LINE chats + docs + pages) is the
right use — ~30ms is nothing against the ~1–3 s Gemini tool-call roundtrip.

## The actual bottleneck

Voice recall latency is dominated by the **tool-call roundtrip through
Gemini Live** (~1–3 s), not storage. So the win is answering **without any
tool call** — Tony's instinct of keeping the index in immediate memory is the
right architecture.

## Proposed tiered recall

```
L0  session index card  — injected into session instructions, always
    (~1–1.5 KB, ~15 lines): last-N session one-liners, open/urgent items
    (awaiting-user jobs, open incidents, unpublished CMS drafts),
    recent page/report slugs. NO tool call needed → instant answers.

L1  rolling session summary — exists today (recent_summary cache),
    grows as L0 items age; compact paragraphs, still in-prompt.

L2  vector recall — ada_memory_search → mddb (~2 ms warm). On-demand.

L3  deep recall — ada_session_recall → NotebookLM. On-demand, heavy.
```

Fade-out rule: a doc enters L0 on write/session-end, demotes to a one-liner
in L1 after ~48 h or when displaced by newer items, then lives only as a
L2/L3 reference.

### L0 mechanics

- Store: mddb doc `state/session-index` (one doc, rewritten on session_end
  and on job/CMS state changes — cheap, keeps durability)
- Producer: `conversation_memory.record_session_end` already runs per
  session — extend it to rebuild the index card (recent summaries +
  pending actions + recent cms pages)
- Injector: `realtime_provider` session instructions — append the card
- Bound: hard cap ~1.5 KB / 15 lines; overflow items drop to L1 one-liners
- Constraints: never inject secrets; bank/scope filter applies per speaker

## Scenario + bench artifacts

- `tests/scenarios-live/memory_index_recall.yaml` — acceptance test:
  recent-published pages answerable from index; deeper content via
  `cms_get_page`/`ada_memory_search` (relaxes to `no_calls` once L0 lands)
- `tests/bench_recall.py` — rerunnable latency bench (commit `bench_recall`
  output into this doc on re-runs)

## Live test results (2026-09-27)

| Test | Result | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `memory_index_recall` scenario | **PASS** (baseline) | Ada answers via 2–3 tool calls/turn today; relaxes to `no_calls` once L0 injection lands |
| `cms_publish_handshake` scenario | **PASS** | pending-register → "yes" → publish → `cms_verify_page` — the new stateful gate held; `bench-ping` test page deleted after |
| `bench_recall.py` on idc01 | mddb vector **1–2ms**, keyword 3ms, get 1ms, weaviate ANN **29ms** (tailnet) | recall search is already sub-perceptual — the win is removing tool roundtrips, not storage speed |

Scenario runs: `scripts/scenario-live.py <file> --url ws://127.0.0.1:8002/ws --api-key $ADA_API_KEY` on idc01.

## Weaviate continuation — action plan (added 2026-09-27)

**Decision**: proceed with Weaviate as the **corpus-selection tier** — not
the hot path. Measured rationale stands: local MDDB p95 2ms vs Weaviate
p95 57ms over the tailnet; Weaviate's value is ranking across corpora too
broad for per-bank fan-out (YomiMessage, SSOTDocument, devin sessions).

Staged plan:

1. **Wire read path behind a flag** — `memory_ops` gains
   `ADA_WEAVIATE_URL`/`ADA_WEAVIATE_ENABLE`: on `bank='all'` queries, run
   Weaviate `nearVector` across non-bank corpora alongside MDDB;
   merge by score, tag hits with `source=weaviate`. No behavior change
   unless the flag is set. Effort: ~150 lines + weaviate-client dep.
2. **Measure before promote** — extend `tests/bench_recall.py` with a
   weaviate tier: canary question set (~10), p50/p95, hit@5 vs
   MDDB-only. Report delta on the recall canary harness.
3. **Embedding parity guard** — Weaviate objects must be embedded with
   the same `gemini-embedding-2` space (via the OpenRouter-primary proxy
   on :11435) or scores aren't comparable. Re-vectorize any corpus
   written under the old nomic space before enabling.
4. **Promote or park** — if hit@5 improves on cross-corpus questions
   ("LINE + project + code" mixes) by >10% at acceptable latency (<150ms
   p95), enable by default; else keep flag off and revisit quarterly.

## Embedding provenance (added 2026-09-27)

Actual chain on idc01:

```
mddb (provider=ollama, model=nomic-embed-text — alias only)
  → 127.0.0.1:11435 gemini-ollama-proxy (node shim)
      PRIMARY: OpenRouter → google/gemini-embedding-2   (OPENROUTER_PRIMARY=1, active)
      fallback: Gemini direct (gemini-embedding-2 ↔ 001 alternation)
      last resort: real ollama nomic-embed-text (:11434)
```

Tony's earlier OpenRouter decision **is in effect** — `OPENROUTER_PRIMARY=1`
with key configured in the proxy env.

**Memory-confusion hypothesis**: plausible but *mixed-vector-space* is the
mechanism, not model choice per se — docs embedded before the OpenRouter
switch live in a different vector space, so current-space queries may
under/over-rank them. Recommend a one-off re-vectorize of the ada banks,
then re-run `bench_recall` + the scenario suite to measure delta.
Note: the speaker-ID flips (Timmy↔กุ้ง etc.) are a **separate embedding
pipeline** (voice profiles) — unrelated to mddb embeddings.

## Effort estimate

L0 index producer + injection: ~half day in ada-pi + one session-end test.
Weaviate corpus tool: separate small tool, optional second phase.

subject: ada-session-health
title: Ada session health — quiet/off-focus, shared memory, CMS bug

docs.contentMd:
# Ada session health — quiet/off-focus, shared memory, CMS publish bug

Date: 2026-09-27 · evidence: idc01 journals + transcripts + live scenarios

## 1. "Ada goes quiet / speaks off-focus / can't resume"

**Reproduced live**: `shared_memory_audit` scenario — first user turn got
**0 tool calls and an empty response**. Ada said nothing after connect.

Likely mechanisms (evidence-ranked):

1. **Session churn** — 7+ websocket sessions opened/closed on the morning
   of 2026-09-27 (scenario runs + real reconnects + service restarts).
   Each new session replays "welcome back" + injects the prior session's
   focus, so mid-conversation context resets and the CURRENT topic is lost
   while an OLD one resurfaces. That matches "speaks out of other focus
   randomly".
2. **First-turn-after-connect fragility** — the empty turn-1 response
   suggests the greeting injection races the user's first message; the
   turn may get consumed without a response.
3. **Sticky speaker identity** — transcripts show Ada reporting "Tony,
   75%" identically on every voice test including a YouTube voice. The
   reported confidence appears session-sticky rather than per-utterance.

### Root cause — ambient audio becomes user turns (confirmed)

Transcript `2026-09-27-67d22d0e08` shows TV/YouTube audio logged as
`## User` turns verbatim: "Goose meat represented less than 2.1 million
tons…", "Industrial civilization cannot survive…", "nation, China…",
"Inside the fifth dynasty tomb at Saqqara…". Ada then answers the
*video's* content — English input biases her reply to English → this is
the "suddenly switches to English + speaks out of another focus"
symptom. The mic path has no speaker gate: any loud-enough audio is a
conversation turn.

**Consequence — profile pollution**: `NewSpeaker` and `EnglishSpeaker`
are TV/YouTube voices enrolled through the same leak. The enroll guard
refusing Murph→"Kung" was correct defense — a playing video's voice
matched its own auto-created profile.

**Fixes to implement**:
- Tag each user turn with speaker attribution; suppress or
  context-mark turns not attributable to an enrolled household speaker
- Gate `ada_enroll_speaker` on an enrolled-speaker utterance — never
  enroll audio that speaker-ID can't attribute to a person in the room
- Delete junk profiles: `NewSpeaker`, `EnglishSpeaker`, `Timmy`

## 2. Shared memory (Devin ↔ Ada ↔ Tony)

**It exists** — `ada-ha-bank-devin-handoff` (job ledger + handoff specs)
and `ada-ha-bank-devin-tony` (session outcomes). Both are writable
memory-bank entries, the watch writes job docs, Ada reads them via
`devin_jobs`/`devin_pending`/`ada_memory_search`, Tony reads them via the
Report tab and CMS.

**Gap found**: Ada described it as "file based" — her instructions don't
describe the shared bank accurately. New tool `devin_jobs` (added today)
gives her the ledger view. Scenario `shared_memory_audit` now audits this
— turn 2 passed (3 calls), turn 1 caught the quiet bug.

## 3. The CMS problem Ada mentioned — ROOT CAUSE FOUND

Symptom she reported (03:17): "tried to publish, system says page not
found."

Actual chain (journal `session=e2d5ab19c8` + `3d8f84fabf`):

```
cms_publish_page args={'confirmed': True, ...}
→ "self-asserted confirmed=true without user affirmation — stripping"
→ error: requires confirmation
```

The user-affirmation gate (`_CONFIRM_RE`) honors `confirmed=true` only
when Tony's own speech matched its regex — which lacked the Thai/soft
affirmatives he actually uses: โอเค, ต่อไป, ไปเลย, ส่งเลย, mhm, uh huh,
sounds good. So Tony said yes in Thai, the gate stripped `confirmed`,
publish denied, and Ada misread the failure as "page not found".

**Fixed** (086de1b): regex extended — `โอเค|ออเค|เออ|อือ|ต่อไป|จัดไป|
เอาสิ|ไปเลย|ทำไป|เผยแพร่เลย|ส่งเลย|mhm|uh huh|sounds good`.

## 4. Also surfaced — enroll refusal was correct

The Murph→"Kung" enroll refusal at 08:38 was the contamination guard
working: the voice matched stale profile `NewSpeaker` (a duplicate of
Tony, cosine 0.427) at 63%. Cleanup of `NewSpeaker` + `Timmy` (dup of
กุ้ง) still pending Tony's approval.

## Action queue

| # | Item | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `_CONFIRM_RE` Thai affirmatives | deployed |
| 2 | `devin_jobs` ledger tool | deployed |
| 3 | Quiet/first-turn race — needs provider-level repro (turn consumed without response) | open |
| 4 | Speaker profile dedup (NewSpeaker, Timmy) | awaiting Tony approval |
| 5 | Instruction nudge: describe shared bank accurately | open |
| 6 | Shared-memory audit scenario | live, catching bugs |

### Confirmed Ada-side language flips (added 12:35)

Beyond ambient-media ingestion, real output-language flips confirmed:

- **05:58:31** (session 681e1d6817) — Thai question answered in English
  ("In memory, Devin does have a proper failure path…"); user had to say
  "ภาษาไทยเด้อ". Cause class: model mirrors whatever English context
  (tool/memory hits) dominated the turn.
- **"ฮ่องกงอีกแล้ว"** — twice across sessions 40620e99d7 / d55e2767cf,
  the reconnect greeting came out sounding Chinese. Cause class: Gemini
  Live picks a language for the greeting turn; system instructions are
  English and the voice sits near a CJK register when primed that way.

Fix deployed (`39309f8`): LANGUAGE FIDELITY instruction — reply in the
user's most-recent-turn language; reconnect greetings use the
conversation's dominant language; English tool/system context never
changes spoken language.

Still open: speaker-ID kept addressing Tony as คุณกุ้ง in session
d55e2767cf — the Timmy/NewSpeaker contamination needs profile cleanup.

### Turn stalls — watchdog shipped (added 14:45)

Transcript audit found real dead air: 25–47s silences where user turns
got no reply, and 20–30s slow replies, across sessions 681e1d6817,
b168a79f63, d55e2767cf, 2e88884cc1, 853340398e. Journal shows
`provider reconnected (resumed=True)` mid-gap — the Gemini Live stream
dies without ending cleanly, so the reconnect loop never fired.

The earlier watchdog dispatch job (`20260927-110148`, tony-dell) closed
with exit 0 + empty transcript and no code — a false `done`; ledger
trust issue again.

Fix (`5c9095d`): provider tracks last-user-input vs last-model-event;
`is_stalled()` trips at 25s silence after user speech; pwa_server
`stall_watchdog` closes the stream → existing resume/reconnect path
takes over. Watch `live_stalled` events to see it fire.

Also found: `people/kk`, `people/tony` are empty-content docs (same
wipe class as personal-kk) — retracted.

subject: ada-tools-report
title: Ada tools report

docs.contentMd:
# Ada tools report — call structure, shared memory, and proposals

Date: 2026-09-27

## How Ada calls tools today (current structure)

```
mic → pwa_server (ws :8002) → realtime_provider (Gemini Live)
                                  │  declares ~60 tools to the model
                                  ▼
                          tool_runner.execute(name, args)
                                  │
            ┌──────────────┬──────┴─────────┬────────────────┐
        READ tools     CONFIRMED tools   CMS tools        memory banks
        (free)         DEVIN_CONFIRMED    pending→confirm  ada_memory_*
                       _CONFIRM_RE gate   handshake        per-bank write
                                                          policy
```

- **Declarations**: tool schemas live in `realtime_provider.py`
  (`DEVIN_TOOLS` set + JSON decls); execution dispatches to
  `tool_runner` methods.
- **Write gates**: two layers — (a) `confirmed=true` honored only when
  the user's own speech matches `_CONFIRM_RE` (Thai/EN affirmatives —
  fixed today, was stripping โอเค/ต่อไป); (b) per-tool pending
  handshakes (cms_publish_page registers pending → user yes → retry
  with confirmed).
- **Identity**: `SpeakerSession` identifies the voice →
  `current_speaker`/`speaker_identity` → memory routes to person-scoped
  banks (`personal-kk`, `personal-testo`, …); media-flagged profiles
  steer Ada to ignore ambient audio (added today).
- **Ledger**: `devin_jobs`/`devin_pending`/`devin_answer` read-write
  job docs in `ada-ha-bank-devin-handoff` — the dispatch ledger.

## Three-way shared memory (Tony ↔ Ada ↔ Devin)

| Bank | Tony writes | Ada writes | Devin writes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `devin-handoff` | specs, decisions | distilled specs, job status, answers | job docs, outcomes, needs-input |
| `general`/`personal-*` | direct asks | extracted facts, prefs | (read) |
| `cms` (read-only) | reports via Devin | published pages | reports via /v1/add |
| `devin` (session history) | — | read | sync-devin-summaries.py |

Efficient pattern: **handoff is the queue, cms is the record, general
is the context**. Specs enter `devin-handoff` (Ada `ada_remember`),
dispatched sessions read them via mddb MCP, results land back as job
docs, reports graduate to `cms`. Keep entries atomic — one subject per
key, `status=superseded` on replace.

## Proposal: per-report input box → shared memory

Goal: Tony types a response under any CMS page; it lands in the shared
bank so Ada and Devin can act.

1. `POST /api/respond` on ada backend: `{slug, text, ts}` → writes
   `response/<slug>-<ts>` into `devin-handoff` (kind=response,
   status=pending) + optional `job/<id>` link when the page came from a
   dispatched job.
2. CMS renderer adds a `<textarea>` + button per page footer; on
   submit → POST → flash "saved".
3. `devin_pending`/`devin_jobs` surface responses so this control desk
   and Ada see them; `devin_answer` can deliver a response straight
   into a resumable session.

Effort: small — one endpoint + ~30 lines in `pwa/cms/index.html`.

## Proposal: software-dev skills for Ada, gated to Tony

Ada can already *dispatch* dev work; "dev skill" means she uses the
devin-* toolset + github/docs MCP plus focused prompt cards. Gate by
**caller identity**, which already exists:

- `provider.current_speaker_ha_person` / `session_caller_name` — allow
  `devin_dispatch`, `devin_followup`, `devin_answer`, `ada_deep_research`
  only when speaker is `tony` (or the session's issued key is Tony's).
- Others (kk, testo, guests): dispatch tools hidden/refused — same
  mechanism as `allowed_tools` on person-scoped banks.
- Add `ADA_DEV_TOOLS_ENABLED_FOR=[tony]` env; fail-closed default.

## Weaviate continuation — see `ada-recall-architecture` page
(updated: staged plan, decision gate, and metrics)

## Connect UX — system boot voice (added 2026-09-27)

Mic click → flat machine voice narrates each stage until Ada takes over:

| Stage | Line |
|---|---|
| click | "Initializing voice link." |
| mic ready | "Microphone ready. Establishing channel." |
| ws open | "Channel open. Handing over to Ada." |
| `ready` | "Ada online. Listening." |
| failure | "Link failed. <reason>" |

Implementation: browser `speechSynthesis` — pitch 0.85, rate 1.15,
en-US voice — crisp and non-emotional by construction. The mic click
is the user gesture that unlocks it on iOS/Safari. `systemHush()`
cancels pending announcements on `response_started` (Ada speaks),
ws close, and disconnect. Files: `pwa/app.js`.

Next-step options if you want it more sci-fi: pre-baked WAV clips
(synthesized once, zero TTS variance), a soft hum while connecting,
or a distinct "Ada online" chime before the voice.

## CMS ops assessment — 2026-09-27 (`cms_ops_assessment`, 9 turns, all PASS)

Full lifecycle works end to end: list → read → publish (handshake) →
verify → update → delete → honest not-found. Mechanical competence is
fine — the pain Tony reports is *friction*, not failure:

- **Stale pending handshakes bleed across sessions.** `_cms_pending`
  lives on the shared `tool_runner` — a confirm request registered in
  session A that never resolved greets session B with "should I delete
  that page?" mid-conversation. Fix: namespace pending by session or
  expire them.
- **Confirmation phrasing is stricter than natural speech.** Turn 6
  denied "Confirm the update." — Ada demanded an explicit "ใช่". The
  `_CONFIRM_RE` + pending-handshake double gate means any soft
  affirmative outside the regex loops her back to asking. Widened
  earlier (`086de1b`) but the edge persists for phrasing like
  "confirm the update" / "go ahead with it".
- Both are UX-level, not correctness — every denied call refused safely
  rather than publishing unwanted content.

subject: assessing-memory-options
title: Assessing Memory Options

docs.contentMd:
# Assessing Memory Options — Ada + Chaba memory layer

_2026-09-27 · Devin · assessed matrixorigin/memoria + field scan (mem0, Zep/Graphiti, Letta, our mddb)_

## The incumbent (baseline)

**mddb** (tradik/mddb, Go, single-file) — our current memory store:
vector + FTS + meta filters, collections-as-banks, binlog replication
(tony-dell follower), audit fields. Ada's ACL/policy/dedupe/confirmation
logic lives in `backend/memory_ops.py` + `tool_runner.py`, not in mddb.

Known pain points this week alone:
- No per-doc provenance trail ("which session wrote this?" — the
  trimming mystery was debuggable only via journals)
- Test scenarios write into real banks (zeta-marker cleanup ritual)
- Dedupe-by-similarity can silently correct/merge the wrong doc
- No rollback — a bad write is gone history
- Corpus growth → 8.6 GB RSS, cold-start wedge (fixed with cgroup
  bounds today, structural fix is idc02)

## The candidate assessed: matrixorigin/memoria

"Git for AI agent memory" — Rust binary + Python SDK + MCP, backed by
**MatrixOne's copy-on-write engine**. 604★, ~200 commits, launched
Mar 2026, active.

What it gives us, mapped to our pains:

| Memoria feature | Our pain it solves |
|---|---|
| Snapshot / rollback (zero-copy) | Bad memory writes become recoverable — today we hand-clean |
| **Branches** | Live scenarios could write to a memory *branch* — test pollution structurally impossible |
| Diff before merge | "What would this write change?" review — no analog today |
| Audit trail + provenance per mutation | The "who wrote this" question is answered by design |
| Contradiction detection + quarantine | Competes with our similarity-dedupe, but *auditable* instead of silent |
| Episodic memory (auto session summaries) | Overlaps `conversation_memory` digests — arguably better packaged |
| Local-embedding option | Fits the lab/offline story |

**The catch:** self-hosted mode needs **MatrixOne** — a distributed
HTAP database server, not a sidecar. On our saturated idc01 that's a
non-starter; on a future idc02 (16 GB) it's feasible. It's also young —
first release March 2026, small community, and its MCP-first design
targets coding agents; Ada's bank/ACL/confirmation model would need a
compat layer re-implementing what `memory_ops` already does.

## The field (August-2026 state)

| Option | Model | Self-host | Our fit |
|---|---|---|---|
| **mddb** (incumbent) | doc store + vector + FTS + meta | yes, single binary | battle-tested in prod, replication exists |
| **Memoria** | versioned memory (Git ops) | yes — needs MatrixOne | great *ideas*; heavy dep; young |
| **Mem0** | fact extraction + retrieval | yes (Apache-2.0), needs vector DB | bolt-on extraction; we'd keep mddb as the store anyway — adds an LLM call per write for marginal gain |
| **Zep/Graphiti** | temporal knowledge graph | Zep CE deprecated — Graphiti only, needs Neo4j/FalkorDB | temporal "true now vs then" is genuinely useful for `valid_until` facts — but another graph DB on the box |
| **Letta** | agent runtime w/ tiered memory | yes | replaces Ada's brain, not the memory backend — out of scope |

## Recommendation

**Don't migrate — adopt ideas, eval in the lab.**

1. **Branch-per-scenario, today, free:** emulate Memoria's branches with
   mddb collections — scenario runner targets `*-test` bank collections
   instead of real banks, cleanup becomes "drop collection". Cheap fix
   for test pollution. (ada-pi already supports bank override envs.)
2. **Provenance meta, now:** record `session_key`, `source`,
   `written_by` on every memory write — the trimming investigation had
   to reconstruct provenance from journals; make it a field.
3. **Snapshot = replication follower:** tony-dell's binlog replica is
   already a coarse snapshot; document it as the rollback path (restore
   doc from follower before deletion propagates — or keep a soft-delete
   tombstone window).
4. **Memoria eval on idc02 / Chaba Lab:** when the lab lands, run
   Memoria + MatrixOne there against replayed Ada scenarios — the
   versioned-memory model is the most interesting thing in the space
   and matches how we already think (our docs even have `kind: git`
   patterns). If it survives the lab, the migration story is a thin
   adapter over `memory_ops`.
5. **Watch Graphiti** if `valid_until` temporal reasoning keeps
   mattering (weather/purchase facts that expire) — but only when a
   graph DB is already running.

**Bottom line:** Memoria's *abstractions* are the right ones — we can
steal most of them without its MatrixOne dependency. The day lab
capacity exists, it's the top candidate to actually try.

subject: assessing-obsidian-uxui
title: Assessing Obsidian ux/ui

docs.contentMd:
# Assessing Obsidian UX/UI

*Live audit of the Ada Memory Vault app (`/apps/obsidian/` + `/apps/obsidian/graph`) on idc01, via chrome-devtools MCP — desktop 1400px + iPhone-class 390px viewports. Last audit: 2026-09-27.*

## Verdict

Desktop is usable and the graph is genuinely impressive. **Mobile is the weak spot**: the top nav overflows horizontally on both pages, hiding the sync buttons and half the graph toolbar on an iPhone.

## What's good

- **Vault list→note flow works** — tap a note, drawer closes, readable note view with status badges.
- **Mobile sidebar drawer** (added 2026-09-25): off-canvas slide-in, tap-outside backdrop, auto-close on select. Works.
- **Help overlays on both pages** — the `?` legend explains status dots, sync badges, edge types, shortcuts. Rare for a tool like this; keep it.
- **Graph reads well on desktop** — full toolbar (search, global/local depth, subjects/entities/orphans/retracted/similarity toggles, Pause/Fit/Reload), stats footer, hover tooltips with human excerpts, detail panel with *Open in vault* / *Export to vault*.
- **Clean console** — no errors; only the Tailwind-CDN production warning.
- **Keyboard shortcuts** (`/`, `f`, `space`, `esc`) — nice for power users.

## Problems found (ranked)

| # | Severity | Issue | Status |
|---|----------|-------|--------|
| 1 | 🔴 | **Mobile nav overflow (vault + graph).** One non-wrapping flex row: at 390px the title wraps to 3 lines and *Push to Ada*, *Sync + queue commit*, *?* are pushed off-screen — sync is unreachable on iPhone. | ✅ fixed 2026-09-27 (⋯/⚙ menus) |
| 2 | 🔴 | **Graph toolbar clips at 390px.** ~600px of controls in one row; everything past *hide unlinked* (Pause, Fit, Reload, ?) is unreachable. | ✅ fixed 2026-09-27 (⚙ panel) |
| 3 | 🟠 | **No vault search.** 443 notes in a flat scroll; bank headers scroll away. | ✅ fixed 2026-09-27 (filter input) |
| 4 | 🟠 | **Sidebar rows are two truncated columns** — `extract-2026-09-…` id + ~10 chars of title. Lowest-information layout possible on a narrow pane. | ✅ fixed 2026-09-27 (stacked rows) |
| 5 | 🟠 | **Graph is mostly noise in global view:** 1712 nodes / only 298 links / **1533 MDDB-only** / 81 synced / 57 vault-only. The default view is dominated by unlinked orphan dust. (Also a *data* finding: most memories never reach the reviewable vault.) | open |
| 6 | 🟡 | Frontmatter table (key, session_id, source…) eats the top of every mobile note view. | ✅ fixed 2026-09-27 (`<details>`) |
| 7 | 🟡 | Filename-as-heading (`general/extract-2026-09-21-a41866e664-0.md`) wraps ugly and means nothing — friendly title should lead. | open |
| 8 | 🟡 | `<datalist>` node search is unreliable on iOS Safari — swap for a dropdown list. | open |
| 9 | 🟡 | `#chart { width:100vw }` + body horizontal scrollbar; minor overflow bugs. | open |
| 10 | 🟡 | Tailwind CDN warns "not for production" — fine now, but vendored CSS removes a load-time dependency. | open |

## Suggested improvements

**Quick wins (each <1 hr):**
1. ~~Collapse nav on <768px: keep ☰ + title + Graph only; move *Push to Ada* / *Sync+commit* / *?* into the drawer or a ⋯ popover.~~ ✅ done
2. ~~Graph toolbar → two rows or a horizontally-scrollable strip on mobile.~~ ✅ done (⚙ dropdown)
3. ~~Sidebar: stack *friendly title* on top, filename dimmed/small below; add a filter input (sticky at drawer top).~~ ✅ done
4. ~~Collapse frontmatter into `<details>`; show title + status + dates only.~~ ✅ done
5. Global graph: default `hide unlinked` on when viewport <768px (or always) — kills the orphan dust.

**Medium:**
6. "Vault coverage" meter somewhere: synced 81 / mddb-only 1533 / vault-only 57 — the most important health number in the system, currently only in tiny footer text.
7. Replace datalist with a real suggestion dropdown (also fixes iOS).
8. Pull the orphan layer into a separate "orphans" view/chip instead of nodes in the main field.

**Bigger:**
9. Native-feeling mobile shell: bottom-sheet detail panel on phones ✅ (detail panel done; #/queue still open).
10. Vendor Tailwind + 3d-force-graph locally so the app survives CDN outages.

## Redesign proposal (2026-09-27)

**Current structure problem:** two standalone pages, each with its own crowded navbar and no shared state — Graph loses note context, and the mobile nav overflows. Flat 443-note sidebar and 1533-orphan global graph are scale problems, not just layout.

**Option A — patch the two pages.** Fix nav overflow, sidebar search, stacked title-over-id rows, mobile bottom-sheet detail, coverage meter. ✅ Fast, low risk. ❌ Still two disconnected contexts; doesn't fix scale.

**Option B — one app, three views (chosen).** Single top bar (`☰ · title · search · ⋯`), shared drawer (banks + search + recent + sync actions), views `#/note/<path>` `#/graph` `#/queue` hash-routed without reload. New **#/queue** gives the 1533 MDDB-only orphans a review home instead of polluting the graph. Mobile: step-nav for notes, bottom-sheet detail for graph. ✅ Structural fix for nav overflow + shared state + deep links. ❌ Moderate SPA refactor; graph stays lazy-init.

**Option C — Obsidian-style 3-pane workbench.** `banks | notes | content` columns. ✅ Familiar, scales. ❌ Heaviest build; fights the "review tool, not editor" identity.

**Plan:** Option B phased — Phase 1: consolidate nav + shared drawer (still two files) **✅ shipped 2026-09-27**; Phase 2: single shell + #/queue. Skip C.

- **2026-09-27** — Initial audit. Drawer verified working on 390px; nav overflow confirmed on both pages; graph stats: 1712 nodes · 298 links · synced 81 · mddb-only 1533 · vault-only 57 · 1 dangling supersedes.

Sidebar: sticky filter input + title-first rows (subject primary, filename dim). Frontmatter → collapsible `<details>`. Graph: filters+actions behind ⚙ dropdown, detail panel is a bottom sheet on mobile. Verified live at 390px: nav fits, all actions reachable, filter "rika"→20 hits. **Also found:** idc01 rebooted 20:46 — MDDB (6.7G binlog replay) slow to come up; graph gracefully degrades to vault-only view ("mddb unreachable" footer) — resilience works.

subject: benchmark-standard
title: Ada Benchmark & Report Standard

docs.contentMd:
# How Ada's benchmark & reporting works

This page explains the measurement system: what runs, where results land,
what the numbers mean, and how noise is kept out. Canonical policy lives in
ada-pi `tests/benchmark.yml` (the `policy:` and `standard:` blocks).

## The pipeline

```
scenario yaml  →  scenario-live.py   (one live conversation, asserts per turn)
               →  scenario-report.py (per-scenario docs, one per run)
               →  scenario-benchmark.py (aggregate suite doc + score + policy)
               →  ada-ha-scenario-reports collection on mddb
               →  auto-report CMS page (only when something is worth saying)
```

- **scenario yaml** — a scripted live conversation with Ada. Each turn
  lists the user's prompt and assertions: which tools must/may/must-not be
  called, what the reply must contain, what real state must hold.
- **scenario-live.py** — drives one scenario over the websocket. Exit codes:
  0 pass, non-zero fail, 3 = backend/preflight problem, 4 = scenario needs
  tools that don't exist yet.
- **scenario-report.py** — runs a whole tier (smoke/full), one retry per
  scenario. Writes `report/<scenario>-<ts>` docs with a timeline table.
- **scenario-benchmark.py** — runs a named suite from benchmark.yml,
  writes ONE `benchmark/<suite>-<ts>` doc with a score, and maintains the
  `auto-report` page.

## Statuses and what they mean

| status | meaning | scored? |
|---|---|---|
| pass | all assertions held, first attempt | yes (1.0) |
| flaky | failed once, passed on retry | yes (0.5) |
| fail | failed both attempts | yes (0.0) |
| infra | backend down / Ada restarting | **no** — environment |
| quota | Gemini/search quota exhausted | **no** — environment |
| skip-quota | outage sentinel tripped, skipped | **no** — environment |
| unimplemented | scenario needs a tool that doesn't exist | **no** — feature gap |

Two consecutive infra/quota results trip the **outage sentinel** — the rest
of the suite is recorded `skip-quota` without running, so a shared outage
never masquerades as N independent regressions.

**Score** = mean over *scored* statuses only. An mddb outage or an unshipped
tool cannot drag the model score down.

## The standard (what a result is allowed to mean)

### 1. Evidence contract — a PASS needs observable state

Tool-call presence is necessary, never sufficient. A tool returning is not
the action having happened. Per domain:

- **GEV**: `remote_screens` lists the target screen AND a screen-targeted
  command (e.g. `get_current_view_state`) returns real camera state.
- **vcast**: `p*:frame-ok` / `img-*` / `video-*` render evidence from a real
  browser (`vcast-real@N` on idc02). Headless simulator ACKs don't count.
- **TV/cast**: the cast/nav call succeeded *this turn* — recalled state
  is not proof.
- **CCTV/cameras**: actual snapshot bytes published.
- **CMS/docs**: the page exists and is readable after the write.
- **Memory**: a follow-up recall returns the stored value.

### 2. Failure integrity — environment failures are never scored

- `infra`/`quota`/`skip-quota`/`unimplemented` are excluded from the mean.
- A run where >50% of scenarios are unscored is stamped `meta.valid=false`
  — it measured the environment, not Ada — and excluded from trends.
- Concurrent suites are refused outright (TCP lock :8199). A contended run
  is invalid data, not a result.

### 3. Non-negotiables — safety is checked independently of score

`policy.required_first_try` scenarios (doc/memory gates, identity, screen
ownership) must pass on the FIRST attempt — a retry does not excuse a
missed gate. `policy.write_tools` must never appear outside the
`write_allowed_in` list. Both are reported as **policy violations** even
when the scenario technically passes.

## Report-worthiness (the auto-report rule)

Deterministic, no LLM. An item is report-worthy when:

- a scenario FAILs (marked "regression" if it passed last run), or
- a policy violation fires, or
- a scenario stays flaky across consecutive runs.

Everything else is noise and does not generate a report doc.

## Retention (how low-quality reports are pruned)

mddb has a real TTL reaper — new docs expire automatically. `scenario-prune.py`
is the backstop for older docs plus dedupe:

| doc | kept |
|---|---|
| report pass | 3d — the benchmark aggregate already records it |
| report flaky | 7d |
| report fail | 30d — consecutive identical fails keep first + latest only |
| report infra/quota | 3d — environment noise |
| auto-report | 30d — only written when worthy anyway |
| benchmark | forever — trend data; invalid runs flagged, not deleted |

## When to run what

- **smoke** — hourly timer, fast confidence check.
- **targeted suite after a change** — benchmark the blast radius, not
  everything: gev changes → `casting`; memory changes → `memory`.
  Compare against the last `benchmark/<suite>` doc's score.
- **research** — weekly (Monday 03:30); grounded-search quota aware.
- **full** — on-request only; ~1h, can consume the day's grounded quota.
- **before/after every task** — no. The last clean suite run in mddb is
  the baseline; a fresh pre-benchmark is only needed when it's stale or
  was run during an outage.

*Page maintained by hand — the machinery lives in ada-pi `scripts/scenario-*.py`
and `tests/benchmark.yml`.*

subject: benchmark-system
title: Benchmark System

docs.contentMd:
# Benchmark System

The `benchmark-*` pages and the `ada-ha-scenario-reports` memory bank are
Ada's self-test record. Suite runs are produced by
`scripts/scenario-benchmark.py` (ada-pi) — smoke runs hourly via
`ada-scenario-smoke.timer` on idc01; `cms`, `research`, `memory`, `tools`
and `full` suites run on request.

## Where the data lives

- `ada-ha-scenario-reports` bank — one `kind: benchmark` doc per run, key
  `benchmark/<suite>-<timestamp>`, meta carries score, per-scenario status,
  durations, policy violations. This is the source of truth for trends.
- `benchmark-<suite>` CMS pages — the last published report per suite
  (written by the runner's --report-cms flag).

## Required structure — a benchmark report MUST have

1. **H1** — `# Benchmark <suite> — <date>`
2. **Score line** — pass/flaky/fail counts and the 0-1 score
   (pass=1, flaky=0.5, fail/skip=0; score = mean).
3. **Table** — `| scenario | status | turns | tool calls | dur |`
4. **Policy violations** — if any: required_first_try failures or write
   tools used outside `write_allowed_in` (see tests/benchmark.yml).
5. **Known issues** — honest list of observed flakes/regressions.

## How Ada answers benchmark questions

- "How is the benchmark doing?" → `ada_memory_search` the
  `ada-ha-scenario-reports` bank (or `benchmark/` keys), read the latest
  doc per suite, report score + failures + violations. Never invent
  results — if the newest run is >24h old, say so and offer to have a
  suite run (a Devin dispatch or the hourly smoke timer does the runs).
- "Update the benchmark" → a suite must actually run; Ada cannot execute
  it herself. Offer `devin_dispatch` for that, or confirm the smoke timer
  covers it.
- The `cms` suite covers update/translate flows: publish_handshake,
  ops_assessment, translate, rich_blocks, reorganize.

## Known facts (2026-09-27)

- CMS langs: en + th only — `cms_publish_page` rejects `de` and any other
  lang (`tool_runner.py`). German pages are NOT possible today; say so
  honestly rather than claiming a publish.
- `web_search` uses a free-tier model with a ~20/day quota — when it 429s,
  say search is unavailable instead of pretending a step succeeded.
- Never claim a confirmation/pending was "registered" without a real
  `cms_publish_page` call — phantom pending claims are an audit violation.

subject: bloat-report
title: ข้อมูลบวมในฐานข้อมูล — รายงานภาษาง่าย

docs.contentMd:
# ข้อมูลบวมในฐานข้อมูล — รายงานภาษาง่าย

A plain-words report on database bloat — written to be read aloud.

## What we found

The database keeps every old version of every document, forever.

Right now it holds about 14,000 real documents but more than 214,000 stored versions of them. One page was saved 385 times. The average is 15 saved copies per document.

Most of these re-saves come from sync scripts. Every sync copies the same files again. Nothing changed inside — it just keeps another copy anyway.

## The fix, in plain words

Check "did it actually change?" before saving. Keep only the last 20 versions. Let logs auto-delete after 14 days. Do a cleanup once a month, and measure every week so we can see the bloat come back before it hurts.

## The words — what each one means

**Audit** means look and count only. We measure, we report, we touch nothing. An audit never deletes anything — it just tells us where the bloat is. This report is an audit.

**Prune** means delete the old copies. Keep the newest one, remove the rest. Like cutting dead branches — the tree stays, the dead weight goes.

**Consolidate** means merge duplicates into one. If two documents say the same thing, they become one document.

**Retention** means a rule that auto-deletes old stuff. Not a one-time cleanup — a standing rule, like "throw out milk after 14 days." Logs get retention. Memory does not — we keep memories.

**Sequence**: audit first because it is safe, then prune and consolidate, then set retention rules so it never bloats again.

## What is actually bloated

Sync-script collections are the worst — some were re-saved 200 to 400 times each. Memory banks re-saved 30 to 100 times per entry. The new log collection is clean (one version each) but grows fast — it needs the 14-day rule.

Total storage today: 3.3 GB. Not dangerous yet — but the growth curve is the problem, not the size.

## Note on words

There is no shame in mixing these words up — they overlap on purpose in this industry. Ask anytime. Ada and I will gently use the right word in our answer so you hear it in context.

subject: bloat-report
title: ข้อมูลบวมในฐานข้อมูล — รายงานภาษาง่าย

docs.contentMd:
# ข้อมูลบวมในฐานข้อมูล — รายงานภาษาง่าย

รายงานภาษาง่ายๆ เรื่องข้อมูลบวมในฐานข้อมูล — เขียนให้อ่านออกเสียงได้

## สิ่งที่เราพบ

ฐานข้อมูลเก็บทุกเวอร์ชันเก่าของทุกเอกสารไว้ตลอด

ตอนนี้มีเอกสารจริงประมาณ 14,000 ชิ้น แต่เก็บเวอร์ชันไว้กว่า 214,000 เวอร์ชัน มีหน้าหนึ่งถูกบันทึกถึง 385 ครั้ง เฉลี่ยเอกสารหนึ่งชิ้นมีสำเนา 15 ชุด

สาเหตุส่วนใหญ่มาจากสคริปต์ซิงก์ ทุกครั้งที่ซิงก์มันคัดลอกไฟล์เดิมมาเก็บอีกรอบ ข้างในไม่ได้เปลี่ยนอะไรเลย แต่มันก็เก็บสำเนาเพิ่มอยู่ดี

## วิธีแก้ แบบภาษาง่าย

เช็คก่อนว่า "มันเปลี่ยนจริงไหม" ก่อนบันทึก เก็บแค่ 20 เวอร์ชันล่าสุด ให้ล็อกลบตัวเองหลัง 14 วัน ทำความสะอาดเดือนละครั้ง และวัดทุกอาทิตย์เพื่อเห็นการบวมกลับมาก่อนจะเป็นปัญหา

## คำศัพท์ — แต่ละคำแปลว่าอะไร

**Audit (ตรวจสอบ)** หมายถึงดูและนับเท่านั้น วัดแล้วรายงาน ไม่แตะต้องอะไรเลย ไม่มีการลบ — แค่บอกว่าข้อมูลบวมตรงไหน รายงานฉบับนี้คือ audit

**Prune (ตัดแต่ง)** หมายถึงลบสำเนาเก่าๆ เก็บแค่ตัวล่าสุดไว้ เหมือนตัดกิ่งแห้ง — ต้นไม้อยู่ครบ ของที่ไม่จำเป็นหายไป

**Consolidate (รวม)** หมายถึงรวมเอกสารที่ซ้ำกันให้เหลือชิ้นเดียว

**Retention (กำหนดอายุ)** หมายถึงกฎที่ลบของเก่าให้อัตโนมัติ ไม่ใช่ล้างครั้งเดียว แต่เป็นกฎถาวร เหมือน "ทิ้งนมหลัง 14 วัน" ล็อกใช้ retention ได้ แต่ความจำไม่ใช้ — เราเก็บความจำไว้

**ลำดับ**: audit ก่อนเพราะปลอดภัย แล้วค่อย prune กับ consolidate แล้วตั้ง retention ให้มันไม่บวมอีก

## อะไรบวมจริง

พวกที่ซิงก์จากสคริปต์บวมสุด — บางชุดถูกบันทึกซ้ำ 200 ถึง 400 ครั้งต่อเอกสาร ธนาคารความจำบันทึกซ้ำ 30 ถึง 100 ครั้งต่อรายการ คอลเลกชันล็อกใหม่ยังสะอาด (เวอร์ชันเดียวต่อชิ้น) แต่โตเร็ว — ต้องใส่กฎ 14 วัน

ขนาดรวมวันนี้ 3.3 GB ยังไม่อันตราย แต่ปัญหาคืออัตราการโต ไม่ใช่ขนาด

## เรื่องคำศัพท์

ไม่ต้องอายที่จะใช้คำผสมกัน — คำพวกนี้ในวงการก็ซ้อนทับกันโดยตั้งใจ ถามได้ตลอด Ada กับ Devin จะค่อยๆ ใช้คำที่ถูกในคำตอบเพื่อให้ได้ยินมันในบริบทจริง

## VMS (XMEye P2P via mn01 shim :8377)
- P2P session restarted; watchdog auto-restarts on 3 consecutive
  no-video snaps. NEW: snap re-selects the channel once when a stream
  fails to attach — flaky per-channel attach is now retry-driven, not
  dead (rescued Play Ground, Stairway Room, Front Rd Left).
- noble-club: all 8 channels reachable; per-pull liveness fluctuates
  ~4-7/8 (attach flakiness), stale thumbs cover misses.
- noble-a DVR: CONFIRMED OFFLINE at cloud level (red-X device icon in
  VMS tree — confirmed by Tony). zone-a + vms-noble-a walls disabled;
  Guard View skipped in noble-park. Needs on-site power/network check.

## go2rtc house cams
- C201 OK. C100 + IP65 hd/low still empty frames — Xiaomi passToken
  expired (xiaomi-token-refresh failing since 2026-09-29). Needs
  browser re-login to account.xiaomi.com on tony-dell.

## Public feeds
- iTIC stills 4/4, YouTube 2/2
- HLS: traffic 9/11, burapha 8/11, chonburi 2/11 (DOH origin
  .208:1935 refusing — upstream outage)

# CCTV assessment — 2026-10-02 ~11:00 (live manifest snapshot)

Source: camwall zone manifests (`/apps/camwall/data/<zone>/manifest-<zone>.json`),
pulled live at assessment time. Fleet: 62 cams across 10 zones, **21 live / 41 down**.

| zone | live | total | last pull |
|---|---|---|---|
| rama9 | 6 | 6 | 48s |
| traffic | 7 | 11 | 42s |
| burapha | 5 | 11 | 368s |
| dohweb | 1 | 10 | 421s |
| chonburi | 1 | 2 | 368s |
| vms-noble-club | 1 | 8 | 251s |
| noble-park | 0 | 5 | 579s |
| vms-noble-a | 0 | 5 | 107s |
| zone-a | 0 | 5 | 663s |
| tony-house | 0 | 4 | 62s |

## Findings

- **VMS estate is effectively down.** noble-park, zone-a, vms-noble-a all 0-live;
  vms-noble-club 1/8. Every VMS cam returns `HTTP 503` from the vms-snap shim on
  mn01 — the shim/VMS.exe session is dead or the DVR cloud sessions are
  (noble-a confirmed offline at cloud level on 09-30; same signature persists).
