docs.contentMd:
# CCTV Request Flow — Voice Command to Screen (Ada · VMS · XMEye)

How "Ada, show me the swimming pool camera" becomes a picture on a screen,
including the XMEye DVR layer. Written 2026-10-01 alongside the status-card
standard rollout.

## The chain

```
voice turn  →  ada_camera_snapshot {channel}
        │        backend/realtime_provider.py — 45s budget
        ▼        backend/vms_camera.py — GET mn01:8377/snap?ch=…
   vms-snap.py on mn01 (inside xmeye-vms podman, Wine + Xvfb :99)
   1. channels.json — name/alias → {x,y, device: DVR serial}
   2. global lock (serial — one snap at a time, ~35–90s worst case)
   3. xdotool: pin 4-grid → scroll device tree → double-click channel row
   4. row-highlight verification (layout-drift guard)
   5. double-click pane 1 → zoom (~4× resolution)
   6. _has_video poll — 3 rounds × 8 × 1.5s; re-select between rounds
   7. xwd -root → crop pane → PNG → 200 (+x-channel header)
   8. dead after retries → 503 · unknown name → 404 + channel list
      watchdog: 3 consecutive all-dead sweeps → restarts VMS.exe
        │
        ▼   P2P attach over XMEye cloud (www.xmeye.net)
     DVR     noble-club  serial d811d82e21d6c031
             noble-a     serial f2ca2dca0bc4ae4f…
        │
        ▼  PNG returns to Ada
   _camera_snapshot publishes the frame to the input-bridge
   (POST /api/input-bridge/frame, token=cam:<slug>-<ts>) → cast_url,
   plus a static copy under /static/cam-snap/.
   Vision sidecar (moondream @ tony-omen:11434, ADA_VISION_MODE=describe)
   turns the frame into text — no Gemini image quota burned.
        │
        ▼
   cast_to_screen(action='image', url=cast_url) → screen N
   vcast_snapshot verifies what's actually displayed.
```

## DVR realities the flow has to survive

- **Device-tree listing ≠ liveness.** A DVR can list all channels while its
  cloud session is dead (noble-a red-X for ~36h). Only a stream attach
  proves the camera is up — that's what the _has_video poll checks.
- **Serial shim.** One global lock; every snap holds it for up to ~90s.
  The camwall puller budget-skips VMS zones so walls don't starve.
- **Tree drift.** channels.json is a positional map — the shim verifies the
  selected row and errors loudly ('recalibrate channels.json') instead of
  snapping the wrong camera.

## Guaranteed-image standard (2026-10-01)

Live snap fails → `stale_snapshot()` finds the camwall last-good thumb by
slug across the VMS zone manifests → result carries `stale:true, age_s,
live_error`. A failed pull generates `<key>-status.jpg` — dimmed last-good
+ bilingual banner (STALE/DELAYED/OFFLINE/NO SIGNAL + "last frame <age>"):

| class   | trigger                        | look                         |
|---------|--------------------------------|------------------------------|
| stale   | pull failed, thumb < 6h        | dimmed frame + amber STALE   |
| delayed | VMS budget skip this cycle     | dimmed frame + blue DELAYED  |
| offline | no thumb ever, or > 6h old     | red OFFLINE (slate/dimmed)   |
| error   | other                          | NO SIGNAL                    |

Consumers: wall tiles show the card when !ok · montage bakes the card ·
**the card is what lands on a cast screen** for a dead cam — the raw
last-good still feeds the describe/vision path. Card deleted on next
successful pull. Standard: docs/ssot/apps/ssot.apps.camwall.yml.

## Reports → CMS → Ada tells Tony (closed loop)

- `cam-wall-cms.py` (15min timer, tony-dell) republishes `wall-<zone>` +
  `cctv-walls` index + per-zone 24h detection timeline into ada-cms-pages.
- As of 2026-10-01 it also diffs per-zone live counts
  (`_cms-notify-state.json`) and POSTs `/api/notify` on transitions only —
  zone recovered, zone went all-dead. Deferred (non-urgent) note — Ada
  relays it without hijacking the current turn.
- Ada-side rules: 'live' only for fresh snap or age < 2×interval; stale →
  quote the age; no thumb ever → 'no image yet'. wall_offline_dvr scenario
  guards the all-dead honesty path.

## Verified live 2026-10-01

camera_stale_fallback PASS (tennis, honest age) · camera_snapshot PASS
(pool, "17 min ago") · camera_snapshot_offline PASS (guardhouse,
"2,096 min ago") · wall_offline_dvr PASS (noble-a all-dead) · wall_ops
PASS · noble-a partially back: Road In + Walkway In live (visible flood
water on Road In), Guard View / Road Corner / CAM01 still OFFLINE cards.

docs.contentMd:
# สายท่อ CCTV ของอาดา — จากคำสั่งเสียงถึงภาพบนจอ

เวอร์ชันภาษาไทยของ "CCTV Request Flow" — อธิบายว่าประโยคว่า
"อาดา ขอดูกล้องสระว่ายน้ำหน่อย" กลายเป็นภาพบนจอได้ยังไง
รวมถึงชั้น XMEye DVR ด้วย (เขียน 2026-10-01)

## ลำดับขั้นตอน

```
คำสั่งเสียง  →  ada_camera_snapshot {channel}
        │        backend/realtime_provider.py — เวลาสูงสุด 45 วินาที
        ▼        backend/vms_camera.py — GET mn01:8377/snap?ch=…
   vms-snap.py บน mn01 (ใน podman xmeye-vms, Wine + Xvfb :99)
   1. channels.json — ชื่อ/alias → {x,y, device: serial ของ DVR}
   2. global lock (ทำทีละเครื่อง — snap หนึ่งใช้เวลา ~35–90 วินาที)
   3. xdotool: กริด 4 ช่อง → เลื่อน device tree → ดับเบิลคลิกแถวช่อง
   4. ตรวจว่าแถวถูกเลือกจริง (กัน layout เพี้ยน)
   5. ดับเบิลคลิก pane 1 → zoom (~4× ความละเอียด)
   6. _has_video poll — 3 รอบ × 8 × 1.5 วินาที; ลองเลือกใหม่ระหว่างรอบ
   7. xwd -root → crop pane → PNG → 200 (+header x-channel)
   8. ตายหลังลองซ้ำ → 503 · ชื่อไม่รู้จัก → 404 + รายชื่อช่อง
      watchdog: 3 รอบติดกันที่ทุกกล้องตาย → รีสตาร์ท VMS.exe
        │
        ▼   ต่อ P2P ผ่าน XMEye cloud (www.xmeye.net)
     DVR     noble-club  serial d811d82e21d6c031
             noble-a     serial f2ca2dca0bc4ae4f…
        │
        ▼  PNG กลับมาที่ Ada
   _camera_snapshot ส่งเฟรมเข้า input-bridge
   (POST /api/input-bridge/frame, token=cam:<slug>-<ts>) → cast_url,
   บวกสำเนา static ที่ /static/cam-snap/
   Vision sidecar (moondream @ tony-omen:11434, ADA_VISION_MODE=describe)
   แปลงภาพเป็นข้อความ — ไม่เสียโควต้าภาพของ Gemini
        │
        ▼
   cast_to_screen(action='image', url=cast_url) → จอหมายเลข N
   vcast_snapshot ยืนยันว่าจอแสดงจริง
```

## ความจริงของ DVR ที่ระบบต้องรอด

- **รายชื่อช่องใน device tree ≠ กล้องมีชีวิต** — DVR list ช่องครบได้ทั้งที่
  session cloud ตาย (noble-a ขึ้นกากบาทแดง ~36 ชม.) การพิสูจน์จริงคือ
  การ attach stream — นี่คือสิ่งที่ _has_video ตรวจ
- **shim ทำทีละงาน** — lock เดียว ทุก snap ถือนานถึง ~90 วินาที
  camwall puller มี budget ข้ามโซน VMS เพื่อไม่ให้ wall อื่นติด
- **tree เพี้ยนได้** — channels.json เป็นแผนที่เชิงตำแหน่ง; shim ตรวจแถวที่เลือก
  และแจ้งเตือนดัง ๆ ('recalibrate channels.json') แทนที่จะส่งภาพกล้องผิดตัว

## มาตรฐาน "มีภาพเสมอ" (2026-10-01)

ถ้า snap สดล้มเหลว → `stale_snapshot()` หาภาพล่าสุดจาก camwall manifest
→ ผลลัพธ์มี `stale:true, age_s, live_error`; เมื่อ pull ไม่สำเร็จจะสร้าง
`<key>-status.jpg` — ภาพล่าสุดแบบหรี่ + แบนเนอร์สองภาษา
(STALE/DELAYED/OFFLINE/NO SIGNAL + "เฟรมล่าสุด <อายุ>"):

| ประเภท   | เงื่อนไข                          | หน้าตา                         |
|---------|-----------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| stale   | pull พลาด แต่ thumb อายุ < 6 ชม.   | เฟรมหรี่ + แถบ STALE สีเหลือง   |
| delayed | VMS ถูกข้ามด้วย budget รอบนี้       | เฟรมหรี่ + แถบ DELAYED สีฟ้า    |
| offline | ไม่เคยมี thumb หรือเก่า > 6 ชม.     | OFFLINE แดง                    |
| error   | อื่น ๆ                             | NO SIGNAL                      |

ผู้ใช้: tile ใน wall แสดงการ์ดเมื่อ !ok · montage อบการ์ดเข้ารูป ·
**การ์ดคือสิ่งที่ขึ้นจอ cast** สำหรับกล้องตาย — ภาพดิบล่าสุดใช้กับ
describe/vision เท่านั้น · การ์ดถูกลบเมื่อ pull สำเร็จรอบถัดไป
มาตรฐาน: docs/ssot/apps/ssot.apps.camwall.yml

## รายงาน → CMS → Ada บอก Tony (วงจรปิด)

- `cam-wall-cms.py` (timer 15 นาที บน tony-dell) เผยแพร่ `wall-<zone>` +
  ดัชนี `cctv-walls` + timeline การตรวจจับ 24 ชม. เข้า ada-cms-pages
- ตั้งแต่ 2026-10-01 diff จำนวนกล้องที่มีชีวิตต่อโซน
  (`_cms-notify-state.json`) และ POST `/api/notify` เฉพาะตอนเปลี่ยนสถานะ —
  โซนกลับมา หรือโซนตายทั้งใบ · เป็นโน้ตแบบ non-urgent — Ada แจ้งโดยไม่
  แทรกบทสนทนาปัจจุบัน
- กฎฝั่ง Ada: 'live' เฉพาะ snap สดหรืออายุ < 2×interval · stale → บอกอายุ ·
  ไม่เคยมี thumb → 'ยังไม่มีภาพ' · scenario wall_offline_dvr คุ้มเส้นทาง
  "ตายทั้งใบ" ไว้

## ตรวจสอบจริง 2026-10-01

camera_stale_fallback PASS (tennis บอกอายุซื่อตรง) · camera_snapshot PASS
(pool "17 นาทีก่อน") · camera_snapshot_offline PASS (guardhouse
"2,096 นาทีก่อน") · wall_offline_dvr PASS (noble-a ตายทั้งใบ) · wall_ops
PASS · noble-a กลับมาบางส่วน: Road In + Walkway In live (เห็นน้ำท่วมที่

# Chaba Compound AI System *Living report — updated as the architecture evolves. Domain: chaba-core. Began 2026-09-30.* ## What it is A **compound AI system** (Berkeley's umbrella term): multiple models, memory stores, and control logic wired together so each does the job it's best at. Not one big model — a fleet of specialists with a spine. ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph VOICE[Chaba Voice — idc01] V[User voice] --> STT[STT] STT --> RT[Gemini Live
realtime_provider] RT --> TR[tool_runner] end subgraph EXPERTS[Expert layer] RT --> TR TR -->|confirm gate| CS[student distilbert :8778
92% @ ~30ms] TR -->|heavy scoring| J4[gemma-3-4b idc02 :8777
routing 8/8 @ ~20s] TR -->|memory recall| MD[(MDDB banks
ada-*)] end subgraph MEMORY[Memory — reports are L2] MD --> CMS[ada-cms-pages
kind:report + timeline] CMS --> IDX[reports-index
projection, auto-regen] IDX -->|Ada reads first| RT end J4 -.bench/advisory.-> CS ``` ## Current components | layer | component | status | measured | |---|---|---|---| | confirm gate | distilbert student | ✅ live idc01:8778 | 12/13 golden, ~30ms | | heavy scorer | gemma-3-4b bf16 | ✅ live idc02:8777 | 83%, 20s, routing 8/8 | | advisory | gemma-3-1b | ⏸ retired — student replaced | 56% | | memory banks | MDDB ada-* | ✅ leader idc01, follower tony-dell | — | | reports | ada-cms-pages + index | ✅ live | freshness + timeline | | health | ops-health-report | ✅ 15min timer | caught Gemini 429 outage | ## Memory model — v2 (proposed, under review) Reports move from *side artifact* to **the curated tier**: ```mermaid flowchart TB L0[L0 raw — transcripts, sessions] --> L1[L1 banks — ada-* facts/recalls] L1 -->|distill| L2[L2 reports — summary/domain/fresh_for/timeline/links] L2 -->|auto| L3[L3 reports-index — navigation] RT2[Ada] -->|answer order: L3 → L2 → L1| L3 RT2 -->|new info| NU[cms_note_update → L2 timeline] ``` - **L0 raw** — transcripts, session logs. Cold storage, never queried live. - **L1 banks** — facts + recalls (current MDDB ada-* collections). Authoritative. - **L2 reports** — curated projections: summary, domain, fresh_for TTL, timeline of changes, `links:` to parent/child reports and source banks. *High-class = reviewed, dated, indexed.* - **L3 index** — `reports-index` auto-regen; Ada's first read. Reads go top-down (index → report → bank); writes bottom-up (raw → bank → distilled report). Freshness metadata gates reliance. ## What's already landed today - [x] report meta: summary/domain/fresh_for + timeline on every publish - [x] reports-index auto-regeneration - [x] cms_note_update — cheap linked-report annotation - [x] health reporter → `report/health-*` + `ops-health` page - [x] idc02 onboarded — hardened, tailnet, open-jev 4b homed - [x] student retrained — imperative affirmations now pass (12/13) ## Forward queue - [ ] `links:` field — parent/child + source-bank provenance in report meta - [ ] auto-distill: bench misses → corpus → nightly retrain timer - [ ] orch-bench harness: cascade/vote/router/verifier vs student baseline - [ ] L0→L1→L2 promotion jobs (transcript → memory → report) - [ ] scenario timers off idc01 → idc02 - [ ] mddb read-only replica on idc02 ## Scores so far | date | model | golden | latency | note | |---|---|---|---|---| | 09-30 | gemma-3-1b idc01 | 10/18 (56%) | 4.8s | retired | | 09-30 | gemma-3-4b idc02 | 15/18 (83%) | 19.6s | bench/routing only | | 09-30 | student v1 | 11/13 | ~30ms | imperative misses | | 09-30 | student v2 | **12/13** | ~30ms | live | *Maintainer: devin. docs.contentMd:
# Chaba Edge Plan — Cloudflare on surf-thailand.com

_2026-09-27 · Devin · domain: chaba.surf-thailand.com + *.chaba.surf-thailand.com_

## Architecture

```
internet → Cloudflare edge (SIN, ~15ms from TH)
         → cloudflared on idc01 (outbound-only, no public inbound ports)
         → per-hostname ingress → local services
```

`cloudflared` runs as a quadlet on idc01 (second instance on idc02 later
— CF health-checks tunnel replicas natively → free failover). idc01's
firewall drops ALL public inbound once the tunnel is live; today's
public IP stops mattering except as a SSH/Tailscale backdoor.

## Hostname layout

One wildcard DNS record + explicit ingress rules (keeps the app list
audited — no accidental exposure by adding a local service):

| Hostname | Backend | Access policy |
|---|---|---|
| `chaba.surf-thailand.com` | status/landing page (static, in stacks/web) | public |
| `ada.chaba…` | ada-pi-pwa :8001 | **none** — app-level user keys (KK/guests use this) |
| `cms.chaba…` | CMS pages (ada-pwa /cms or dedicated) | Access: Tony Google login |
| `gev.chaba…` | GEV + `/apps/gev-live/ws` | Access: Tony |
| `obsidian.chaba…` | obsidian-vault | Access: Tony |
| `mddb.chaba…` | mddb-panel | Access: Tony + CF rate-limit |
| `vms.chaba…` | noVNC bridge | Access: Tony (replaces Tailscale-User-Login gating for off-tailnet use) |

Cloudflared ingress sketch:

```yaml
ingress:
  - hostname: ada.chaba.surf-thailand.com
    service: http://127.0.0.1:8001
  - hostname: cms.chaba.surf-thailand.com
    service: http://127.0.0.1:8001
    originRequest: {httpHostHeader: cms}
  - hostname: gev.chaba.surf-thailand.com
    service: http://127.0.0.1:80        # caddy serves the static bundle
  - hostname: "*.chaba.surf-thailand.com"
    service: http_status:404           # explicit deny by default
  - service: http_status:404
```

## What each CF layer buys here

- **Tunnel**: zero inbound attack surface on the VPS — upgrades the
  "tailnet-only" posture to cover public reach too. The public IP can
  eventually go (cheaper VPS tier).
- **Access**: Google's login becomes the perimeter for Tony-only apps —
  better than IP tricks and works from any network. App-level keys
  (ada PWA) stay for shared/guest apps.
- **WAF + rate limiting**: protects the Ada endpoint from quota abuse —
  a public voice agent is free Gemini/OpenRouter compute for scrapers
  otherwise.
- **Caching**: PWA/static assets at SIN edge — actual speedup for the
  iPad.

## Privacy note (the one real cost)

CF terminates TLS for every proxied/tunneled app — voice transcripts and
memory content transit their edge in plaintext internally. For a
personal stack this is usually acceptable, but sensitive paths
(mddb-panel, obsidian) could stay tailnet-only if that ever bothers us —
the tunnel layout doesn't force anything public.

## Rollout order

1. Register DNS zone in CF, set `chaba.surf-thailand.com` + `*.chaba` CNAMEs
2. `cloudflared` quadlet on idc01, token from CF Zero-Trust dashboard
3. Start with ONE hostname: `ada` — verify ws/audio work through CF
4. Layer Access policies on Tony-only apps
5. When idc02 exists: second `cloudflared` → automatic tunnel HA
6. Only then consider dropping the public IP / tightening idc01 firewall

## Setup — DNS + Cloudflare (do in this order)

### 1. Onboard the domain (one-time, ~5 min + propagation)

1. CF dashboard → **Add site** → `surf-thailand.com` → Free plan
2. CF assigns two nameservers (e.g. `x.ns.cloudflare.com`)
3. At the domain registrar: replace existing NS records with CF's pair
4. Wait for CF to show **Active** (minutes to hours; `dig NS surf-thailand.com` to check)

### 2. Create the tunnel

1. **Zero Trust → Networks → Tunnels → Create** → name `chaba` → copy the token
2. Choose **dashboard-managed** (public hostnames edited in UI — no config files on the box)

### 3. cloudflared on idc01 (quadlet)

`stacks/services/cloudflared/cloudflared.container`:

```ini
[Container]
Image=docker.io/cloudflare/cloudflared:latest
Exec=tunnel --no-autoupdate run
Secret=<cf-tunnel-token-secret-name>,type=env,target=TUNNEL_TOKEN
Network=host

[Service]
Restart=always

[Install]
WantedBy=default.target
```

```bash
podman secret create cf_tunnel_token < <(echo -n 'eyJ...TOKEN...')
systemctl --user daemon-reload && systemctl --user start cloudflared
systemctl --user status cloudflared   # look for "Registered tunnel connection"
```

### 4. Public hostnames (dashboard — auto-creates the DNS)

For each row below, **Tunnels → chaba → Public Hostnames → Add**:

| Public hostname | Service | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `chaba.surf-thailand.com` | `http://127.0.0.1:80` (caddy → status page) | public |
| `ada.chaba.surf-thailand.com` | `http://127.0.0.1:8001` | none (app keys) |
| `cms.chaba.surf-thailand.com` | `http://127.0.0.1:8001` (path /apps/ha/ada-tony/cms) | Tony only |
| `gev.chaba.surf-thailand.com` | `http://127.0.0.1:80` | Tony only |
| `obsidian.chaba.surf-thailand.com` | `http://127.0.0.1:<obsidian port>` | Tony only |
| `mddb.chaba.surf-thailand.com` | `http://127.0.0.1:<panel port>` | Tony only |

Adding each hostname auto-creates the matching `CNAME →
<tunnel-id>.cfargotunnel.com` record — no manual DNS editing needed.
(Verify: **DNS → Records** will show them all, proxied.)

### 5. Access policies (Tony-only apps)

**Zero Trust → Access → Applications → Add** — one app per Tony-only
hostname, or one app covering `*.chaba.surf-thailand.com` minus the
public paths:

- Application domain: `cms.chaba.surf-thailand.com` (repeat per app)
- Policy: `Allow` → `Emails: <your gmail>` → provider: Google
- Session duration: 12h (re-login is cheap on a personal stack)

### 6. Verify

```bash
curl -sI https://ada.chaba.surf-thailand.com/ | head -3     # 200 + cf-ray header
curl -sI https://cms.chaba.surf-thailand.com/ | grep -i location  # 302 → CF login
dig +short ada.chaba.surf-thailand.com   # → <id>.cfargotunnel.com
```

Ada voice sanity: open `ada.chaba…`, one utterance — websockets pass
through the tunnel transparently.

### 7. Lock down idc01 (last step, after ~a week of clean tunnel runs)

```bash
# keep only Tailscale+SSH public; drop 80/443 inbound on the public iface
sudo ufw deny in on <pubiface> to any port 80,443 proto tcp
```

Test tailnet access before/after — the tunnel makes public inbound
unnecessary, but keep SSH on the public IP until you're confident.

## Current posture (what already exists)

already running:

| Primitive | Status |
|---|---|
| Nightly mddb snapshot | ✅ `mddb-backup.timer` 02:30 → native `/v1/backup` → `~/mddb-backups/` (7-day retention) |
| Off-host backup copy | ✅ `mddb-backup-pull.timer` on tony-omen |
| Standby replica | ✅ `mddb-standby-pull.timer` on tony-dell — file-copy replica |
| Ada standby node | ✅ mn01 runs Ada standby (chaba-web lane) |
| Portable stacks | ✅ all services are host-agnostic quadlets under `stacks/services/*` |
| Readiness gates | ✅ ada-* waits for mddb `/health` (installed 2026-09-27) |
| Health visibility | ⚠️ mcp-health exists; no uptime alerting yet (Beszel proposed) |
| Verified restore | ❌ restore tested for open-notebook only (`open-notebook-restore-check.timer`); mddb restore never rehearsed |
| Live replication | ❌ file-copy standby ≠ live replica; mddb upstream HAS real replication |

## Tiering — what HA actually means here

| Tier | Services | Target |
|---|---|---|
| **A — must survive** | mddb (all Ada memory), ada-ha-tony | RPO ≤24h now → ≤5min with replication; RTO ≤30min |
| **B — degraded OK** | ada-pi-pwa, caddy-edge, obsidian-vault, open-notebook | RPO ≤24h, RTO ≤2h |
| **C — best effort** | doc-archive, mddb-panel, input-bridge, ollama-proxy | rebuild when convenient |

## The plan

### Phase 1 — make rebuild deterministic (now, no new hardware)

The recovery path is the weak link: backups exist but **restore has
never been rehearsed**. One mddb restore drill + a written runbook:

1. Restore drill: take last night's `mddb-backups/*.db`, stand it up
   on tony-dell as `mddb-restore-test`, point an Ada client at it,
   verify a memory recall. Time it — that's our real RTO.
2. Write `runbook-idc01-rebuild.md`: fresh VPS → tailscale up → clone
   chaba → install.sh per stack → restore mddb.db → enable units.
   Target: <90 min cold rebuild.
3. Extend `open-notebook-restore-check` pattern to mddb: monthly
   automated restore-verify timer (restore to scratch container,
   `/v1/stats` doc-count check, tear down).

### Phase 2 — idc02 live replica (when the second server lands)

4. **mddb real replication**: upstream `tradik/mddb` ships primary→
   replica sync (the restore-sync fixes I found earlier are in this
   path). Run idc01 primary → idc02 replica; RPO drops from 24h to
   near-zero. The file-copy standby on tony-dell stays as tier-3
   insurance.
5. **Ada failover pair**: ada-ha-tony stays primary on idc01; mn01
   standby already exists — formalize: keep mn01's Ada pointed at
   mddb on the tailnet IP (not idc01-specific), document the manual
   cutover (switch HA websocket endpoint).
6. **Edge split — revised**: public reach moves to a **Cloudflare
   Tunnel** (`chaba-edge-plan`): outbound-only `cloudflared` on idc01,
   subdomain-per-app, CF Access as the identity gate. idc01 drops all
   public inbound. On idc02 a second `cloudflared` gives CF-native
   tunnel failover — the Phase-3 automatic failover comes free and
   safe (CF health-checks the tunnel, not our apps).

### Phase 3 — automatic failover (later, optional)

7. Healthcheck-driven routing: caddy `lb_policy` + health_uri across
   mddb primaries, or Tailscale `tailscale serve` failover. Only worth
   it once Phase 2 proves the replica is trustworthy — automatic
   failover to a bad replica is worse than manual.

## Failure matrix

| Event | Impact today | Plan answer |
|---|---|---|
| mddb crash-loop | Ada can't recall; restart storms | gates (done) + restore-verified backups (P1) |
| idc01 dies entirely | everything public + voice + memory down | tony-dell file-replica + mn01 Ada standby (P1 drill proves it) |
| idc01 + slow rebuild | days of degraded ops | idc02 live replica (P2) |
| mddb db corruption | backup restores corrupted copy | 7-day retention + off-host copy (done) |

## Cost of the honest version

- Phase 1: ~2 hours of my time, zero money
- Phase 2: idc02 (~฿420–856/mo — see `hosting-provider-assessment`)
- Phase 3: skip until needed — manual cutover at this scale is fine;
  premature failover automation is its own outage generator

**Bottom line**: provider backups correctly skipped — our RPO is the
nightly snapshot + off-host pull, our RTO is an unrehearsed restore.
The next concrete action is a **restore drill**, not more backup
infrastructure.

  key path — KK can be handed an iPad and walked through the checklist
  while transcripts auto-evaluate.

CMS page `lab-checklist` holds a fixed set of voice tasks (ask time/
flood status, remember a preference, publish a page, ask to recall it
next session, try an English question). Each session gets a transcript;
a `transcript_eval` pass grades tool-calls, answer correctness, and
language fidelity afterward — real-user signal without scripting her.

1. Smoke timer live hourly — watch `lab-results` tomorrow for flakes.
2. Nightly `--tier full` + weekly trend digest to `chaba-home/report`.
3. `speaker:` session override so KK-scoped scenarios run in CI (today

- KK test day: checklist page + record sessions + eval pass after.

memory/context system, and the scripts that keep everything in sync.
It started life as a 3DGS/Frigate research stack (README still says

title: CMS Edit Manual

docs.contentMd:
# CMS Edit Manual — how to work on pages

The CMS viewer now has an **Edit drawer**: open any page, click **Edit**
(top-right), pick a section (or "whole page"), and push a button.

## The ops

| op | what it does | needs |
|---|---|---|
| **Add** | appends markdown to the page (or into a section) | text |
| **Update** | replaces the section body, or the whole page if no section picked | text |
| **Improve** | rewrites tighter — keeps every fact, no new info | section (or page) |
| **Expand** | deepens the section with more detail | section (or page) |
| **Consolidate** | merges overlapping/duplicate sections in a page | page |
| **Split →** | moves the picked section to a NEW page, leaves a link behind | section + target slug |
| **Merge ←** | pulls another page's content into this one and marks that page superseded | target slug |

## Sections

Sections are markdown `## Heading` blocks — pick one by name from the
dropdown. The textarea scopes to that section so you can see/edit just
it. "whole page" = the entire markdown.

## What happens on every edit

- `meta.updated` refreshes, a timeline entry is appended
- `reports-index` regenerates, so the change shows up in Ada's index
- `split`/`merge` write the `links`/`supersedes`/`superseded_by` fields
  on both pages so the graph stays honest

## Voice path is unchanged

Ada still uses `cms_publish_page` / `cms_note_update` — the drawer is a
*human* tool, not a voice tool. Voice write-confirmation gates are
untouched.

subject: cms-page-standard
title: CMS page standard — landing-page format

docs.contentMd:
# CMS page standard — landing-page format

Every `ada-cms-pages` document should open like a mini landing page:
the reader gets the verdict and the newest developments without
scrolling, and can jump to detail via section links.

## Required structure

```markdown
# Title — matches meta.title

**Status: one-line verdict a reader can act on.**

## Latest

- **YYYY-MM-DD** — newest development first, one line each (≤5 entries;
  roll older ones into a History/archive section at the bottom).

Sections: [Section A](#section-a) · [Section B](#section-b)

## Section A / Section B ...

## History — earlier dated entries, newest first (optional)

*Generated by <writer> · <date>Z · sources: <n>*  ← provenance footer
```

## Rules

1. **Status line first** — bold, immediately under the H1. Answers
   "what's the current state?" in one sentence.
2. **`## Latest` before detail** — reverse-chronological, dated bullets.
   Updated pages put the change here, not buried mid-document.
3. **Section links** — one line of markdown anchor links right after
   Latest when the page has >2 sections.
4. **Media welcome** — charts/diagrams embedded as `![alt](url)` with
   assets served from `stacks/web/public/apps/reports/` (reachable at
   `https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net/apps/reports/<file>`).
   Benchmarks should always include a graph, not just a table.
5. **Provenance footer** — `*Generated by … · sources: …*` (audit rule
   R2); generated reports also need `meta.sources` (R1).
6. **Meta** — full schema block: kind=page, slug, title, format,
   updated, bank, scope, status, source, written_by, subject,
   attribute, valid_from, last_verified.

## Audit

`scripts/ada/cms-audit.py` enforces the older A/R/N/S rules plus:
- `status: stub` or `status: archived` skips the A1 thin check — mark
  intentional stubs instead of leaving empty pages failing.
- `A5_EXEMPT` covers docs that describe the placeholder rule itself
  (`cms-audit-report`, `document-audit-policy`).

State after 2026-10-01 cleanup: **133 pass · 0 fail · 29 warnings**
(remaining warnings: S1 schema gaps on `wall-*`, C1 duplicate pairs,
R5 missing registry docs).

subject: colab-assessment
title: Colab assessment — GPU offload for chaba/ada

docs.contentMd:
# Colab Assessment — GPU offload options for the chaba/ada stack

_2026-09-27 · devin session · status: assessment (no purchase made)_

## Why now

Our only GPU host is **tony-omen** (GTX 1650 Mobile, 4 GB VRAM) — and its link
is currently down. Everything GPU-side is contended: `mcp-gpu` literally has to
`hold_llama` (drop llama-server to CPU) to free VRAM for an imagen2 run. Any
batch GPU work we add (embedding backfills, evals, transcription) competes with
the always-on Llama router. Question: can Colab absorb the batch tier?

## What Colab offers (Sept 2026)

Colab Pro/Pro+ are being folded into **Google AI plans** (announced 2026-09-22);
legacy Colab subs still work and stack.

| Tier | Price | Compute units | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | ~nothing guaranteed | T4 when available, ~12h sessions |
| **Colab Pro** | ~$9.99/mo ($8.33 annual) | 100/mo | premium GPU queue (L4/A100), high-mem machines, terminal |
| **Colab Pro+** | ~$49.99/mo ($41.66 annual) | 500/mo | Pro + **background execution** (runs without browser open) |
| Google AI Pro/Ultra | existing subs | included benefits | Ultra adds Premium GPU + uninterrupted background exec |

Rough unit burn: T4 ≈ 2 CU/hr · L4 ≈ 5 CU/hr · A100 ≈ 13 CU/hr.
So Pro ≈ ~50h T4 or ~7h A100 per month; Pro+ is 5× that.

## Fit against our workloads

| Workload | Fit | Why |
|---|---|---|
| MDDB re-embed / embedding backfill | ✅ excellent | pure batch; nomic-embed-text or text-embedding-004 parity check, measure tokens/s vs tony-omen CPU |
| Model evals for Llama router candidates | ✅ excellent | run candidates on L4/A100, benchmark, pick — noVRAM juggling at home |
| Whisper batch transcription (audio backlogs) | ✅ excellent | large-v3 on T4 ≈ 10-20× realtime |
| Image generation batches | ✅ good | SDXL/Diffusers on L4; frees tony-omen entirely |
| LoRA fine-tunes | ⚠️ possible | fits L4/A100 but session caps bite; needs Pro+ background exec for real runs |
| Always-on services (mcp-llama, mcp-gpu) | ❌ no | ephemeral runtimes, ~24h max, idle disconnect, no inbound ports, no Docker |
| Latency-sensitive / MCP-callable compute | ❌ no | cold-start + queue; nothing to call synchronously |

**Rule of thumb: Colab = batch GPU, not a host.** Anything with a service
endpoint stays at home (or moves to a real GPU VPS).

## Alternatives compared

| Option | Cost | vs Colab |
|---|---|---|
| **Kaggle notebooks** | free, ~30 GPU-hr/wk (T4×2 / P100) | covers most of our batch needs at $0 — try this first |
| Colab Enterprise (GCP) | pay-go: T4 ~$0.49/hr, L4 ~$0.78/hr, A100 ~$4.1/hr | same notebook UX, real billing, no monthly quota cliff; better for occasional spikes |
| vast.ai / runpod | ~$0.20–0.50/hr real GPUs | can host *services* (inbound ports, Docker) — the answer if we ever need an always-on GPU endpoint |
| Google AI Ultra | existing sub check | if already subscribed, Colab premium + background exec come free — verify before buying Pro+ |

## Integration path (if adopted)

1. Keep notebook templates in repo (`notebooks/colab/` in chaba or ada-pi):
   param cell for job type + input refs; Drive folder as the artifact sink.
2. Results write-back: either (a) notebook pushes to MDDB `/v1/add` via
   userspace Tailscale (`tailscaled --tun=userspace-networking` works in Colab —
   auth key needed), or (b) write artifacts to Drive and let an idc01 cron pull.
   Option (b) is simpler and keeps secrets off the notebook.
3. Devin workflow: generate/refresh notebook → Tony kicks the run (Colab has no
   API to start runtimes unattended) → artifacts land → idc01 ingest job.

## Recommendation

- **Pilot free first**: run one MDDB re-embed benchmark on Kaggle's free
  T4×2 vs tony-omen CPU to get real numbers — no spend.
- If batch GPU becomes a recurring need: **Colab Pro at ~$10/mo** is trivially
  cheap; skip Pro+ unless overnight unattended runs matter (or it's already
  covered by an existing Google AI sub).
- If we ever need a *hosted* GPU service (always-on inference off tony-omen):
  that's vast.ai/runpod/GPU VPS territory, not Colab.

## Open questions

- Is there an existing Google AI Pro/Ultra subscription on the account?
  (If yes, most of this is already unlocked.)
- How much batch work actually exists — real backlog vs hypothetical?
- Worth a notebook template + Drive sink setup only if the pilot shows
  meaningful speedup.

title: Colab GPU Media-Gen Research

docs.contentMd:
# Colab GPU Media-Gen Research

Free Google Colab GPU (Tesla T4) as an on-demand lab for image/video generation experiments. Sessions are ephemeral — `colab run` allocates a fresh VM per job and releases it; nothing stays warm (free GPU quota is scarce and idle VMs burn it).

## Tooling

- `google-colab-cli` — provision CPU/GPU/TPU sessions from the terminal. Note: installed 0.6.0 `exec` is broken with current `jupyter-kernel-client`; pin `uvx --from google-colab-cli==0.7.4` until the venv is upgraded.
- `colab-mcp` server (uvx `git+https://github.com/googlecolab/colab-mcp`) — registered in `~/.config/devin/mcp_config.json` as `colab-mcp`. Browser-side notebook control (open connection → add/run/update/move/delete/get cells).
- Experiment runner: `scripts/colab/img_gen.py` (chaba repo) — parameterized model/prompt/size/steps/seed, writes PNG + `report.json` to `/content/output`, pull with `colab download`.
- Artifacts land in `~/.local/colab-research/<exp>/` on tony-omen. Canonical notes: `docs/kb/colab-gpu-research.md` (chaba repo).

## Experiment log

### exp-01 — SD baseline (2026-09-30)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Model | prompthero/openjourney |
| Prompt | a serene lake in the mountains at sunset, highly detailed |
| Config | 512×512, 25 steps, guidance 7.5, seed 42 |
| Device | Tesla T4 (15360 MiB) |
| Pipeline load | 119.4 s (cold — weights download) |
| Generation time | 5.2 s |
| Peak VRAM | 3257.6 MB |
| Output | ~/.local/colab-research/exp-01/generated.png |

Result: PASS. fp16 512×512 gen is cheap on T4 — ~5 s/img, 3.2 GB VRAM. Headroom for 768×768 and for multiple images per session.

## Queue

| # | Task | Model | Config | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| exp-02 | Resolution scaling | prompthero/openjourney | 768×768, 25 steps | queued |
| exp-03 | Larger model | stabilityai/sdxl-turbo | 512×512 | queued — gated, needs HF_TOKEN |
| exp-04 | Video probe | SVD/Wan-class | short clip | queued — T4 feasibility check first |

## Notes

- HF downloads are unauthenticated by default (no token set). Gated models need `HF_TOKEN` in Colab secrets or `colab run --env HF_TOKEN=...`.

# Deep-dive session flow — analysis, improvements, benchmark

Date: 2026-09-27 · scenario: `tests/scenarios-live/deep_dive_flood_report.yaml`

## What the flow should be

Discuss → drill → analyze → improve → benchmark. Tony picks an artifact
(a flood report page), talks it over with Ada, she critiques, improves it,
and re-verifies — all inside one conversation.

## Live run findings (2026-09-27)

| Turn | Expectation | Ada did | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| "pull up the flood report" | `cms_get_page`/list/search | fetched + summarized correctly | ✓ |
| "analyze it like an editor" | (was: must call tool) | answered inline — no call, and the critique was genuinely good (imprecision, staleness) | ✓ behavior — scenario was wrong |
| "improve it — restructure + save + verify" | `cms_publish_page` | reached for `web_search` first, hit the 20/day grounding quota, then asked permission instead of publishing | partial |
| "yes, go ahead" | publish + verify | drafted new structure; publish handshake fired ("jumped the gun" → pending) | handshake working |

### Issues surfaced

1. **Quota trap**: when asked to *improve* a page she defaulted to
   fetching fresher data (`web_search`) instead of restructuring what
   exists — and hit the free-tier cap. Improve-with-what-we-have should
   be the default; research is a separate ask.
2. **Editorial turns shouldn't tool-call** — once the page is fetched,
   analysis is in-context. Fixed the scenario to assert `no_calls_except`
   (the L0-index design already predicted this).
3. **No benchmark turn yet** — the scenario needs a 5th step: "how do we
   measure if the report got better" → she should propose metrics
   (freshness, coverage, cite count, structure completeness) and ideally
   score the page.

## Improvements to land

- Ada instruction: "improve a page = restructure existing content; only
  reach for web_search when the user asks for new information"
- `cms_verify_page` block-report already returns structure — extend the
  improvement turn to compare before/after (report diff)
- Add a `benchmark` turn: she rates the updated page on a rubric
  (freshness/specificity/sources/structure 0-2 each) — gives a numeric
  before/after we can track in the ledger

## Benchmark proposal (report quality score)

Per report/page, score 0–8: specificity (proper names/dates), freshness
(timestamps within window), sources cited, structure completeness. Store
score in the page meta on each update — `cms_verify_page` could emit it.
Then "dig deep → improve" sessions become measurable: score should rise
each pass, and the trend is reviewable in the CMS report list.

docs.contentMd:
# Document Audit Policy Report

_2026-09-27 · Devin · live-verified against ada-cms-pages (40 pages)_

## Why this exists

Ada generates CMS pages through `cms_publish_page`, and until today
there was **no quality gate** — the first news-* batch shipped with
missing H1s, no source links, no "why it matters", and nobody could
tell without eyeballing every page. An audit rule-set now exists
(`chaba/scripts/ada/cms-audit.py`, committed `9f9eadb4`) plus a
tightened format spec (`news-system` page).

## The policy — what a page must satisfy

### Generic rules (all `kind: page` docs)

| Rule | Requirement |
|---|---|
| A1 | Body non-empty, ≥ 200 chars — *the empty-shell bug (`content_md` vs `contentMd`) is exactly what this catches* |
| A2 | Meta complete: `slug`, `title`, `format`, `updated`, `kind=page` |
| A3 | H1 heading present and matching the page title |
| A4 | Real structure — headings or lists, not a bare paragraph blob |
| A5 | No placeholders (TODO / TBD / lorem / placeholder) |
| A6 | No secret-shaped strings (`api_key=`, `password:`, …) |

### News brief rules (`news-*` pages only)

| Rule | Requirement |
|---|---|
| N1 | `TL;DR:` line — one sentence, concrete |
| N2 | ≤ 6 items per page |
| N3 | `[Source](url)` link per item |
| N4 | `Why it matters:` per item |

The full contract lives on the `news-system` page — Ada reads it before
drafting, so tightening the spec is the lever that improves output.

## What the first audit found (before → after)

| Group | Result |
|---|---|
| All 40 pages | 34 pass / **11 fail** |
| news-* (6 pages) | **all 6 failed**: missing H1 ×4, no sources ×4, no why-it-matters ×3, no TL;DR ×1 |

Fix loop that ran today:
1. `news_pages_update` scenario — Ada updated all 5 news pages (PASS
   on handshake/flow, but content failed audit).
2. Spec tightened → `news-system` now lists *required* elements.
3. `news_audit_fix` scenario — Ada re-drafted under the spec; 3 pages
   landed compliant, `news-world` got eaten by the pending-confirm
   handshake (she believed it published — it didn't), `news-thailand`
   was outside the fix scope.
4. Direct repair on the stragglers → **final audit: 6/6 news pass,
   37/40 overall** (remaining fails: `todo-list`, `idea-summary`,
   `cached-videos-report`, `vcast-failure-report`, `devin-job-report-fail`
   — mostly old/placeholder pages, deliberately left).

## Findings worth keeping

- **Pending-confirm can swallow a publish silently** — Ada thinks it
  landed; verify-after-publish should be mandatory, not optional
  (news-system now says so).
- **Ada invents structure per session** unless the spec is hard.
  "House style" as prose → soft compliance; as numbered MUSTs → she
  hit it on the first retry for 3/4 pages.
- **The audit is runnable cheaply** — `python3 scripts/ada/cms-audit.py
  [prefix]`, ~1s against mddb. Hookable into the scenario runner's
  ExecStopPost alongside lab-results.

## GitHub knowledge applied

- **errata-ai/vale** + `elastic/vale-rules` — the prose-linter model:
  our A-rules are a lighter, zero-dependency version (Vale itself is
  overkill for a 40-page CMS but is the upgrade path if the corpus
  grows).
- **GitHub Docs content linter** (markdownlint-based, custom rules on
  top) — the pattern we copied: stock rules *plus* collection-specific
  rules (N-rules), warning vs error severity.
- **lychee** (link checking) — not implemented yet; N3 checks link
  *presence*, a future pass could check link *liveness*.
- Microsoft code-with playbook / docs-as-code practice — "docs get the
  same gates as code" is the framing: audit on publish, not on review.

## Suggested next steps

1. Wire `cms-audit.py` into `ada-scenario-smoke`'s ExecStopPost (next to
   lab-results.py) so every suite run re-audits.
2. Add a `cms_audit` tool for Ada — she could self-check before asking
   you to confirm a publish.
3. Extend rules: image/link liveness, stale-date warnings on living
   pages (todo-list class), Thai-language pages pass fine today but a
   bilingual style rule may be worth pinning.

subject: fix-vcast-controls
title: Fix V-Cast & Controls Report

docs.contentMd: # Project Analysis: V-Cast Interface & Automation Failures **Target:** Devin coding session & Ada RCA study. ## Problem Statement Ongoing issues impact user confidence in the WeCast system and automated home controls. ## Known Failures 1. ### Visual Failures (V-Cast) - Screen 1 ownership logic prevents public access. - Content fails to render (broken image icon). 2. ### Automation Loop Failures - Unexpected TV plug activation triggers. ## Devin Action Plan - [x] Analyze `chaba` PWA receiver logic for broken image handling. — DONE 2026-09-28 - [ ] Review Home Assistant logbook for plug trigger source context. --- ## Repair Outcome — 2026-09-28 (Devin dispatch, chaba) **Broken image icon — root causes found & fixed:** 1. **Scheme**: the casted URL used `http://` on `:8123`, an HTTPS-only listener (plain HTTP → bare 400). On the HTTPS receiver page it was also mixed-content blocked. Fixed: receiver's `mediaUrl()` upgrades `http:`→`https:` media URLs. 2. **Missing file**: `/local/documents/A-68/...jpg` 404s even over HTTPS on both HA instances — that path was never published (A-68 pages live only in the idc01 doc-archive, behind `X-API-Key`, unusable as ``). 3. Image load failures now surface: HUD "image failed" + toast + `state:error` to the relay (previously a silent broken icon). **"Ada can't see the cast screen" — fixed:** - Snapshot path (`snap-request` → canvas → `/frame` → `vcast_snapshot`) was live but died on cross-origin `` (tainted canvas SecurityError). New relay endpoint `GET /img?url=` (tailnet/LAN allowlisted) lets the display refetch the URL server-side so pixels stay readable. Live-verified: casting the HA cam jpg to screen 2 now returns a real 424×240 JPEG frame. - Webpage (`nav`) casts verified working on screen 2; cross-origin iframes honestly report `uncapturable-iframe` + page URL — Ada can name the page, can't screenshot it (browser security, not a bug). **Deployed:** receiver `index.html` → live web mount; `server.mjs` → idc01 `input-bridge` (restarted). iPad (screen 1) picks up the new build on next connect. **Still open:** - Screen-1 owner-lock complaint (public screen treated as private) — separate ada-pi `cast-screens.json` ACL issue, not addressed here. - `/local/documents/` publishing decision (options logged in chaba job record `2026-09-28-vcast-image-mixed-content`). - TV plug automation trigger — not investigated.

# รายงานข้อมูลบริการรถยกฟรี เขตบางพลี

จากการตรวจสอบข้อมูลเบื้องต้นเกี่ยวกับบริการรถยกฟรีในเขตบางพลี จังหวัดสมุทรปราการ ในช่วงสถานการณ์น้ำท่วม มีข้อมูลที่สำคัญดังนี้:

## หน่วยงานให้บริการ
*   **บก.จร. (กองบังคับการตำรวจจราจร):** มีการประชาสัมพันธ์ให้บริการรถยกฟรีเพื่อช่วยเหลือประชาชนในการเคลื่อนย้ายรถยนต์ที่ประสบปัญหาน้ำท่วมขัง โดยเน้นการเคลื่อนย้ายหลังจากระดับน้ำลดลงแล้ว สามารถติดต่อสอบถามข้อมูลเพิ่มเติมได้ที่สายด่วนตำรวจจราจร 1197

## ข้อแนะนำเพิ่มเติม
*   ประชาชนที่ต้องการความช่วยเหลือควรเตรียมข้อมูลสถานที่ที่รถจอดอยู่และจุดหมายที่ต้องการให้พ่วงลากไปให้ชัดเจน
*   ควรรวบรวมข้อมูลหน่วยงานท้องถิ่นอื่นๆ เช่น เทศบาล หรือ อบต. ในพื้นที่บางพลี ที่อาจมีมาตรการช่วยเหลือเพิ่มเติมในช่วงวิกฤต

## หน่วยงานและช่องทางช่วยเหลือ
*   **สายด่วนเมืองพัทยา 1337:** ประชาชนสามารถติดต่อเพื่อขอความช่วยเหลือได้ตลอด 24 ชั่วโมง ซึ่งอาจรวมถึงการประสานงานเรื่องรถยกหรือการช่วยเหลือฉุกเฉินอื่นๆ
*   **บริการยกรถจากบริษัทประกันภัย:** ลูกค้าที่มีประกันภัยรถยนต์บางบริษัท (เช่น ชับบ์สามัคคีประกันภัย) ที่ประสบภัยน้ำท่วมในพื้นที่พัทยา อาจได้รับบริการยกรถฉุกเฉินฟรีตามเงื่อนไขกรมธรรม์ ควรติดต่อบริษัทประกันภัยของท่านโดยตรง

*   ตรวจสอบสิทธิ์การบริการรถยกฉุกเฉินจากกรมธรรม์ประกันภัยรถยนต์ของท่าน

docs.contentMd:
# Gemini Deep Research agent — capability assessment for Chaba/Ada

Date: 2026-09-27 · Sources: ai.google.dev deep-research & interactions docs, Google dev blog (Dec 2025), AI Studio forum

## What it is

Google's autonomous research agent, exposed to developers via the **Interactions API**
(the new GA single endpoint for models *and* agents — `generateContent` is now legacy).
Three agents:

| Agent id | Character | Est. cost/task |
|---|---|---|
| `deep-research-preview-04-2026` | fast, streamable, ~80 queries / ~250k in / ~60k out | ~$1–3 |
| `deep-research-max-preview-04-2026` | max comprehensiveness, ~160 queries / ~900k in / ~80k out | ~$3–7 |
| `deep-research-pro-preview-12-2025` | older Gemini 3.1 Pro version | — |

Powered by Gemini 3 Pro (SOTA on HLE + DeepSearchQA per Google; best-on-BrowseComp claim).
DeepSearchQA benchmark itself is open-sourced — usable for our own evals.

## API shape

- `interactions.create` with `agent=deep-research-*`, **`background=true` required**,
  `store=true` (retention: 55d paid / 1d free tier)
- Poll `interaction_id` until `completed`/`failed`, or `stream=true` for live steps
- `collaborative_planning=True` → agent returns a research *plan* first; a follow-up
  turn confirms/edits it before execution — **this maps 1:1 onto our confirm gates**
- `visualization="auto"` → generates charts/graphs inline in the report
- `tools` override: `google_search`, `external_data_mcp` (**it can call MCP servers**),
  `vertex_search`, File Upload/File Search for private docs (PDF/CSV)
- `service_tier="deferred"` → off-peak scheduling at **50% discount**
- Multiple concurrent background tasks allowed; label `is_deep_research` tracks cost

## Fit with our stack

### Ada voice tool — `ada_deep_research(topic, depth="standard"|"max")`

Natural fit for the dispatch/awaiting-user model:

1. Ada registers an MDDB job doc + starts interaction (`background`, `store`)
2. She answers immediately: "research queued, job X — I'll tell you when it lands"
3. A watcher (or poll-on-ask via `ada_deep_research_status`) detects completion
4. Report → `cms_publish_page` (via the new pending-confirm handshake for publish) +
   extract summary into memory bank + notify via `/api/notify`
5. Verification: CMS slug + interaction_id recorded on the job doc

The `collaborative_planning` option is the interesting one for voice: Ada reads the
plan aloud, Tony says "yes" or edits it, then she proceeds — exactly the
confirmation pattern we already want.

### Devin dispatch lanes

For project research (codebases, vendor comparisons): the dispatch JSONL ledger
already models long-running jobs — DR calls could be steps inside dispatched
sessions rather than separate plumbing.

### NotebookLM

DR is coming to NotebookLM natively — overlaps our NotebookLM summarization path;
watch for it replacing our digest step rather than duplicating it.

### Benchmarking

DeepSearchQA (open-source, Google) = a real benchmark corpus for complex web
research — could score Ada's `web_search`+synthesis path against DR directly.

## Constraints / watch-outs

- **Preview** — agents ids are dated previews; expect churn
- **Paid tier required** — our key is free tier now (web_search hit the 20/day
  grounding cap today); DR has no free quota worth using; also API keys must be
  restricted to generativelanguage.googleapis.com by June 2026 policy
- Runs take **minutes** — never inline on a live voice turn; always background
- Retention: free=1d (too short for our job ledger), paid=55d — we must snapshot
  the report to MDDB/CMS on completion regardless
- `store=true` means queries live on Google's side — no sensitive content in prompts

## Recommendation

Yes — adopt as Ada's `ada_deep_research` tool (standard tier default, `max` opt-in,
`deferred` when not urgent). It's the strongest missing piece between quick
`web_search` and full Devin dispatch: ~$1–3 for a cited multi-source report lands
squarely in our "control desk → job → notify → verify" architecture.

Prereqs: paid-tier API key (restricted scope), watcher for completion,
CMS publish on land. MVP ~half a day of plumbing.

subject: gemini-or-embedding-benchmark
title: Gemini & OR Embedding Benchmark

docs.contentMd:
# Gemini & OR Embedding Benchmark

Run 2026-09-28T04:33:00Z — 29 real `ada-cms-pages` docs, 768 dims.
Direct = `generativelanguage.googleapis.com` batchEmbedContents;
OR = `google/gemini-embedding-2` via OpenRouter (provider order: Google Vertex).

## Verdict

**Same vector space — OR is a drop-in mirror, safe to keep.**

| metric | direct Gemini | OpenRouter |
|---|---|---|
| latency p50 (10-doc batch) | 1.87s | 10.42s |
| latency worst batch | 2.01s | 10.58s |
| top-1 retrieval probes | 8/8 | 8/8 |

cosine(OR, direct) per doc — mean **1.0**, min **1.0**
(≈1.0 = identical space; same underlying model via Vertex).

## Cost

- OR billed tokens this run: **10711** ≈ **$0.00161**
  (at $0.15/Mtok — recheck OR pricing if it shifts).
- Projected: mddb daily writes ≈ tens of docs → **< $0.01/month** steady state;
  full-corpus re-embed ≈ a few cents one-shot.
- Comparison for *search* (not embeddings): Gemini paid grounding is
  ~$35/1K queries vs OR online/sonar routes ~$4-5/1K — the bigger
  argument for OR lives there; free-tier grounding stays at 20/day.

## Routes measured

- Primary (live): `gemini-ollama-proxy` → OR `google/gemini-embedding-2`
- Backup chain in proxy: OR → direct Gemini → local Ollama (`nomic-embed-text`)
- Hard-fail on OR error is deliberate — a different-space fallback would
  poison retrieval silently.

## Pros & cons of keeping OR in parallel

**Pros**
- Same vector space proven (cosine 1.000) — OR is a true mirror, no
  re-embed or collection migration ever needed.
- Off the Gemini free tier — embeddings no longer share the 20-req/day
  budget with grounded `web_search` and voice traffic.
- Predictable spend: measured **$0.0016/run**; steady state < $0.01/mo.
- Chain stays intact on OR outage: OR → (direct Gemini) → local Ollama.

**Cons**
- ~5× slower per batch — OR's Vertex route rejects array input, so every
  text is its own HTTP call (fine at our write volume). OR docs claim
  arrays are supported; the pin to provider `Google` is what breaks it.
- Silent spend creep — needs an occasional usage check, not alerts.
- OR AI-Studio provider route is broken (bogus API_KEY_INVALID) —
  pinned `order:[Google]` is the only working path.

## Improvements — applied vs open

**Applied this run**
- `GEMINI_API_KEY` restored in `mddb-gemini.env` + proxy now falls back
  to direct Gemini (same space, verified 1.000) on OR failure — Ollama
  still refused. Failover tested live: dead OR → direct Gemini → 768d.
- **int8 quantization set on all 40 collections** (`/v1/collection-config`).
  Applies to new writes + the in-memory index; existing float32 storage
  stays readable.

**Live observations during rollout**
- The cold-start vector-index rebuild took **>75 min at ~96% CPU** on
  ~11.6K vectors / 3.4GB DB — vector-search 503s the entire time
  (500+ failed calls; Ada semantic recall degraded during rebuilds).
  Cold-index rebuild is mddb's main operational weakness on this host.
- mddb flagged **18 collections with stale embedding provenance**
  (pre-gemini-embedding-2 space) and auto-re-embeds them through the
  proxy at ~2 calls/min — OR-sequential latency again.
- `POST /v1/vector-reindex` exists and is cheap to call.

**Open (ranked)**
1. **Scheduled `vector-reindex` for the 18 mismatched collections**
   (provenance cleanup — do during off-hours; costs pennies in OR).
2. **OR search tier for `web_search`** — paid Gemini grounding ≈ $35/1K
   vs OR sonar ≈ $5/1K; sits between free-20/day and DuckDuckGo.
3. **Chunk-size tuning** — mddb chunks at 1500 chars; each chunk is one
   sequential OR call → the 20s+ CMS write times. Larger chunks or
   proxy concurrency would cut it.
4. **Parallelize OR embed calls** (4-8 concurrent) in the proxy.
5. **Weekly `embed-bench` timer + OR usage readout.**
6. **Pin `dimensions:768` + model in SSOT.**
7. **OR Batch API** exists for embeddings (async, `provider.only` pin)
   — right tool for bulk re-embeds, not live writes.

## Sources

- mddb quantization: github.com/tradik/mddb → docs/QUANTIZATION.md
- mddb chunking/cache: docs/features + EMBEDDING_PROVIDERS.md
- OR embeddings spec: openrouter.ai/docs/api_reference/embeddings
- OR batch API: openrouter.ai/docs/batch-quickstart

# Gesture UI — ada_v2 complete implementation reference + YOLO assessment

Self-contained reference for rebuilding the ada_v2 hand-gesture UI. Everything
needed is in this file — no re-digging the archive required.

**Source of truth:** `tonezzz/ada` (archived) @ `af6d57223f72fce68b4d6f47bbfc6a75b7bc0085`
— `ada_v2/src/App.jsx` (gesture pipeline lines ~1068–1558, window manager
~339–413, ~510–536, ~1720–1876, render ~1919–2238), `ada_v2/package.json`,
`ada_v2/electron/main.js`, `ada_v2/src/index.css`,
`ada_v2/src/components/ToolsModule.jsx`, `ada_v2/backend/server.py`,
`ada_v2/hand_gesture_test.py`, `ada_v2/README.md`.

## Architecture at a glance

```
Webcam (getUserMedia 1920x1080)
  -> <video> (hidden, opacity-0)
  -> requestAnimationFrame(predictWebcam)        ~60fps when video on
       |- drawImage -> visible <canvas>          (CAM_01 tile, optional mirror)
       |- every 5th frame -> 640x360 canvas -> JPEG q0.6
       |     -> socket.emit('video_frame')       -> backend ada.py
       |     -> audio_loop.send_frame -> Gemini Live vision  (side-channel)
       '- if handTracking enabled && new video frame:
             detectForVideo -> 21 normalized landmarks
             -> fingertip cursor math -> pinch click / fist drag
             -> cyan skeleton drawn on canvas
```

All gesture interpretation is **browser-local**. The backend never saw gesture
events — the two paths (UI control vs AI vision) are fully independent.

## Dependencies & assets

- `@mediapipe/tasks-vision` `^0.10.22-rc.20250304` (npm dep in package.json)
- WASM runtime loaded from CDN: `FilesetResolver.forVisionTasks(
  "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@mediapipe/tasks-vision@0.10.0/wasm")` —
  **note the version skew** (CDN pinned @0.10.0 vs npm rc-20250304)
- Model: `/hand_landmarker.task` served from `public/` (~7.8 MB, Google's stock
  HandLandmarker full model)
- React 18, socket.io-client 4.7.4, electron 28, vite 5, lucide-react icons
- Electron: frameless 1920x1080 window (`frame: false`); top bar uses
  `WebkitAppRegion: 'drag'` (mouse-only OS window drag)

## Init sequence (runs once, guarded)

```js
const vision = await FilesetResolver.forVisionTasks(
    "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@mediapipe/tasks-vision@0.10.0/wasm");
handLandmarkerRef.current = await HandLandmarker.createFromOptions(vision, {
    baseOptions: { modelAssetPath: "/hand_landmarker.task", delegate: "GPU" },
    runningMode: "VIDEO",
    numHands: 1
});
```

- First `fetch('/hand_landmarker.task')` verifies the file exists (logs
  content-type/length) before creating the landmarker.
- Guarded by `handLandmarkerInitStartedRef` — init runs once on mount.
- Success posts "Hand Tracking Ready" to the chat; failure posts the error.

## Capture & loop

- `getUserMedia({ video: { width: ideal 1920, height: ideal 1080,
  aspectRatio: 16/9, deviceId? } })` -> `video.srcObject` -> `play()`.
- `predictWebcam` runs via `requestAnimationFrame` only while `isVideoOn`.
- Guards: bail if `video.readyState < 2` or `videoWidth/Height === 0`
  (prevents MediaPipe crash on cold start).
- Dedup: `video.currentTime !== lastVideoTimeRef` — skips inference on
  repeated frames.
- `detectForVideo(video, performance.now())` — needs monotonic ms timestamp.
- Hand tracking requires **video ON** (`isVideoOn`) **and** the Hand toggle
  (`isHandTrackingEnabled`, default OFF) — two separate switches.
- FPS counter displayed in top bar while video is on.

## Constants (verified from source)

| Constant | Value | Location |
|---|---|---|
| SENSITIVITY | `cursorSensitivity`, default **2.0** | settings slider; center 50% of camera maps to 100% of screen |
| LERP | **0.2** | `smoothedCursorPos += (target - smoothed) * 0.2` |
| SNAP_THRESHOLD | **50 px** | snap cursor to closest interactive element's center |
| UNSNAP_THRESHOLD | **100 px** | hysteresis — must pass 100px to release |
| PINCH threshold | **0.05** | normalized `dist(lm4, lm8)` |
| Drag deadzone | **0.5 px** | ignore wrist deltas below this |
| Transmission | **640x360, JPEG q0.6, every 5th frame** | `video_frame` socket event |
| numHands | **1** | second hand ignored |
| z base | **30** | `getZIndex = 30 + index in zIndexOrder` |

## Cursor math (per detected frame)

```js
rawX   = isCameraFlipped ? 1 - lm8.x : lm8.x;   // optional mirror
normX  = clamp((rawX - 0.5) * SENSITIVITY + 0.5, 0, 1);
normY  = clamp((lm8.y - 0.5) * SENSITIVITY + 0.5, 0, 1);   // y not flipped
target = normX * innerWidth, normY * innerHeight;
smoothed += (target - smoothed) * 0.2;          // lerp
finalX/finalY = smoothed (unless snapped);
```

**Snap hysteresis** — every frame scans
`document.querySelectorAll('button, input, select, .draggable')`, finds the
element whose **rect center** is nearest the cursor; if `dist < 50px` the
cursor locks to that center and the element gets a cyan glow
(`boxShadow 0 0 20px rgba(34,211,238,.6)`, `backgroundColor rgba(6,182,212,.2)`,
`borderColor cyan` — all **inline styles**; `.snap-highlight` class is added
but has no CSS). Releases only when cursor drifts `> 100px` from the snap
point.

## Pinch = click

- `dist(lm4, lm8) < 0.05` in normalized coordinates.
- **Rising edge only**: fires when `isPinchNow && !isPinching` — one click per
  pinch, hold doesn't repeat.
- Hit-test: `document.elementFromPoint(finalX, finalY)` then
  `el.closest('button, input, a, [role="button"]')` -> `.click()`; falls back
  to `el.click()` if no clickable ancestor.
- Consequence: pinch fires `.click()` but **not** mousedown/mouseup — elements
  driven by pointer-down handlers (drag handles, 3D canvas) don't respond to
  pinch. Dragging is fist-only.

## Fist = grab/drag window

```js
isFingerFolded(tip, mcp) = dist(tip, lm0_wrist) < dist(mcp, lm0_wrist)
isFist = folded(8,5) && folded(12,9) && folded(16,13) && folded(20,17)
         // index, middle, ring, pinky — thumb NOT checked
```

- On fist, if no drag active: hit-test cursor against `getBoundingClientRect()`
  of **`['cad','browser','kasa','printer']`** (popup window ids only) — cursor
  inside rect -> `activeDragElement = id`, `bringToFront(id)`, lock wrist pos.
- While fist held: compute **wrist (lm0)** screen pos with the same
  flip/sensitivity/clamp math (no lerp), delta vs last wrist pos; apply via
  `updateElementPosition(id, dx, dy)` when `|dx|>0.5 || |dy|>0.5`.
- Wrist (not fingertip) is used because the wrist doesn't move while forming
  the fist — fingertip would jump.
- Any non-fist frame releases (`activeDragElement = null`). The README's
  "open palm = release" is just the natural non-fist pose.
- `activeDragElement` also drives a green ring highlight on the grabbed window.

## Window manager contract (what gestures manipulate)

- `elementPositions` / `elementSizes` maps; **anchors differ per element**:
  - `chat`: top-center (`translate(-50%,0)`) — x=中心, y=top edge
  - `video`: top-left
  - everything else: center (`translate(-50%,-50%)`)
- `updateElementPosition` clamps to viewport bounds per anchor type
  (margin 0); `clampToViewport` (margin 10, topBar 60) is used for popup
  initial placement.
- `zIndexOrder` array; `getZIndex = 30 + index`; `bringToFront` moves id to
  end of array.
- `fixedElements = ['visualizer','chat','video','tools']` — never mouse-draggable.
- Mouse path: `handleMouseDown` requires `[data-drag-handle]` inside the
  target **unless** modular mode is on; blocks drag start on
  input/button/textarea/canvas. Fist-drag bypasses the handle requirement and
  works anywhere inside the four popup rects.
- Popup visibility toggles (`showCadWindow` etc.) come from socket events
  (`cad_data`, `browser_frame`, `request_print_window`) or ToolsModule buttons.

## DOM contract for a rebuild

- Hidden `<video>` (opacity-0) + visible `<canvas>` (80% opacity, optional
  `scaleX(-1)` mirror) inside a `w-80 aspect-video` tile labeled CAM_01,
  fixed bottom-right, id=`video`, z=20.
- Cursor: `fixed w-6 h-6 border-2 rounded-full pointer-events-none z-[100]`
  cyan ring + white center dot at `{left: cursorPos.x, top: cursorPos.y,
  transform: translate(-50%,-50%)}`; while pinching it gets
  `bg-cyan-400 scale-75` + stronger glow.
- Popup windows: `id={cad|browser|kasa|printer}`, positioned `absolute` at
  `elementPositions[id]` with `translate(-50%,-50%)`, `zIndex: getZIndex(id)`,
  `data-drag-handle` on their header bars for mouse drag.
- Hand toggle: `Hand` icon button in bottom `ToolsModule` toolbar — orange
  border/glow when enabled.
- Settings: `SettingsWindow` exposes `cursorSensitivity` slider +
  `isCameraFlipped` checkbox; **flip is persisted server-side** —
  backend `settings.json` key `camera_flipped`, pushed on `settings` socket
  event, applied via `setIsCameraFlipped`. (Sensitivity stays client-side.)

## Debug/visual aids

- `drawSkeleton`: cyan `HAND_CONNECTIONS` lines on the display canvas at
  native resolution.
- Logging: "Tracking loop running... Hand Found/No Hand" every 100 frames;
  "First hand detection!" once.
- Removed features still referenced: `cursorTrailRef`, `ripples` state,
  "Trail Logic"/"Ripple Effect" comments — dead code, don't port.

## Worked trace with real values

Cursor — index tip `lm8=(0.58, 0.30)`, screen 1920x1080, SENSITIVITY=2.0:

```
norm    = ((0.58-.5)*2+.5, (0.30-.5)*2+.5)  =  (0.66, 0.10)
target  = (1267, 108) px
lerp a=0.2:  f1 (253,22) -> f3 (618,53) -> f6 (935,80) -> ... -> (1267,108)
```

Snap — button center at (1264,198): dist 16px < 50 -> snaps & locks; drift
60px -> still glued (<=100); drift 120px -> unsnaps.

Pinch — `dist(lm4,lm8) = 0.0071 < 0.05` -> rising edge -> elementFromPoint ->
`.closest('button…').click()`.

Fist drag — all four tips closer to wrist than their MCPs -> cursor inside
`cad` rect -> grab; wrist `(0.55,0.62)->(0.58,0.60)` -> screen
`(1152,799)->(1267,756)` -> `updateElementPosition('cad', +115, -43)`.

## Edge cases & sharp edges

- `numHands: 1` — a second hand is silently ignored; `landmarks[0]` wins.
- Smoothed cursor starts at (0,0) — first frames lerp in from the corner;
  `lastWristPos` only locks on grab so drag doesn't jump.
- Snap scan is O(all interactive DOM nodes) every frame — fine at this scale,
  cache the list if porting to a bigger DOM.
- Fist hit-test uses the *smoothed/snapped* cursor position (finalX/finalY),
  not the wrist — so you aim with the fingertip, then clench.
- Thumb isn't part of the fist check — thumb-out fist still counts (and is
  required for the pinch detector to not conflict).
- `elementFromPoint` ignores `pointer-events-none` layers (cursor, noise,
  backdrop) — by design they can't be clicked or hit-tested.
- No scroll gesture, no right-click, no two-hand gestures, no dwell click.
- Browser/Safari: MediaPipe WASM works but needs a secure context and a user
  gesture for camera permission; iOS standalone-PWA mic issues are
  audio-specific but camera in PWA mode is its own gamble — test early.
- CDN WASM pin (@0.10.0) vs npm dep (0.10.22-rc) mismatch — vendor both for
  a rebuild (same pattern as vendored echarts `/local/` assets on HA hosts).

## Can YOLO do it?

Not directly — wrong-shaped output. YOLO detection gives bounding boxes +
class labels; the ada_v2 UX needs continuous 21-point landmark geometry
(fingertip pointer, sub-pixel pinch distance).

| Requirement | YOLO detection | YOLO-pose (keypoints) |
|---|---|---|
| Fingertip cursor (sub-pixel) | box centre only — too coarse | yes, if trained on hand-keypoint data |
| Pinch distance | not possible | yes |
| Fist/palm classification | yes (train classes, e.g. HaGRID) | derived from keypoints |

### Pros

- **Range/scale** — MediaPipe's palm detector drops hands beyond ~1-2 m; a
  YOLO trained on diverse data detects raised hands across a room (kiosk /
  wall tablet / TV surfaces).
- **Multi-hand/multi-person** tracking is more robust at distance.
- **Vocabulary growth** — new poses = retrain, no hand-tuned landmark
  heuristics (ada_v2's folded-finger check is brittle: ignores thumb, 2-D only).
- Easy server-side GPU inference via ultralytics.

### Cons

- Boxes != landmarks — gesture-class YOLO loses the pointer UX that made it
  feel like Minority Report.
- Custom data/training burden beyond HaGRID's vocabulary.
- Latency — browser WASM/WebGPU MediaPipe runs ~60 fps locally; a server
  round-trip adds 30-100 ms, felt immediately in a pointer UI.
- In-browser YOLO (TFJS/ONNX.js) is heavier than MediaPipe WASM.
- On Pi-class hardware (ada-pi): YOLO won't hit interactive rates on CPU;
  MediaPipe TFLite gets ~15-30 fps on Pi 5, or needs the Hailo AI HAT.

## Recommendation

1. **Keep MediaPipe** if reviving for ada-pi/PWA — or bump to `tasks-vision`
   WebGPU delegate, or `GestureRecognizer` (prebuilt classes: closed fist,
   open palm, point-up, thumbs up/down, victory). The feature was dropped for
   product reasons, not because it failed.
2. **Use YOLO where it wins** — a "hand raised" wake/attention gesture for
   room-scale surfaces. Hybrid: cheap YOLO watch -> activate the landmark
   pipeline only while a hand is up.
3. **Keep the UX layer** — lerp smoothing, snap-with-hysteresis, wrist-delta
   dragging are model-agnostic and made it usable. With YOLO classes add
   N-of-M temporal voting to stop label flicker.
4. **Pi hardware** — prefer inference in the PWA (browser already has webcam +
   GPU) over streaming frames to a GPU server; privacy and latency both better.

Net: YOLO can do gesture *recognition*; ada_v2 was a landmark-driven
*pointer system*. For that, MediaPipe (or any 21-keypoint model) is the
right primitive. YOLO is the answer only if the goal shifts to room-scale,
discrete, multi-person gestures.

## Rebuild checklist (ada-pi / PWA)

1. Vendor `hand_landmarker.task` + tasks-vision WASM locally (no CDN
   dependency; version-lock both to the same release).
2. Port `predictWebcam` verbatim: readyState guard -> canvas draw ->
   (optional) backend frame relay -> landmark pipeline.
3. Port cursor pipeline: flip -> sensitivity -> clamp -> lerp -> snap
   hysteresis -> setCursorPos; DOM cursor div; pinch/fist state machines;
   wrist-delta drag + bounds-by-anchor.
4. Recreate the DOM contract: popup ids, `data-drag-handle`, snap target
   selector, cursor div, Hand toggle button, settings (sensitivity + flip).
5. Decide persistence: ada_v2 kept `camera_flipped` in backend settings.json —
   in ada-pi pick the equivalent (HA input_boolean / PWA localStorage /
   backend settings file).
6. Improve on it: add dwell-click or N-of-M pinch voting, second-hand support
   (`numHands: 2`), `GestureRecognizer` for extra vocabulary, wake-word-style
   "hand up" gate to save GPU when idle.

## References

- Archive report: `docs/kb/archive/ada/ada-v2-platform.md`
- Manifest: `docs/archive/manifests/ada.yml`
- Source: `tonezzz/ada` @ `af6d572` — `ada_v2/src/App.jsx`,
  `ada_v2/src/components/{ToolsModule,SettingsWindow,...}.jsx`,
  `ada_v2/backend/server.py`, `ada_v2/electron/main.js`,
  `ada_v2/hand_gesture_test.py` (standalone OpenCV prototype — wider vocab
  incl. directional pointing + peace sign; scratch code, not shipped),
  `ada_v2/README.md`, `ada_v2/package.json`

title: GEV Screen Interaction Benchmark

docs.contentMd:
# GEV Screen Interaction Benchmark

`gev_screen1_interact` — Ada casts God's Eye View to vcast screen 1 and drives it incrementally. 6 turns: cast → what's showing → fly to Bangkok → zoom to globe → verify view state → stop cast.

## Result

| Run | Expectations | Functional outcome |
|-----|--------------|--------------------|
| run 1 | PASS (0 failed) | cast OK; every `gev_command` hit relay 404 — relay was never deployed |
| run 2 | PASS | `gev_command` called but errored `urllib not defined` — latent bug |
| run 3 | **PASS, functional** | cast → fly Bangkok → zoom globe → state query all delivered to live GEV client |

## Chain verified end-to-end

`Ada tool gev_command` → `POST /apps/gev-cmd/command` → gev-gemini bridge → `function_call` frame → browser clients → `runTool(runner)` executes on the casted page.

## Bugs found & fixed this run

1. **Caddy route missing** — repo `stacks/web/Caddyfile` had `/apps/gev-cmd/*` since commit `472f5a0a` but it was never deployed; running edge had no route (404). Also discovered `/etc/caddy/Caddyfile` had reverted to the stock 13-line template — the entire apps edge was one reload away from total loss; the real config (with gev-cmd) is now on disk and validated on caddy 2.6.2.
2. **Bridge image stale** — deployed `gev-gemini` predated the `/command` endpoint; image rebuilt + restarted.
3. **`gev_command` crash** — `urllib.request` used without import (the import lived inside a sibling method). ada-pi `54ab1c2`.
4. **Passive displays unreachable** — the bridge only counted voice-session sockets as clients; a casted page never registered. **New:** `?remote=1` ws = command-only client, no Gemini Live session (zero quota cost). GEV `index.html` now opens the remote socket at page parse (before Cesium init) and queues commands until the action runner is ready; `gevGeminiRealtime.js` registers a listener after `initGevVoiceCommands`. Live-verified: `/command/health` reports `{clients, remote}`, commands deliver to casted screens.

## Caveats

- **Fire-and-forget**: `/command` returns `delivered` count only — `get_current_view_state` reaches the client but its result doesn't come back through the relay. Verification loop is Ada → relay → screen state, not client-returned state.
- **Broadcast**: commands go to every connected GEV page — if two screens show GEV they both fly.
- **Display must be awake**: iPad suspended = page JS dead = no remote client (screen 1 stayed remote:0 while asleep; screen 2's desktop browser connected instantly).
- Commands on a still-initializing page queue until the action runner exists (early ws + 2s drain).

## Files

- scenario: `ada-pi/tests/scenarios-live/gev_screen1_interact.yaml` (tier: full)
- bridge: `chaba/stacks/tony-dell/gev-gemini/bridge.py` (`REMOTE` set + `?remote=1` path)
- frontend: `gods-eye-view` `index.html` early listener + `src/voice/gevGeminiRealtime.js` `initGevRemoteListener`
- edge: `chaba/stacks/web/Caddyfile` `/apps/gev-cmd/*` → `127.0.0.1:8790` (deployed via admin API + persisted to /etc/caddy)

## Next

- Tool-response return path: bridge waits briefly for remote client's `tool_response` so `get_current_view_state` can answer Ada.
- Screen-scoped commands: `screen=N` arg so broadcast doesn't hit every GEV page.
- iPad wake hook: vcast wakeLock exists but iOS still suspends background tabs.

## Screen narration (added same session)

`vcast_say(screen, text)` — Ada speaks short narration through the display's
own speechSynthesis ("Flying the map to Bangkok"). Implemented:
- vcast `speak` message handler (`stacks/web/public/apps/vcast/index.html`)
- tool `vcast_say` in ada-pi (owner-gated like cast_to_screen; in ACTUATING_TOOLS)
- tool description nudges Ada to announce screen actions inline.
iOS gates speech behind one user tap on the display's "audio" button; before
that the display shows the line as a toast and reports `speak-blocked`.
A sleeping iPad runs no page JS — narration requires the screen awake.

## Verification loop + screen targeting (added 2026-09-29)

The relay is no longer fire-and-forget:
- `POST /command` accepts `{name, args, screen?, wait?}` — `screen:N`
  targets only remotes whose hello announced that vcast screen (the
  same-origin iframe reads `parent.__vcastScreen`; also `?screen=N` url
  param); `wait:>0` collects `tool_response` frames and returns them in
  `responses` — `get_current_view_state` can now actually answer Ada.
- Remote clients announce `{type:'hello', screen}` on ws open (+6s/+20s
  retries — the vcast 'registered' msg races the socket open).
- `/command/health` reports `remote_screens` for debugging.
- Verified end-to-end: hello'd screen-3 python client received a
  screen-scoped command and its tool_response came back in the POST body.
- `gev_command` tool args: `screen` + `wait` (default 3s).

Operational note: displays must be RELOADED to pick up new vcast/GEV
page code — connected screens run whatever JS was loaded at boot
(`{"type":"reload"}` via /pub). Pages still initializing queue commands
until the action runner exists.

## Update — bundle corruption root-caused (2026-09-29)

The 'still initializing' mystery on real browsers was a **corrupted
bundle**: an early path-prefix sed ran unanchored on `dist/` and broke JS
syntax (`Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected token '/'` — no page JS ran at
all). Fixed: clean `npm run build` + quote-anchored `/api/`/`/models/`
prefixes only; `node --check` gates deploy now. Lesson: never regex-patch
minified bundles without a syntax check.

Also verified live:
- `uplink_confirm_flow` scenario — full PASS (confirm-gate before camera
  uplink, acknowledge running capture, clean stop, lease cleared)
- `cast_switch_flow` scenario — full PASS (confirm gates, source switch,
  busy-destination check, move, teardown). Notably strict consent:
  'screen 4 is free' was NOT accepted as camera permission — she asked
  again explicitly.

## gev_screen4_interact — FULL PASS (2026-09-29)

All 7 turns green on a live browser display: cast → confirm → describe →
fly Bangkok → zoom globe → verify (real view-state returned in
`responses` — Ada honestly reported ~18,000km near Austin, i.e. drifted
from Bangkok after zoom-out) → stop.

Two bugs this run flushed out:

1. **Cross-session speaker bleed** — a concurrent `simulate_speaker=KK`
   scenario flipped the shared runner's `current_speaker_ha_person` and
   MY session's cast/gev calls were denied as `person.kk` (owner-gated).
   Fixed: `execute()` takes `speaker=` via `_CALLER_SPEAKER` contextvar;
   explicit None (unidentified session) no longer falls back to the
   shared field. ada-pi `012dee9` + `e73a15f`, 58 unit tests green.
2. **Phantom assertion keys** — `result_contains_any` and quoted
   substrings (`"ok": true`) silently no-op'd/missed because tool results
   arrive JSON-escaped in events. Assertions rewritten escape-agnostic
   (`delivered`, `responses` bare; both `": 0` serializations blocked).

# God's Eye View — development jobs & Ada control plan

Platform: Cesium geospatial app (`gods-eye-view`), Gemini Live voice
bridge `gev-gemini` (:8789) + **command relay `/command` (:8790,
Caddy `/apps/gev-cmd/*`)** — drives connected GEV clients without voice.

## Verified live (2026-09-30)

- `POST /apps/gev-cmd/command {name,args,screen,pane,wait}` →
  `function_call` frame → client executes + returns `tool_response`
- Tested: `fly_to_location {query:"Bangkok"}` → camera at
  `lat 13.75 lon 100.49` in a headless GEV client
- Ada tool `gev_command(name,args,screen,pane,wait)` deployed on idc01
  (ada-ha-tony restarted 11:58) with full schema guidance
- Remote clients register `?remote=1` + `hello {screen,pane}` — casted
  GEV pages are individually targetable

## The flow that works today

1. `Ada, cast God's Eye View to screen N` → `cast_to_screen nav /apps/gev/`
2. `Ada, fly to Bangkok` → `gev_command fly_to_location {query}` → TV flies
3. `Ada, what's showing?` → `gev_command get_current_view_state` → answers

## Development jobs

| # | job | status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `POST /command` bridge relay | **done + deployed** (screen/pane targeting, response wait, coord normalization) |
| 2 | Ada `gev_command` tool + schema coaching | **done + deployed** |
| 3 | `gev_cast_control` scenario | written, queued behind scenario lock |
| 4 | vcast smoothness audit | relay 183ms pub; GEV renders in iframe; pending-claim UX gap open |
| 5 | CMS mobile UX | done (collapse/filter/highlight) |
| 6 | turn-stall watchdog | deployed 09-27 (`5c9095d`) — watch `live_stalled` |

## Open issues

- 2 stale `remote_pending` clients (unannounced screens) — likely test
  pages; idle cleanup in bridge would tidy them
- `vcast-screen-cast` scenario failing 2 runs (09-29) — investigate
- New-device claim flow still manual (`/claim`) — Ada can't self-assign
- Phantom write claim flagged 09-29 08:12 ("GEV is now on scr…" with no
  tool call) — the scenario's `no_failed_result` guard targets this

sluggishness investigation and the mddb corruption repair. Supersedes
the 06:46 fleet audit delta readings (omen load 98.69 pre-fix).

## Host status

| Host | Uptime | Load (1/5/15) | RAM used | Swap | Disk | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| tony-dell | 9d 6h | 8.5 / 12.7 / 12.1 | 10/14 GiB | 11/15 GiB | 82% | loaded — mddb rescan + desktop |

`/apps/yolo/api/*` earlier); weaviate-embedding :5000 active;
