docs.contentMd:
# Hosting Provider Assessment

_2026-09-27 · Devin · idc02 spec: Linux · ≥4 vCPU · ≥16GB RAM · ≥200GB SSD · daily backups · ~฿800/mo_

## Shortlist

| Provider / Plan | vCPU | RAM | SSD | Price/mo | DC | Meets spec? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **ReadyIDC VPS Business L2SS** | 4 | 16 GB | 300 GB | ฿800 (+7% VAT = ฿856) | Thailand | ✅ exact fit, at budget |
| **ReadyIDC VPS Game LG2SS+** | 8 | 18 GB | 150 GB | ฿800 | Thailand | ⚠️ storage short 50GB |
| ReadyIDC VPS Game LG3SS+ | 10 | 26 GB | 200 GB | ฿1,100 | Thailand | ✅ over budget 37% |
| **Contabo Cloud VPS 8** | 8 | 24 GB | 300 GB | €11.20 (~฿420, 24-mo price; €14 list) | **Singapore** | ✅ 2× spec at half price |
| Hetzner CPX41 | 8 | 16 GB | 240 GB NVMe | €23.29 (~฿880) + backups ~20% → ~฿1,050 | EU (SIN ~$39 = ฿1,370) | ✅ over budget ~30% |
| _reference: Siamdata (idc01)_ | — | — | — | ฿800-ish | Thailand | existing provider |

## Caveats that decide this

**Backups are not free anywhere.** None of the plans include daily
backups by default — Hetzner auto-backup is +20%, Contabo gives 3
snapshots (manual), ReadyIDC sells backup as a separate product line.
The spec's "daily backups included" effectively means *self-managed
backup* (our mddb-backup.timer pattern) regardless of provider — do
not pay extra for it unless it's a real managed service.

**Contabo's price is real but so is its reputation**: oversubscribed
hosts, CPU steal at peak hours, ticket support measured in days. For
mddb's sustained-index-rebuild workload — exactly what saturated idc01 —
Contabo is a coin flip. Fine for Chaba Lab; risky for production mddb.

**Latency**: Thai DC ~1–5ms from home; Singapore ~10–30ms; EU ~180ms.
For an Ada-facing node, SIN is acceptable, EU is not for interactive
paths (but fine for batch memory/index workloads).

**Provider-correlation risk still stands**: a second Siamdata box shares
the failure modes of idc01. ReadyIDC is a different Thai operator —
same latency, different blast radius. That argues *for* ReadyIDC over
a second Siamdata.

## Recommendation

1. **ReadyIDC VPS Business L2SS (฿856 incl. VAT)** — meets the spec
   *exactly* at budget, Thai DC (voice-adjacent latency), independent
   provider (no correlation with Siamdata), Thai support. The
   straightforward idc02 pick.
2. **Contabo Cloud VPS 8 (~฿420)** — if the node is for Lab/bench
   workloads where occasional CPU-steal hurts nothing. Twice the spec
   at half the price; just don't put production mddb there without a
   soak test.
3. **Hetzner CPX41 (~฿1,050 w/ backups)** — if quality/API maturity
   beats budget. Over budget but the cleanest ops story (Terraform,
   hourly billing, snapshot API). EU latency fine for batch, not for
   Ada-facing services.

**Public IP optional**: with the Cloudflare Tunnel edge (see
`chaba-edge-plan`), idc02 does not need its own public IPv4 — outbound
cloudflared covers "public" reach, and tailnet covers admin. That
removes the included-IP line from the decision and slightly favors
the cheapest spec-fit (Contabo) — though ReadyIDC remains the pick for
provider independence + Thai latency.

**Keep the original split either way**: mddb/indexing on idc02, Ada +
edge stays on idc01, tailnet-only, replicate-then-cutover.

subject: idc02-proposal
title: IDC02 Proposal

docs.contentMd:
# IDC02 Proposal — offload node for idc01

_2026-09-27 · Devin · measured on idc01 live (podman stats + service RSS)_

## Why

idc01 (Siamdata VPS, 2 vCPU / 12 GB / 100 GB) is saturated. Steady-state
usage is ~10 of 12 GB, and mddb alone consumes ~8.6 GB — enough that it
was in a cgroup-OOM crash loop today until its bounds were raised. Every
mddb restart wedges Ada's memory backend for minutes, and there is no
headroom left for Chaba Lab or any new workload.

## Current footprint (measured)

| Service | RSS (steady) | Role |
|---|---|---|
| mddb | **~8.6 GB** (rebuild spikes to ceiling) | memory/vector DB — the hog |
| ada-ha-tony | ~350 MB | production voice (latency-sensitive) |
| ada-ha-michael | ~110 MB | production voice |
| ada-pi-pwa | ~65 MB | PWA backend |
| open-notebook + surreal | ~340 MB | notebook stack |
| obsidian-vault | ~100 MB | vault sync target |
| ollama | ~10 MB idle / ~2 GB loaded | embed fallback (now unused — OR-only) + lab models |
| edge + proxy + panel + misc | <150 MB total | Caddy :80/:443 public edge, embed proxy |

## Proposed split

**idc01 keeps** (latency-critical / edge / small):
- Caddy public edge (:80/:443), input-bridge
- ada-ha-tony, ada-ha-michael, ada-pi-pwa (voice paths stay near the edge)
- obsidian-vault, gemini-ollama-proxy, mddb-panel

**idc02 gets** (memory-heavy / stateful / bursty):
- **mddb primary** (~9 GB working set, needs room to grow)
- open-notebook + surreal
- ollama (dev/lab models; embedding no longer needed — OR is primary)
- Chaba Lab when it deploys (was never viable on idc01 anyway)

tony-dell already runs an mddb binlog follower — with idc02 as primary
the replication topology stays intact and DR improves.

## Suggested spec (same provider — Siamdata)

**Recommended: 4 vCPU / 16 GB / 150 GB**

- 16 GB: mddb (9–10) + notebook (~0.4) + ollama (~2–4 loaded) + lab (~3)
  still leaves headroom; a 12 GB box would already be tight on day one.
- 4 vCPU: mddb's cold-start index build is CPU-bound — on 2 vCPU today it
  churned ~10 min per restart and starved all HTTP requests. 4 cores
  roughly halves that pain and gives the lab room to breathe.
- 150 GB: mddb.db + vectors grow; lab adds images/models.

**Cheaper floor: 2 vCPU / 16 GB / 100 GB** — works if the lab goes
elsewhere later; vCPU is the part that hurts least to start with on
Siamdata since upgrades are resize-reboots.

## Pros

- idc01 drops to ~2 GB used — ada voice + edge get a quiet, stable host;
  today's wedge-class incident disappears
- mddb gets real headroom + faster rebuilds; Ada memory ops stop being
  the failure-blast-radius of every restart
- Chaba Lab finally has a home without touching prod
- Same provider = same DC latency (~1 ms tailnet RTT) — mddb→ada calls
  add no meaningful delay

## Cons

- New monthly cost (est. Siamdata 4c/16G tier — check panel pricing)
- Second public IP = second thing to secure/patch; Caddy edge stays on
  idc01 so idc02 can be tailnet-only (recommended — don't expose it)
- Provider-correlated failure: one DC outage takes both (mitigated —
  tony-dell keeps an mddb replica)
- One-time migration: mddb.db + HNSW indexes move with ~30–60 min
  downtime, or replication-promote cutover (cleaner — seed replica on
  idc02, then promote)

## Suggestion

1. Order 4 vCPU / 16 GB / 150 GB on Siamdata, tailnet-only.
2. Bring up mddb as a replication follower first, verify, then promote —
  avoids a dump/restore window.
3. Move open-notebook + ollama after mddb is proven stable on idc02.
4. Keep Chaba Lab quota-capped there; re-evaluate idc01 sizing after a
  month — it may be worth downsizing to 8 GB once mddb is gone.

subject: jev-ai-assessment
title: Jev AI Assessment — measured v2

docs.contentMd:
# Jev AI Assessment — v2 (measured)

_2026-09-28 · Devin · reconciles pilot + model bench + Ada/GEV/Weaviate plan_

## Verdict

Jev (decision-only models, `/v1/systemone`) earns a permanent seat in the
stack — as an **async judgment tier now**, a **hot-path gate tier later**.
Local open-jev is live on tony-omen `:8777` (gemma-3-4b-it, CPU).

## Measured (3-backend bench, 18 real Ada decisions)

| backend | accuracy | latency | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| open-jev gemma-3-4b (CPU) | **83%** | 11.9s | calibrated — honest 0.559 on ambiguous turns |
| open-jev gemma-3-1b | 56% | 2.6s | too weak — under-scores plain "yes" |
| Gemini 2.5 Flash via OpenRouter | 57% | 1.4s | **uncalibrated — worse than the regex; do NOT gate through chat models** |

The `/v1/systemone` wire contract is backend-portable; the value is
logit-read scores. Chat models self-report confidence — structurally
fake calibration.

## Decision tier ladder

```
Tier 0  RULES      μs         gates, budgets, whitelists
Tier 1a JEV-async  ~12s CPU   post-turn audit, scenario judging, CMS classification  ← NOW
Tier 1b JEV-hot    ~400ms     confirm-gate, tool routing, ambient filtering          ← needs quant/NanoJev/hosted
Tier 2  GEMINI     streams    reasoning, generation, correction duty
```

Rule: cheapest tier that can hold the decision reliably. Each Jev win
removes a Gemini round-trip AND a failure surface.

## Ada↔GEV topology (as built)

- **Ada → `gev_command`** → `POST /command` (:8790) → function_call →
  GEV browsers — inherits Ada's full enforcement stack.
- **GEV's own Gemini session** in the bridge → 28 tools, **no confirm
  gate/budget/ops events** — the unguarded actuation path.
- Fix: thin guard shim in `gev-gemini/bridge.py` (budget + confirm +
  ops events) before any shared-gateway refactor.

## Data plane (unchanged)

MDDB canonical for Ada banks (Gemini-768 space, OR-Vertex primary —
cosine 1.000 proven). Weaviate stays dev-KB hybrid search (MiniLM
space). Different vector spaces — never merge; scope grows only via
retrieval bench data.

## Sequence

1. jev-bench committed → `tests/bench/jev-bench.py` emits
   `kind: benchmark` docs → auto-report catches regressions
2. Async Jev first: post-turn confirm audit, scenario judging
3. gev bridge guard shim (budget + confirm + ops events)
4. Retrieval bench: MDDB-vs-Weaviate recall@5 + latency
5. Hot-path Jev decision with bench numbers: 4-bit quant on the 1650 /
   NanoJev-0.6B trained on our transcripts / hosted API

Full reasoning + ecosystem scan: kb-system
`jev-weaviate-architecture-assessment.md`.

# LINE Bot — outbound messaging project

Date: 2026-09-27 · consolidated for review

## What it is

Outbound LINE notifications — system → Tony (alerts, dispatches,
Ada-initiated messages). Distinct from **Yomi**, which *reads* LINE.

## Current state — gaps found 2026-09-27

- **No Ada tool exists to send LINE messages.** When Tony asked
  "send me a test message" (session 7975f60c71, ~11:15), Ada could only
  call `ada_memory_search` + `web_search` — she guessed and checked the
  LINE Bot *API status page* instead of sending. Nothing arrived.
- **No LINE Messaging-API channel token** found in secrets on idc01 or
  on this box — the classic "bot account + push API" path isn't wired.
- The only working send path is **Yomi's `send_message`** (E2EE send as
  Tony's own account to any chatId) — but that MCP server is not
  reachable from Ada's tool layer, and its session is revoked (see the
  Line Yomi page).

## Proposed path

1. Re-login Yomi (passwordless secondary-device flow on Tony's phone —
   `login` → PIN → `login_complete`; ~3 min window).
2. Expose a thin `line_send` Ada tool: `tool_runner` → yomi
   `send_message` (a small HTTP shim or a local CLI wrapper on idc01).
   Tools needed: `line_send(to, text)` + `line_chats()` for resolving
   recipients. Gate under `ADA_DEV_TOOLS`-style confirmed writes —
   outbound messages are consequential.
3. Until wired, Ada's honest answer is: "LINE send is offline — needs
   Tony's re-login." (Memory note `yomi-vs-line-bot` updated with this.)

## Pending

- [ ] Tony: LINE re-login on the phone (allow-from-other-devices + PIN)
- [ ] Devin: `line_send`/`line_chats` Ada tools via yomi
- [ ] Optional later: dedicated LINE Messaging-API bot channel (cleaner

# Yomi — LINE archive, search & send

Date: 2026-09-27 · consolidated for review

## What it is

LINE message **archive + search + E2EE send** running as the `yomi` MCP
server. Pulls chats via LINE's secondary-device protocol, decrypts E2EE,
summarizes into MDDB, exposes MCP tools. See chaba-docs
`architecture/yomi-architecture-separation.md` (fetch vs process split).

## Capabilities (MCP tools)

- `list_conversations`, `get_chat_messages`, `get_unread_digest`,
  `get_insight` — read/search
- `get_message_media` — decrypted images/video/audio
- **`send_message`** — real E2EE outbound to any chatId (already works —
  the only live LINE-send path in the stack)
- `login`/`login_complete` — passwordless re-auth on Tony's phone

## Status — OFFLINE as of 2026-09-27

`list_conversations` → `Access token refresh required`. Session revoked
(typically when LINE on the phone re-logs elsewhere). Digest→MDDB and
any send path are both blocked until re-login.

**Re-login flow** (Tony, ~3 min): enable 允許自其他裝置登入 on the phone
→ `login` (phone/region) → LINE shows a PIN → `login_complete`
immediately → device approved on the phone.

## Indexed data

- ~489 daily digests in MDDB (`ada-ha-bank-yomi` family)
- Searchable via `ada_memory_search` (bank='yomi') and the MCP tools
- Privacy default: capture-all; excluded chats via `exclude_chats`

## Confusion note for Ada

Yomi ≠ LINE bot. Yomi **reads** (and can send as Tony's account); the
"LINE bot" concept is outbound notifications — currently unbuilt on the
Ada side. See `line-bot` report.

docs.contentMd:
# mddb follower migration: tony-dell → idc02

**Status: benchmarked — idc02 wins by ~800× on the metric that hurt us.
Recommendation: migrate as second follower, soak, then cutover.**

## Latest

- **2026-10-01** — idc01 nightly backup fixed (data-dir ownership →
  `podman cp`; verify needed `-p` port mapping + a 20-min window for the
  `NoFreelistSync` rescan). First **verified** backup of the clean
  post-rebuild DB: `mddb-filecopy-mddb-20261001-0649.db` opens healthy.
- **2026-10-01** — landing-page format piloted on this page: status +
  `## Latest` on top, section links, benchmark chart embedded.
- **2026-09-30** — benchmark done: cold-open 5–16 s on idc02 vs ~3.5 h
  on dell ([details](#why-migrate)); migration procedure below.

Sections: [Why migrate](#why-migrate) ·
[Procedure](#migration-procedure-standard-backup-seed-path) ·
[Risks](#risks--watch-outs) · [CMS pages audit](#cms-pages-audit--where-old-reports-stand)

## Why migrate

![Cold-open benchmark: dell HDD ~3.5h vs idc02 5–16s](https://tony-dell.taila0626a.ts.net/apps/reports/mddb-coldopen-2026-09-30.png)

| | tony-dell (current) | idc02 (target) |
|---|---|---|
| Disk | 465 GB HDD, contended (r_await ~90 ms) | VPS SSD-backed, idle |
| RAM | 15 GiB shared w/ desktop | 15 GiB, nearly free |
| Cold-open of clean 1.54 GB DB | **~3.5 h** (measured today) | **5–16 s** (measured today) |
| Role | desktop/workstation | dedicated offload |

The `NoFreelistSync` open-time rescan is the killer on dell — every
restart is a multi-hour IO-bound B-tree walk. On idc02 the same file
opened in **16 s warm / 5 s after `drop_caches`** (benchmark:
`tradik/mddb:2.15.3`, throwaway container `mddb-bench`, now removed).

## Migration procedure (standard backup-seed path)

1. **Stage idc02**: copy `~/.config/containers/systemd/mddb.container`
   from dell; set `node_id`/`followerID` to `idc02`, bind tailnet
   `100.123.163.11:11023/11024`; copy the `MDDB_REPLICATION_SECRET`
   podman secret out-of-band (never via repo).
2. **Seed**: `POST /v1/backup` on the leader (now clean — backup works
   again post-rebuild) → scp file to idc02 → `podman unshare chown
   1000:1000` inside the mount.
3. **Start + verify**: `systemctl --user start mddb` on idc02 — expect
   bind in seconds, `Replication connected` in logs, counts converging.
   Dell follower keeps running meanwhile (two followers can coexist —
   followerID differs).
4. **Repoint the one consumer**: Caddy `/api/mddb/*` upstream
   `100.68.142.13:11023` → `100.123.163.11:11023`. All other clients
   hit the leader directly — nothing else to move.
5. **Cutover + standby**: after a soak period, stop dell's unit and
   keep it stopped-but-seeded as the emergency standby (dell stays in
   the SSOT as `role: standby`).
6. **SSOT**: update `ssot.services.yml` follower block (host, IP, note),
   `ssot.audit.hosts.yml` (move `mddb.service` expectation tony-dell →
   idc02 — idc02 entry already exists), `ssot.host-roles.yml`.

## Risks / watch-outs

- **Replication gap today**: the dell follower is still replaying the
  reindex backlog; a fresh idc02 seed inherits whatever LSN the backup
  carries and catches up by streaming — verify with a doc-count compare
  before cutover.
- **Secrets**: replication secret copy is the only manual step; use
  `podman secret` on idc02, don't paste it anywhere.
- **idc02 capacity**: 15 GiB RAM is plenty for a 1.5 GB DB; disk 290 GB.
- **Rollback**: leave dell's follower intact until idc02 soaks clean.

## CMS pages audit — where old reports stand

`scripts/ada/cms-audit.py` live run (127 pages): **107 pass · 20 fail ·
47 warnings**.

Failure clusters (fix the generator once → many pages comply):

- **8 `*-digest` pages** — `R1:no-sources` + `R2:no-provenance-footer` +
  `A2:kind!=page`. The digest writer doesn't emit the report standard's
  meta/footer. One fix in the generator clears ~40% of failures.
- **6 pages missing `kind=page` meta** (ada-decision-flow, bench-orch,
  chaba-compound-ai-system, multi-model-orchestration, ops-health,
  vps-secperf-baseline) — mechanical `cms-normalize-meta.py` pass.
- **`chaba-edge-plan` — A6 secret-ish** — inspect before anything else;
  a possible secret pattern in page content.
- **Thin/scratch**: `bench-ping`, `devin-job-report-fail` (empty),
  `document-audit-policy`, `transcript-audit-2026-09-28` (stub markers).
- **`camera-sources-2026-09-30`** — created today with zero meta.
- **34 S1 schema warnings** (missing memory-schema fields — mostly
  `wall-*` pages), **5 C1 duplicate pairs** (my-words~my-words-kk,
  transcript-audit pair, wall-vms-* overlaps) — consolidation candidates.

docs.contentMd:
# MDDB ops split — migration plan

Goal: move high-volume append-only telemetry off the authoritative
leader (idc01) so the semantic index stays small and fast. Vector
index cold start is currently ~2h on 21k docs; ~80% of that is
telemetry that never needs embeddings.

## Target topology

```
idc01  mddb leader :11023 (wr)          — banks, CMS, SSOT, KB, reports
       semantic embeddings ON (ollama gemini-embedding-2)
       ~4k docs — index load minutes, not hours

idc02  mddb-ops    :11025 (wr)          — telemetry, append-only
       embeddings OFF entirely (no provider env)
       expendable — rebuildable from writers, no backup SLA

idc02  mddb-lab    :11024 (ro snapshot) — nightly file-copy of leader

tony-dell          follower (ro)        — geo DR of leader only
```

## Collection assignment

**Move to mddb-ops** (~17.2k docs — 80% of today's index):

| collection | docs | writers |
|---|---|---|
| host-logs | 11,110 | log-shipper.py |
| ada-ha-events-* | 3,667 | event_recorder, realtime_provider |
| ada-ha-scenario-reports | 940 | scenario-report/benchmark/prune |
| ada-ha-snapshots-* | 540 | tool_runner (cam/action snaps) |
| ada-ha-recall-summary-* | 266 | conversation_memory, summary_rollups |
| ada-ha-actions-* | 166 | tool_runner action log |
| yomi-digest | 487 | digest-to-mddb.mjs |

**Keep on leader** (~4.1k docs — semantic content):

- `ada-ha-bank-*` (all memory banks — tony, kk, handoff, general, …)
- `ada-cms-pages`, `ada-cms-automation`
- `ada-ha-reports-*`, `ada-ha-device-safety/confidence-*`
- `infrastructure-ssot`, `kb-*`, `chaba-docs`, `chaba-archive`,
  `chaba-architecture`, `devin-kb`

Scenario reports ride with ops — they're run output, not user memory.
(If we want them searchable by meaning later, promote to leader.)

## Code changes

**ada-pi `backend/mddb_client.py`** — add a second client:

```python
MDDB_OPS_URL = os.environ.get("MDDB_OPS_URL") or MDDB_BASE_URL

OPS_COLLECTIONS = (
    "host-logs", "ada-ha-events-", "ada-ha-actions-",
    "ada-ha-snapshots-", "ada-ha-recall-summary-",
    "ada-ha-scenario-reports", "yomi-digest",
)

def for_collection(name: str) -> MddbClient:
    """Route by collection prefix — ops streams go to mddb-ops,
    everything else to the leader. Prefix match, not exact, so
    per-instance names (ada-ha-events-tony) just work."""
    if any(name.startswith(p) for p in OPS_COLLECTIONS):
        return ops_client()
    return default_client()
```

Every write site swaps `mddb()` for `for_collection(name)` — the
routing lives in one place; writers keep their collection names.

**Writer sites to touch** (each is a 1-line client swap):

- `backend/event_recorder.py` — `ada-ha-events-{instance}`
- `backend/realtime_provider.py` — `_ops_collection` writes
- `backend/tool_runner.py` — snapshots + actions collections
- `backend/conversation_memory.py` — recall-summary writes
- `backend/summary_rollups.py` — recall-summary rollups
- `chaba/scripts/ada/log-shipper.py` — host-logs (`MDDB_OPS_URL` env)
- `chaba/scripts/ada/ops-report.py` — reads host-logs for reports
- `scripts/digest-to-mddb.mjs` — yomi-digest
- `scripts/scenario-*.py` — scenario reports

**Reads that cross the boundary**: `ops-report.py` and any Ada tool
that reads events/actions (recall paths) must query `ops_client` for
ops collections. `for_collection` handles this symmetrically.

## mddb-ops instance (idc02)

Quadlet `mddb-ops.container`, port **11025** tailnet-only:

```
MDDB_MODE=wr
MDDB_REPLICATION_ROLE=standalone
# NO MDDB_EMBEDDING_* — provider unset means no vector index at all
MDDB_DATA_DIR=/var/lib/mddb-ops
```

No embedding provider → no index load → cold start in seconds.
Retention: TTL or a nightly prune job (host-logs older than 30d are
dead weight — pick the policy when we see growth).

## Migration steps

1. **Stand up mddb-ops** on idc02 (quadlet, no embeddings, tailnet :11025)
2. **Ship the client change** to ada-pi staging on idc02 — run
   `camera_describe` + a scenario against ada-lab; verify ops writes
   land on 11025 and bank reads still hit the leader
3. **Set `MDDB_OPS_URL=http://100.123.163.11:11025/v1`** in ada-ha env
   on idc01; redeploy via deploy-ada.sh
4. **Verify split**: writes to `ada-ha-events-tony` appear on idc02,
   `ada-ha-bank-*` on idc01; CMS unaffected
5. **Historical data** — leave existing ops collections on the leader
   initially (read-only residue). Optional: bulk-copy to ops then
   delete from leader in a separate step *after* writers are confirmed
   repointed — never delete first
6. **Vector index benefit**: once the leader's ops collections are
   deleted and it restarts, index load drops from ~2h to minutes
   (~4k semantic docs)

## Rollback

Unset `MDDB_OPS_URL` → every client falls back to the leader. No data
loss either direction; ops collections on idc02 are re-pullable from
the writers' sources (logs, events regenerate).

## What this buys

- idc01 index: 21k docs → ~4k, cold start ~2h → minutes
- Restart/reindex no longer a weekly outage risk
- mddb-ops can be wiped/rebuilt freely — telemetry, not memory
- Clear growth story: banks/CMS scale on the leader, telemetry scales
  on the expendable node

## Explicit non-goals

- idc01 stays leader — idc02 is lab + expendable ops, never authoritative
- No live replication between leader and ops (the OOM lesson)
- tony-dell follows only the leader — it doesn't need telemetry

title: mddb ops/split structure

docs.contentMd:
# mddb ops/split structure — 2026-10-02

**Decision: split mddb into leader + ops instances — Ada memory on
idc01, high-volume operational streams on idc02.**

## Why
The leader vector index rebuilds in ~2h on restart (21k docs). Half the
db is `host-logs` (11k) + event streams that are written constantly and
never vector-searched. Splitting them off makes the leader's index
rebuild in minutes and keeps the follower/DR copy lean.

## Structure
- **idc01 `mddb` :11023 (wr)** — banks, cms-pages, ssot, kb. The memory
  brain. ~5k docs, embedded.
- **idc02 `mddb-ops` :11025 (wr)** — host-logs, ada-ha-events-*,
  snapshots, recall-summary, actions, yomi-digest. `EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=
  none`; timestamped append-logs, keyword/meta search only.
- **idc02 `mddb-lab` :11024 (wr)** — nightly snapshot replica (existing).
- **tony-dell `mddb` (ro follower)** — replicates the LEADER only; ops
  noise never leaves idc02.

## Ada-side mechanism
One new env `MDDB_OPS_URL` (defaults to `MDDB_BASE_URL` — zero-change
deploy). A second `MddbClient` for ops collections; three call-sites
swap: `event_recorder` (ada-ha-events-*), `tool_runner` snapshots,
`conversation_memory`/`summary_rollups` recall-summary.

## Rules
1. Reads always hit the leader — ops collections are write-only.
2. Ops stream has no embedding — it's telemetry, not memory.
3. Follower tracks leader only — DR copy stays ~2.7G and shrinking.

## Follow-ups
- mddb-ops unit spec on idc02
- repoint writers (log-shipper `LOG_COLLECTION`, digest-to-mddb, probes)
- rebuild leader db via the 2026-09-30 runbook to physically shrink the
  file (bbolt doesn't release pages on delete)

docs.contentMd:
# Memory audit — KK misses, confident-gate incident, scenario assessment

Date: 2026-09-27 · incidents from live sessions + scenario runs

## Why Ada misses KK's memory — root cause chain

1. **Extraction lands in Tony's bank.** `speaker_identity` routes
   extracts to `personal-kk` only when speaker-ID resolves KK. Since
   2026-09-24 her sessions resolve to admin/Tony (mis-identified or
   unidentified → caller identity) → extracts land in
   `ada-ha-bank-personal-tony` (daily) while `personal-kk` froze at
   9-24. Then ACL (`person.kk` allow-list) blocks her from reading where
   her own data went.
2. **Wiped docs poisoned ranking** (fixed today `6745f31`): 3 of 10
   personal-kk docs had contentMd='' yet scored ~0.6 — they crowded the
   real hits out. Now: empty hits skipped, meta-only writes refuse when
   the read fails, dead docs retracted.
3. **Profile contamination** (`Timmy`, `NewSpeaker`) still muddies
   speaker-ID → feeds issue 1. Awaiting approval to remove + re-enroll.

Evidence: KK=กุ้ง=Sok Hiang merge note + "CR-V ขาว 5ขว 6249" +
Underworld/EDM + แก้วตา assistant-name all found inside
`ada-ha-bank-personal-tony` extracts 2026-09-26.

## The confident-gate incident — explained

Ada refused "dig deeper" (`recall_gate_override` reproduces it):
server-side `_recall_gated` refuses `ada_session_recall` for 60s after a
confident memory_search hit (score≥0.6). Rationale is sound — saves the
~20s NotebookLM round-trip — but the gate trusted hits whose bodies
were empty, and gave the user no override path.

**Balance now in place** (`d96cf88`):
- Gate only counts confident *content-bearing* hits (empty hits gone)
- `force=true` escapes the gate on explicit push ("dig deeper", "check
  again", "you missed it") — verified live: turn 2 reached recall
- Instruction names the override so she doesn't second-guess it

## References lifecycle — tested (`report_references_lifecycle`, PASS)

Create-with-references → publish → "remove references" → update →
re-read. Workflow valid; found and fixed a real regex bug along the way:
`confirmed?` never matched bare "confirm" (`10f0211`).

## Scenario structure — assessment

**Pros**
- Declarative YAML, one file per capability — easy to add
- `calls_any`/`no_calls_except`/`response_nonempty`/`reconnect` cover
  the real axes; `cleanup.mddb_delete` keeps banks clean
- Live traces caught 4 real bugs today (regex, sticky identity, dead
  stream, wiped docs)

**Cons**
- English expectations vs Thai answers — can't assert on response
  content (`response_contains` only works same-language)
- No speaker-ID injection — can't simulate "talking as KK" so
  per-person memory routing is untestable end-to-end
- `calls_any` silently passes if the runner's tool-name list drifts
  from reality (add a `known_tools` check against the declaration set)
- No per-turn assertions on *args* (e.g. `provider=duckduckgo` asserted
  only via journal grep, not the scenario)

**Suggested improvements**
- `response_regex` + `response_lang` assertions (transcript is captured
  already)
- `speaker:` per-session field → `?speaker_override=person.kk` query
  param honored by the session path, so KK-scoped flows are testable
- A `--dry-run known_tools` lint: every `calls_any` name must exist in
  the declared tool set
- Coverage matrix job (running on mn01) → auto-flag uncovered tools

# Recall latency ladder (L0–L3)

Ada's recall mirrors human memory: fresh items are said immediately; distant ones cost a lookup.

| Level | What | Cost | Fade |
|---|---|---|---|
| **L0 hot** | One-line headlines from new reports (meta.summary, ≤160 chars), injected at session start | instant — Ada says it without querying | announced once (announced_at stamp) or expires at 72h; then cools to L2 |
| **L1 recent** | Domain digest pages (`<domain>-digest`, report-distill) | 1 tool call (~0.5s) | superseded by next distill run; `fresh_for` marks staleness |
| **L2 warm** | Full CMS pages + bank docs | `ada_memory_search` ~1–3 s | status: archived / valid_until expiry |
| **L3 far** | NotebookLM deep tier + recall-summary banks | ~20 s background fetch | permanent — the "let me look that up" cost is intended |

## Rules
- L0 shows only real pages/reports — indexes and digests (report_role=digest|index, *-digest keys) never enter it; aggregates are navigation, not news.
- A headline is told once. Re-announce requires a new updated doc.
- Detail is lazy: the headline answers "what's new"; `cms_get_page` fetches the body only when asked.
- Devin reads the same CMS pages via MDDB search (operational state); repo/SSOT remains canonical truth — CMS pages are generated outputs that link back via meta.sources/links (see ssot.reports.yml `placement`).

## Knobs
`ADA_HEADLINE_MAX_AGE_H` (72) · `ADA_HEADLINE_MAX` (5) · `ADA_CMS_COLLECTION`

*Canonical source: chaba `docs/ssot/apps/ssot.apps.ada-memory.yml` → "Recall latency ladder" + `docs/ssot/infrastructure/ssot.reports.yml` → `placement`.*

# Devin Handoff Spec: Memory YAML Proposal

## Overview
This spec details the proposed structure for the `memory.yml` file, intended to store curated, durable facts for Ada's context.

## Proposed Structure
The YAML file should contain a list of structured fact objects.

### Required Fields
- `subject`: Slug-style identifier (e.g., `gate-remote`).
- `attribute`: Specific property of the subject (e.g., `brand`).
- `text`: The factual statement itself.

### Optional Fields
- `kind`: Defaults to `fact`. Other kinds could be `preference`, `person`.
- `prime`: Boolean, whether to include this fact in every session's bootstrap context.

## Example
```yaml
- subject: gate-remote
  attribute: protocol
  text: The gate remote uses an encrypted 433MHz rolling code.
  kind: fact
  prime: true
```

docs.contentMd:
# Analysis: Migrating Home Assistant and Ada Public URLs to idc01

This document outlines the pros and cons of moving the public entry points for Home Assistant and Ada from their current location on `mn01` to `idc01` (Siamdata VPS, tailnet node 100.74.146.0).

## Current Architecture
- Ada is public via `mn01` Tailscale Funnel.
- `tony-ha` is tailnet-only.
- `idc01` has tailscale serve on tailnet only, no funnel enabled.

## Pros

*   **Consolidation:** Moves public-facing component to a dedicated, public-facing VPS (`idc01` has a static public IP), potentially simplifying network management and decoupling public access from internal node `mn01`.
*   **Availability:** VPS generally has higher availability and more reliable direct network access than a residential connection subject to ISP whims.

## Cons

*   **Increased Latency:** Moving the entry point to `idc01` introduces an additional network hop for the voice websocket (User -> `idc01` -> tailnet to `mn01`). This likely increases voice response latency.
*   **Origin Change:** A new public URL means the browser context (origin) changes. This will **invalidate device-bound API keys** stored in browser `localStorage` and will require re-installation of installed PWAs.
*   **Migration Effort:** Requires configuring `tailscale serve`/`funnel` on `idc01`, updating DNS, updating Ada's configuration, and migrating user data across all devices.
*   **Security Exposure:** Enabling public ingress on `idc01` presents fresh attack surface to the internet.

## Recommendation

Due to the increased voice latency and the breaking changes for users (PWA reinstall, API key invalidation), **migration is not recommended** at this time unless direct `mn01` ingress becomes untenable, or if `idc01` provides tangible performance gains outweighing the extra hop. The current configuration on `mn01` via Tailscale Funnel appears optimal for balancing security, latency, and operational simplicity.

subject: monitoring-proposal
title: Monitoring Proposal

docs.contentMd:
# Monitoring Proposal — multi-host dashboard

_2026-09-27 · Devin · researched: github candidates vs our actual estate_

## Requirement

One dashboard showing load/health across all hosts and services —
idc01, tony-dell, tony-omen, mn01 (+ michael-ha where possible).
Constraints that shape the answer: everything is **rootless podman
quadlets** (no docker), hosts are **tailnet-only**, and idc01 is a
12 GB VPS that can't afford a heavy monitoring stack on top of mddb.

## Candidates evaluated

### 1. Beszel — github.com/henrygd/beszel ⭐ recommended

Hub + agent model: lightweight Go hub (PocketBase, ~50 MB) + tiny agent
per host. Single pane: CPU/mem/disk/net per host + per-container stats.

- **Podman: works** — agent reads podman socket via `DOCKER_HOST=
  unix:///run/user/1000/podman/podman.sock` (Docker-compat API).
- Best run as a **systemd binary agent** (not container): rootless
  agents can't see systemd services/temps/GPU otherwise.
- Alerts (threshold → email/webhook), Docker **and** podman container
  lists with cpu/mem.
- Known quirks: container CPU% inflated ~3.5× for containers inside
  pods (issue #1953); `-infra` pod containers can't be excluded yet;
  container health doesn't show for podman (#1298).

**Fit: best** — smallest footprint, single dashboard for "what's going
on everywhere", exactly the "sense of the estate" need.

### 2. Netdata — github.com/netdata/netdata

Per-host agent, zero-config beautiful dashboards, discovers podman
containers via cgroups automatically, systemd units visible, and
parent/child streaming gives one entry point. Deepest metrics
(processes, cgroup internals, eBPF).

- Cons: heavier agent (~150–300 MB RAM each), busy UI, long-term
  retention via cloud account (free tier exists but pushes Netdata
  Cloud).
- **Fit: strong #2** — best if we want deep per-host forensics
  (e.g. today's mddb wedge would've been instantly diagnosable).

### 3. Prometheus + Grafana + exporters — the "grown-up" stack

- `containers/prometheus-podman-exporter` (official containers org,
  active, podman v5) + `node_exporter` per host → Prometheus → Grafana.
- Pros: max flexibility, proper alertmanager, retention control;
  mddb already exposes `/metrics` — could scrape it directly.
- Cons: **most moving parts** — prometheus server, dashboards to build,
  3-4 exporters × 4 hosts; overkill for "what's going on" and it lands
  on the host we need to watch most.
- **Fit: only if we later need alerting/retention pipelines.**

### Rejected

- **Dozzle** — container logs only, no metrics.
- **Uptime Kuma** — availability checks; we already have mcp-health.
- **Glances** — great per-host TUI/web, no real multi-host aggregation.
- **Zabbix/cAdvisor** — enterprise weight / docker-only.

## Proposal

**Beszel hub on tony-dell** (always-on, tailnet, lightest VPS) —
agents on idc01, tony-omen, mn01, tony-dell. michael-ha can't run an
agent (HAOS appliance) — its health stays in HA + mcp-health instead.

```
tony-dell  beszel-hub :8090 (tailnet only)
    ↑ TCP 45876
idc01      beszel-agent (systemd unit, DOCKER_HOST=podman.sock)
tony-omen  beszel-agent (idem — sees GPU? via binary agent)
mn01       beszel-agent (idem)
tony-dell  beszel-agent (idem)
```

Effort: ~30 min — hub container/quadlet + 4 binary agents + one
`podman.socket` enable per host. Cost: ~50 MB hub + ~20 MB/agent RAM.

Optional phase 2: Netdata on idc01 only (the host that keeps hurting),
pointed at nothing — its per-host dashboard is standalone.

## Why not just scrape with Grafana?

Today the failure mode we actually fight is "host quietly saturated"
(mddb 8.6 GB OOM loop). Beszel shows that instantly with zero build
work. If we later need per-metric alerting or long retention, the
Prometheus path composes on top — nothing about Beszel blocks it.

docs.contentMd:
# Multi-model orchestration — expert-system structures to benchmark The umbrella term: **compound AI system** (Berkeley's name for it) — also called *model orchestration*, *ensemble inference*, or *LLM cascading* when the cheap model is tried first. The confirm-gate is already one: a specialist head in front of a general LM. ## Structures worth benchmarking on our fleet ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph S1[serial / cascade] A1[input] --> B1[student 30ms] B1 -->|conf ≥ T| D1[decide] B1 -->|low| C1[4b on idc02] --> D1 end subgraph S2[parallel vote] A2[input] --> B2[student] A2 --> C2[4b] B2 --> V[vote / weighted] C2 --> V --> D2[decide] end subgraph S3[router / MoE] A3[input] --> R{router head} R -->|confirm| E1[student] R -->|tool choice| E2[4b routing] R -->|memory recall| E3[mddb vector] E1 & E2 & E3 --> D3[decide] end subgraph S4[verifier / judge] A4[input] --> G[student decides] G --> J[4b audits only the
decision, not the task] J -->|veto| D4[reject] J -->|pass| D4 end ``` | structure | our pieces | cost | hypothesis | |---|---|---|---| | serial cascade | student →4b on conf<0.6 | ~30ms + rare 20s | near-student speed, 4b rescues edge cases | | parallel vote | student ∥ 4b | always ~20s | kills the student's imperatives blind spot | | router/MoE | tiny router picks expert | routing overhead + expert | best latency-accuracy but needs a router corpus | | verifier | student decides, 4b audits | 30ms + audit latency | catches false-confirms ("confirm delete…") | | **current** | student only | ~30ms | 92% baseline to beat | ## What to measure - golden confirm set (13) + tool-routing set (8) + a new **hard set**: imperative-lookalikes, code-switched TH/EN, "ok" non-confirmations - metrics: accuracy, p50/p95 latency, $/call proxy (cpu-seconds), calibration (ECE) ## Bench harness plan `tests/bench/orch-bench.py` — runs the same case set through each structure, one curve per structure. The pieces all exist already: student probe fn, 4b endpoint, the 13+8 golden cases. The new part is a `structure` param + composite scoring. ## Follow-up loop - [ ] `orch-bench.py` harness + hard-case set (~30 new cases) - [ ] run serial cascade — expect ~95% at <100ms median - [ ] if cascade wins: add conf-threshold fallback to tool_runner - [ ] if verifier wins: add veto pass to confirm gate - [ ] auto-retrain hook: bench misses → corpus append → retrain timer *Devin 2026-09-30 — parked ideas from fleet consolidation session.*

**audit** — look and count only. Measures and reports, touches nothing.

**prune** — delete old copies, keep the newest.

**consolidate** — merge duplicates into one.

**retention** — a standing rule that auto-deletes after X days. For logs, not memories.

**methodology** — the ordered way of doing a thing: the steps and the reason for their order.

**bloat** — data growing faster than it is useful.

## From Devin — memory words

**embedding** — turning text into a number-list (vector) so search can match by meaning, not just exact words.

**quantization (int8)** — shrinking those number-lists 4x smaller with almost no quality loss.

**HNSW index** — the fast "meaning lookup" structure. Loading it into RAM is what ate the memory.

**cursor** — a bookmark of "how far did we ship" so a sync resumes where it stopped.

**provenance** — a stamp recording which model made an embedding; if the model changes, old embeddings need redoing.

# สมุดคำศัพท์ของ Tony

สมุดคำศัพท์ของ Tony — คำที่โผล่มาในเซสชัน อธิบายแบบภาษาง่าย

สองแหล่งเติมหน้านี้:
- **Ada** จดคำเงียบๆ เมื่อเธอใช้คำที่ถูกแทนในบทสนทนา (vocab_note → ธนาคารส่วนตัวของ tony) แล้วซิงก์มาที่นี่
- **Devin** เติมคำจากเซสชัน Devin โดยตรง

## จาก Devin — คำเรื่องทำความสะอาดข้อมูล (27 ก.ย. 2026)

**audit** — ดูและนับเท่านั้น วัดแล้วรายงาน ไม่แตะต้องอะไรเลย

**prune** — ลบสำเนาเก่า เก็บแค่ตัวล่าสุด

**consolidate** — รวมของที่ซ้ำกันให้เหลือชิ้นเดียว

**retention** — กฎถาวรที่ลบของเก่าอัตโนมัติหลังครบ X วัน ใช้กับล็อก ไม่ใช้กับความจำ

**methodology** — วิธีทำเรื่องหนึ่งแบบมีลำดับ คือขั้นตอนและเหตุผลของลำดับนั้น

**bloat** — ข้อมูลที่โตเร็วกว่าประโยชน์ของมัน

## จาก Devin — คำเรื่องความจำ

**embedding** — แปลงข้อความเป็นชุดตัวเลข (เวกเตอร์) เพื่อให้ค้นหาตามความหมายได้ ไม่ใช่แค่ตัวอักษรตรงกัน

**quantization (int8)** — บีบชุดตัวเลขให้เล็กลง 4 เท่าโดยแทบไม่เสียคุณภาพ

**HNSW index** — โครงสร้างค้นหาตามความหมายที่เร็วมาก การโหลดมันเข้า RAM คือสิ่งที่กินเมมโมรี่

**cursor** — ที่คั่นบอกว่า "ส่งไปถึงไหนแล้ว" เพื่อให้ซิงก์ทำต่อจากจุดเดิม

**provenance** — ตราบันทึกว่าโมเดลไหนสร้าง embedding นั้น ถ้าเปลี่ยนโมเดลต้องทำใหม่

# Neuralink Project Deep Research Report

## Executive Summary

Neuralink, founded in 2016 by Elon Musk, is developing implantable brain-computer interfaces (BCIs). The company hit a major milestone in January 2024 with its first successful human implant in patient Noland Arbaugh. Despite controversies regarding animal testing and transparency, the FDA cleared further human trials, and Neuralink is advancing its goal of creating a next-generation device with significantly higher connection capacity than current approved BCIs. Key competitors include Synchron, Precision Neuroscience, and Blackrock Neurotech.

## Key Findings

### History & Mission
Launched publicly in 2017, Neuralink aims to build a BCI with over 100 times more brain connections than FDA-approved competitors.

### Milestones & Human Trials
- **Jan 2024:** First human implant.
- **2024:** Successful demonstrations by patient Noland Arbaugh.

### Competitors & Criticism
While under scrutiny for ethical and developmental protocols, Neuralink continues to address concerns publicly. Major competition comes from established players like Synchron (stent-based BCI) and Blackrock Neurotech, and newer firms like Precision Neuroscience.

docs.contentMd:
# NEWS Source Assessment — awesome-ai-news

*Assessed 2026-09-27 · repo: github.com/taielab/awesome-ai-news (55★, curated list of AI news/RSS aggregation tools)*

## What the list offers

Curated catalog across 10 categories: news aggregation, RSS processing, academic tracking, GitHub trending, social monitoring, podcast generation, message distribution, security news, static-site publishing.

## Fit to our stack (Ada + news-* CMS pages + chaba digests)

### High value — adopt patterns now

| Repo | Why it fits |
|---|---|
| **ai-news-radar** | 10+ source list with **failed-source handling** + OPML export — its source table is a ready-made seed for our news-* pages |
| **RSS-Master** | AI summarization + **scoring/dedup** of feeds — exactly the step our news pages lack (pages are Ada-written, no feed pipeline) |
| **clawfeed** | Multi-frequency digests (4h/daily/weekly) — mirrors our L1/L2 memory model; good template for a `news-daily` refresh cadence |
| **ai-trend-publish** | Multi-source → published page pipeline — same shape as our `cms_publish_page` + scenario flow, useful conventions to borrow |

### Structural fix — removes the web_search dependency

Our news flow currently leans on `web_search`, which **hit its quota** in the hosting-assessment run. An RSS-based ingestion removes that dependency entirely:

| Option | Shape | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| **FreshRSS** (self-host) | Canonical feed hub on tony-dell/idc02; Ada queries dedup'd items instead of searching | container + reader API |
| **FeedCraft** (Go) | HTML→RSS for sites with no feed (readyidc changelog, Thai gov/news pages) + AI prompts on feeds | single binary, cron |
| **RSS-Master** pattern | scoring + dedup + summaries into MDDB; news-* pages render from there | code, no new service |

Recommended path: **FeedCraft or direct feeds → MDDB doc per item → cms pages render from MDDB.** No new infra in v1; FreshRSS later if the volume justifies a reader.

### Distribution ideas (later)

- **TrendRadar-style** unified timeline + push channels → maps to our chaba-admin events / iPhone notifications, or LINE via yomi.
- **PodRSS / rss_ai_podcast** — RSS→audio brief; Ada already has TTS paths, so a spoken daily brief is feasible once the digest exists.
- **secfeed** — real-time security feed if we want a `news-security` page.

## Recommendations (ordered)

1. Seed the news-* sources table from ai-news-radar's curated list (tagged, with per-source health tracking — it handles failures explicitly).
2. Add an RSS ingestion job (FeedCraft or plain feedparser) writing scored/deduped items to MDDB — kills the web_search quota dependency.
3. Give news-* pages a cadence: clawfeed-style (4h/daily/weekly sections) via the existing scenario runner timer.
4. Later: push distribution (LINE via yomi / chaba-admin) + optional audio brief via Ada TTS.

## Not adopted

- **TelegramForwarder / RSS-to-Telegram-Bot** — Telegram-specific; we push to LINE/iPhone.
- **x-kit / social scrapers** — auth-heavy, brittle; low value per effort for our use.
- Static-site generators (Hextra) — we already have the miniapp/CMS rendering path.

docs.contentMd:
# News System

The `news-*` pages are Ada-maintained daily briefs. Grouped by slug prefix —
filter the page list by "news" or use the links below.

## Pages
- [News Headline](#/news-headline) — combined TL;DR, skim-first
- [News World](#/news-world)
- [News Thailand](#/news-thailand)
- [News Bangplee](#/news-bangplee)
- [News Tabsai](#/news-tabsai) — Bangsaen & Bangphra
- [News Flood](#/news-flood) — automated Thai flood feed

## Required structure — every news-* page MUST have ALL of these

The CMS audit fails any page missing one. Do not publish without them.

1. **H1** — `# <Title>` as the first line, matching the page title.
2. **TL;DR** — `TL;DR:` one sentence, concrete, no adjectives.
3. **3–5 items**, most actionable first. Each item:
   - headline ≤90 chars
   - 1–2 sentence summary
   - `Why it matters:` one concrete sentence
   - `[Source](url)` link to the article/site it came from
4. **Footer** — `*Updated HH:MM ICT*` at the bottom.

If a scope has no real news (e.g. Tasai), say so in the TL;DR and keep
only items actually relevant to that scope — do not pad with national
news that belongs on news-thailand.

## Update flow
1. `web_search` per scope (duckduckgo default, gemini fallback).
2. Draft in the format above → `cms_publish_page` (registers pending).
3. User confirms → resubmit with `confirmed=true`, then `cms_verify_page`.
4. Scenario `news-pages-update` in `tests/scenarios-live/` exercises this.

ถั่วเป็นอาหารที่มีสารอาหารและไขมันเยอะ มีประโยชน์ต่อร่างกาย หลายชนิดมีส่วนช่วยลดความเสี่ยงโรคมะเร็งและหัวใจ

- อัลมอนด์

- เฮเซลนัท
- แมคคาเดเมีย
- ถั่วลิสง (วาเลนเซีย)

- วอลนัท

ควรทานแต่พอดี ประมาณ **หนึ่งกำมือต่อวัน** การรับประทานมากเกินไปอาจทำให้เกิดผลข้างเคียงได้ เช่น ท้องอืด ท้องผูก หรือท้องเสีย เนื่องจากถั่วมีกากใยและไขมันเยอะ

subject: openjev-verdict-benchmark
title: open-jev backend benchmark — Verdict-151M vs gemma-3-4b

docs.contentMd:
# open-jev backend benchmark — Verdict-151M vs gemma-3-4b

**Date:** 2026-09-29
**Host:** tony-omen (i7-9750H 6c/12t, 32 GiB RAM, GTX 1650 4 GB)
**Question:** can Ada's `/v1/systemone` decision service stop burning 15.5 GiB RSS + ~400% CPU on omen?

## TL;DR

| Backend | Latency | Memory | Real-corpus accuracy (confirm-gate noul, n=31) |
|---|---|---|---|
| gemma-3-4b, torch CPU (live :8777) | 10–70 s | 15.5 GiB RSS | **31/31 vs regex** (calibrated: pos 0.999, neg 0.015) |
| gemma-3-1b, torch CUDA | ~0.28 s | ~2 GiB + 2.3 GiB VRAM | not evaluated on corpus; 0/3 agreement on HA probes |
| gemma-3-1b, torch CPU | ~3–9 s | ~5 GiB | same as 1b-CUDA |
| gemma-3-4b, CUDA | — | OOM (needs ~8.6 GiB fp16, card has 3.63 GiB) | — |
| **Verdict-151M (GLiClass/ModernBERT), CPU** | **~90–250 ms** | **~950 MiB, no GPU** | **10/31 single-label, 8/12 multi-label subset — fails zero-shot** |

## What was tested

1. `/score` option-scoring on 5 hand-written HA routing probes → Verdict looked perfect (5/5), 1b was wrong (0/3 vs 4b).
2. **Real corpus replay**: `~/.local/share/ada/jev-corpus.jsonl` on idc01 (31 rows captured by Ada's `jev_confirm_probe` — real user turns with regex labels + recorded 4b scores). Replayed verbatim through a wire-compatible Verdict shim on `127.0.0.1:8778`.

## Results on real data (the part that matters)

The real workload is **noul confirm-gate detection**: "the user turn was 'X' — did they affirm?" 

- **4b: essentially perfect.** Positives ~0.999, negatives ~0.015. Genuinely good at this task.
- **Verdict single-label softmax: no class separation at all** — pos mean 0.938, neg mean 0.916. Two-way softmax saturates when both hypotheses are weak.
- **Verdict multi-label (independent sigmoids): real signal, threshold-sensitive** — positives ~0.995; negatives spread 0.3–0.8. 8/12 on subset at P≥0.5.
- **1b (both devices): wrong picks on HA probes** — e.g. "turn off kitchen lights" for a dim-to-warm request.

## Conclusions

1. **Zero-shot model swaps are dead ends.** 4b's quality on this exact task is unusually good; every cheaper off-the-shelf option measurably degrades it. The earlier "Verdict will just work" hypothesis was wrong — synthetic probes overestimated it.
2. **The designed path is distillation, and the data already exists.** `jev-corpus.jsonl` is explicitly the "training data for a distilled confirm-gate student" (realtime_provider.py). 31 rows now, growing with every confirm-gate event. The 4b is effectively an expensive teacher labeling a corpus at ~12 s/row.
3. **The 4b's cost is partially self-inflicted.** It's advisory-only (regex enforces; Jev measures divergence + captures labels). We're paying ~400% CPU + 15.5 GiB for corpus labels, not for decisions.

## Options going forward

| Option | Cost | Expected outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Fine-tune Verdict/ModernBERT on jev-corpus + 4b-distilled augmentation | ~1 session + corpus growth | ~150M CPU model, <100 ms, task-calibrated. The intended endgame. |
| Tiny classifier on MiniLM embeddings (mn01:5000 already serves them) | logistic-reg on embeddings, ~1 file | cheapest student; needs the corpus to grow first (~200+ rows) |
| jevlike head on gemma-3-1b features | works on CUDA already | middle path; still needs labels |
| Keep 4b CPU but cap it (`CPUQuota=`, fewer threads) | 0 code | kills 10–70 s tail under contention; keeps corpus flowing |
| Retire the probe entirely | 0 | frees all resources; loses corpus + divergence signal |

## Artifacts

- Verdict shim (Jev-compatible, multi-label-capable): `tony-omen:/tmp/verdict_serve.py` (running on `127.0.0.1:8778`, ephemeral)
- Corpus replay scripts: `tony-omen:/tmp/replay_corpus.py`, `/tmp/replay_multi.py`; results `/tmp/corpus-ab.json`
- Corpus source: `idc01:~/.local/share/ada/jev-corpus.jsonl`
- Bench venv: `tony-omen:/tmp/vb` (torch-cpu, gliclass, fastapi)
- HF model cached: `heman10x/rlcd-modernbert-151m` (~600 MB) in omen `~/.cache/huggingface`

## Next actions suggested

1. Let the corpus grow (~200+ rows or a few weeks), meanwhile cap 4b CPU so it stops hurting Devin.
2. Fine-tune GLiClass on corpus + 4b-labeled augmentation → re-run this replay as the acceptance test (target: match 4b's 31/31 separation, pos ≥0.9 / neg ≤0.2).
3. Only then swap `ADA_JEV_URL` — keeping the same wire API means idc01 needs no code change.

subject: orchestration-conflicts
title: Orchestration conflict management

docs.contentMd:
# Orchestration conflict management — proposal

Date: 2026-09-27 · scope: Devin dispatches, Ada tool calls, job-run tasks
acting on shared resources (repos, dashboards, CMS pages, devices, hosts).

## Where conflicts bite today

| Conflict | Real example we hit |
|---|---|
| Same repo, two sessions | `pfg2-card.ts` duplicated render crash, version races → worktree-per-session rule |
| Same dashboard view | nobito + admin edits over websocket — last writer wins silently |
| Same device/entity | Ada voice toggles a plug while a job tests it |
| Same CMS slug | Ada republishes a page a dispatch session is regenerating |
| Same host lane | 3 sessions running heavy work on one host |
| Same deploy | concurrent `deploy-card.sh` — mitigated by `flock` today |

## Design: claim → check → act → release

### 1. Job claims (declared, durable)

Every dispatched/job-run task declares its **resource claims** in
`meta.json` + the job doc: `claims: [{repo: chaba, path: docs/kb/**},
{ha_view: chaba-home/nobito}, {host: tony-omen}, {device: switch.plug_tv}]`.

Dispatch wrapper derives defaults — `--repo chaba` implies
`{repo:chaba}`; `--host omen` implies `{host:omen}`.

### 2. Gate at dispatch time (not runtime)

`devin_dispatch` and `job-run start` check the job ledger first:

- **Conflict** (another `running`/`awaiting-user` job claims the same
  resource) → refuse with `conflict: job X holds repo:chaba` and let the
  caller decide: `queue` it (status `queued`, auto-starts when X closes),
  `proceed_anyway` (needs explicit confirmed), or cancel.
- Ada voice path: devin_dispatch already gates on confirmed — extend the
  deny message to name the conflicting job so Ada can tell Tony
  "job X owns chaba right now — queue it?"

### 3. Locks for hot single-writer resources

- `deploy-card.sh` already has `flock /tmp/pfg-deploy.lock` — keep.
- Dashboard mutations: `push-dashboard.py` gets a `--claim <view>` flag —
  the job doc records the view; a second mutation of the same view while
  a job holds it queues or fails loud.
- CMS slugs: `cms_publish_page` rejects if the slug is claimed by a
  running job (per-content-hash pending already exists — add claim check).

### 4. Ada voice commands vs running jobs

Voice is single-utterance — she shouldn't block. Rule:

- Voice command on a resource claimed by a running job → Ada answers
  "that's currently being changed by job X, want me to override?" —
  overrides go through the confirmed path and mark the job's doc
  `overridden_by: voice`.

### 5. Arbiter = this control desk

The foreground session is the arbiter: before dispatching N tasks, check
the ledger for overlapping claims and serialize them. The ledger query
(`devin_jobs`) already exists — extend it to return `claims` so a session
can plan a non-conflicting wave.

### 6. Resolution rules (documented precedence)

1. Explicit user instruction > everything
2. `awaiting-user` job + user answers → that job proceeds
3. Same-resource conflicts: first-claimed wins; second queues
4. Stale claims (`running` > 6h, no heartbeat) → auto-deny new writes,
   flag for review in the report feed

## What to build

| # | Piece | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `claims` on job docs + dispatch wrapper derives them | small |
| 2 | `devin_jobs` returns claims; Ada prompt: "check conflicts before dispatch" | small |
| 3 | Conflict gate in `devin_dispatch`/`job-run` (refuse/queue/proceed) | medium |
| 4 | `push-dashboard.py --claim` + view-level lock | small |
| 5 | stale-claim sweeper in dispatch-watch (heartbeat check) | small |

## Why this shape

Fits what exists: job docs are already the durable ledger, `flock` proves
the lock pattern, `devin_pending`/`devin_jobs` gives Ada visibility. No
new infra — claims ride on MDDB job docs, no central broker needed.

# Rain Radar Report

## Current Status
Waiting for user confirmation to start the rain radar notification system.

## Proposed Design
1.  **DataSource:** Thai Meteorological Department radar data (or available HA integration).
2.  **Notification Logic:** Trigger alert if a rain cloud cluster is detected within N km radius, moving towards Bangplee.
3.  **Action:** Send alert via LINE/Telegram with estimated arrival time and intensity.
4.  **Display:** Optionally show the live radar loop on Screen 1 when an alert is active.

## Timeline

  old DB copy has forensic value.
- **omen swap 28/71 GiB** — mostly in `/data/hibernate.swap`; Devin
  renderers hold most RAM. Drains slowly; reboot clears.
- **dell mddb follower** still replaying binlog backlog (leader reindex
  churn); converging on its own.
- **uv cache lock** — rerun `uv cache prune` on omen when idle.

# รายงานสไตล์การสื่อสารฉบับปรับปรุง

**สถานะ:** บันทึกในโปรไฟล์ | **ภาษา:** ไทย/อังกฤษ (ตามบริบท)

## สรุปการเปลี่ยนแปลง
ผู้ใช้ต้องการให้ดิฉันใช้คำที่บอกช่วงเวลาแบบสัมพัทธ์ (Relative Time) แทนการระบุวันเวลาที่แน่นอน เพื่อให้อ่านง่ายและเข้าใจได้ทันทีในการโต้ตอบ โดยเฉพาะในภาษาไทย (และภาษาอังกฤษเมื่อเหมาะสม)

**ตัวอย่าง:**
- "1 ชั่วโมงที่แล้ว" (1 hour ago)
- "เมื่อเช้านี้" (This morning)
- "เมื่อวาน" (Yesterday)

**การดำเนินการ:**
ดิฉันได้บันทึกความชอบนี้ไว้ในโปรไฟล์ส่วนตัว และจะนำไปใช้ในการสื่อสารกับผู้ใช้ (User) ทุกครั้งที่มีการอ้างอิงถึงช่วงเวลาในอดีตเพื่อให้ง่ายต่อความเข้าใจ.

docs.contentMd:
# รายงานปัญหาการใช้งานระบบ (System Incident Report)

**สถานะปัจจุบัน:** กำลังตรวจสอบและแก้ไข

## ปัญหาที่พบ

- **การค้นหาประวัติการสนทนาขัดข้อง:** ระบบไม่สามารถค้นหาข้อมูลจากประวัติการสนทนาย้อนหลังตามคำขอของผู้ใช้ได้ โดยมีการแจ้งเตือนว่าข้อมูลในหน่วยความจำหลักเพียงพอแล้ว ทำให้ข้ามขั้นตอนการค้นหาเชิงลึก
- **เครื่องมือ Session Recall ทำงานไม่สำเร็จ:** เครื่องมือ `ada_session_recall` ไม่สามารถดึงข้อมูลที่ต้องการออกมาได้ หรือถูกบล็อกโดยกระบวนการตรวจสอบข้อมูลซ้อนซ้อน (Redundant Data Check)

## การดำเนินการ

- แจ้งให้ Devin ทราบเพื่อดำเนินการตรวจสอบเชิงลึกเกี่ยวกับสาเหตุที่เครื่องมือค้นหาหน่วยความจำทำงานไม่น่าเชื่อถือ
- บันทึกปัญหาลงใน `devin-handoff` เพื่อให้ Devin เข้ามาซ่อมแซมระบบ

# Tiny on-device AI models (~43MB class) as a Chaba front-end preprocessor

**Deep Research report** — Gemini `deep-research-preview-04-2026` · 2026-09-27
· 46 grounded searches · ~2.26M input tokens · ~13 min runtime · est. $1–3

---



### 5.2 The Economics and Calibration of Escalation

The economic impact of this architecture is profound. Routine tool-selection and routing calls to cloud APIs accumulate massive costs at scale. By intercepting 80% to 90% of basic commands locally, a $30 CPU server can effectively replace tens of thousands of dollars in monthly API costs, while simultaneously preserving user privacy for routine domestic queries [cite: 3, 56].

However, the safety of this routing relies entirely on the calibration of the local model's confidence score. Relying strictly on the model's standard output probability distribution is insufficient, as modern LLMs—especially those heavily quantized—are notoriously overconfident on out-of-distribution prompts [cite: 40]. System engineers must enforce explicit verbalized confidence elicitation. This technique forces the model to mathematically rationalize its intent decision and append a numerical probability before finalizing its JSON output, ensuring that ambiguous or complex queries reliably fall below the confidence threshold and are safely handed off to the cloud [cite: 41].

## 6. Comprehensive Benchmark Plan

To validate the deployment of a 50MB model for this semantic routing task, a rigorous, multi-tiered benchmark plan must be executed prior to production. The evaluation must capture the nuanced trade-offs between ultra-low quantization, NLU accuracy, and deterministic hardware performance [cite: 57, 58].

| Benchmark Phase | Target Metric | Methodology & Datasets | Success Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Phase 1: NLU Accuracy** | Intent Accuracy | Utilize subsets of `Banking77` and `TREC` to test the model's ability to map diverse phrasings into a rigid taxonomy [cite: 30, 31]. Evaluate Thai dialect robustness using `SEACrowd` [cite: 44]. | $> 90\%$ accuracy on constrained local intents. Minimal degradation on Thai queries. |
| **Phase 1: Extraction** | Slot $F1_{\text{micro}}$-Score | Utilize `LLMStructBench` to test JSON generation [cite: 42]. Apply a heavier penalty ($\alpha = 0.25$) to false values over incorrect keys [cite: 42]. | $> 85\%$ F1 score with grammar-constrained decoding enabled in `llama.cpp`. |
| **Phase 2: Calibration** | Expected Calibration Error (ECE) | Measure the discrepancy between self-reported verbalized confidence and actual accuracy across 2,000 randomized queries [cite: 40, 41]. | ECE $< 10\%$. Establish an optimal escalation threshold ($\tau$) to minimize false positives. |
| **Phase 3: Latency** | TTFT & p95 Latency | Deploy the GGUF model via `llama.cpp` on the target hardware (Raspberry Pi 5 and Intel N150 iGPU). Measure Time to First Token (TTFT) and total generation time [cite: 53]. | p95 latency $< 200$ milliseconds for a complete 5-token payload. |
| **Phase 3: Hardware** | Peak RAM Consumption | Utilize memory profilers to monitor the peak footprint during context loading and the KV-cache expansion phase [cite: 57, 59]. | Strict adherence to the 50MB physical constraint under active conversational load. |

## 7. Conclusion

Deploying a functional Large Language Model within a strict 50MB envelope for on-device voice processing is mathematically and operationally achievable, provided engineering teams abandon traditional deployment methodologies. While foundational architectures like Qwen2.5-0.5B and Gemma 3 270M offer immense dense intelligence, applying standard 4-bit quantization leaves them far above the memory target. 

Success dictates the hybridization of advanced compression techniques: combining ultra-low-bit Imatrix quantization (1.5-bit to 2-bit) with aggressive embedding layer pruning to remove dead cross-lingual tokens. When structured through this rigorous pipeline and executed via highly optimized runtimes like `llama.cpp`, these micro-models operate as exceptional semantic routers. By leveraging prompt-based confidence elicitation to escalate complex queries to the cloud, systems can execute local commands instantly and privately while seamlessly relying on frontier models for complex dialogue, perfectly optimizing the balance between edge computing economics, privacy, and state-of-the-art capability.

docs.contentMd:
# tony-omen shutdown assessment

Assessment of what survives, degrades, or breaks while tony-omen is down —
run during the 2026-09-27 reboot window (zram 12G→24G, NVML driver fix,
post-migration validation). Ada + Devin collaboration.

## Ada's half (memory recall)

Ada's memory banks held only partial, partially-stale knowledge of omen's
role — she identified it as primarily an MDDB/AI-services host (MDDB actually
lives on idc01). The 2026-09-27 service migration had not yet distilled into
her banks. Finding: **recall quality gap** for same-day infra changes; the
live facts below are authoritative.

From system knowledge (corrected): tony-omen carried the interactive Devin
Desktop sessions, the yolo-xiaomi camera detector, the weaviate MiniLM
embedding service, weaviate-search API + nightly indexer, ollama, the
cast-desktop HLS stream, netdata, and Docker workloads.

## Devin's half (live host checks, 2026-09-27 ~20:45 +07)

- **Reboot clean.** nvidia-smi works (driver 595.91 both sides — NVML
  userspace/kernel mismatch resolved). zram now 24 GiB (was 12). Swap use
  ~0 (was ~14 GiB at 96% zram). Load ~4 (was 5-6).
- **Migration held through reboot.** `yolo-xiaomi` disabled/inactive on
  omen, active on mn01 — `/detect` live (0 persons, 3 detections) and HA
  `sensor.yolo_person_count` updates from `mn01:8780`.
- **Embedding path intact.** `weaviate-embedding` off on omen;
  `weaviate-embed-proxy.socket` holds localhost:5000 → mn01:5000.
  Post-reboot bug found + fixed: `weaviate-search.service` had
  `Requires=weaviate-embedding.service` which re-pulled the retired unit
  into a 114-restart crash loop — now requires
  `weaviate-embed-proxy.socket`; search API active on :3002.
- **Background CPU reduced.** netdata ~1.4% (was 26% at 1s interval → now
  5s); dockerd ~0% / containerd ~10% interval CPU (netdata's docker.sock
  polling had been the churn, not Docker itself).
- **mn01 absorbing fine.** yolo + embedding active, load ~2-3, 3.0/7.1 GiB
  RAM.
- **Expected-down with omen:** Devin Desktop sessions (incl. the 1122-msg
  `flannel-glitter` session), cast-desktop HLS stream, ollama, omen
  netdata, `weaviate-index` nightly timer (host-local; runs via localhost
  proxy whenever omen is up).
- **idc01 incident (same window):** MDDB OOM-killed 3× on the old 11 GiB
  host while tony-dell's follower resynced the 7 GiB binlog from LSN 0;
  host rebooted/resized to 31 GiB — MDDB healthy, resync re-running, no
  data loss.
- **CMS audit (new `cms-pages` audit):** 55 docs in `ada-cms-pages`, all
  satisfy the slug `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$` + meta contract
  (kind=page, title, format, updated).

## Follow-up checklist

- [x] Verify migrated services survive omen reboot (yolo on mn01, HA
      sensor, localhost:5000 proxy)
- [x] Fix weaviate-search → weaviate-embedding dependency leak
- [ ] Update SSOT for weaviate-search dependency correction
- [ ] Confirm weaviate-index 02:00 timer runs clean tonight via proxy
- [ ] Watch mddb follower resync to completion; consider binlog compaction
      (7 GiB) to shorten future resyncs
- [ ] Ada recall gap: same-day migrations aren't in her banks — consider a
      memory write or faster distill cadence after infra changes
- [ ] cms-pages audit enters weekly suite on next scheduled run

# Transcript audit — 2026-09-28 evening sessions

Evidence: idc01 journals + ~/.local/share/ada/transcripts. Sessions reviewed:
`286997a533` (18:17), `30df7726fc` (18:03), `cf25e5de69` (18:22),
`d5f0c2ffca` (18:26), `ac1fe3abda` (18:35–18:46), `5c342398b5` (19:13–19:14).

## Finding 1 — Phantom cast/display claims (FIXED, f15752d)

Session `ac1fe3abda` 18:45: Ada said "วิดีโอวอลล์จราจร แสดงผลบนสกรีน 3
เรียบร้อยแล้ว" and later "ภาพจากกล้องวงจรปิดเครื่องซักผ้า แสดงผลบนสกรีน 3
แล้วนะครับ" — **zero tool calls in the journal for the whole 18:35–18:47
window** (both ada-ha units checked). She asked for confirmation, got
"yes", then announced success without calling `cast_to_screen` or
`cctv_snapshot` at all. Worst class of bug — the user trusts it happened.

Fixes shipped (ada-pi f15752d):
- `_PHANTOM_CLAIM_RE` extended to display/cast completion claims
  (EN "now showing on screen"/"on screen 3"; TH "แสดงผล…แล้ว",
  "ขึ้นจอ…แล้ว", "ส่งไปที่จอ…เรียบร้อย"). Verified on the real utterances;
  offers ("อยากให้แสดงผลบนจอไหม") and intent ("กำลังจะส่งไปที่จอ") don't
  false-positive.
- `DEFAULT_ADA_INSTRUCTIONS` "DONE MEANS DONE" rule: never announce a
  screen/cast/capture as done unless the tool returned success this turn.

## Finding 2 — Traffic-camera call storm on dead cams (FIXED)

Session `5c342398b5` 19:13–19:14: **13 `traffic_camera` calls** — every
Pattaya/Chonburi match hit the iTIC 43-byte dead-frame stub and each
retry cost a full tool roundtrip. Fixes live: feed suspension filter
(`X.X.X.X`/`tempsus` stub records never become candidates),
provider walks up to 4 ranked candidates inside one call, suspended-area
queries return an honest "N matched but suspended" marker.

## Finding 3 — Geo-only traffic query always failed (FIXED, f15752d)

`traffic_camera(lat=…, lon=…)` with no keyword/heading always returned
"no match": distance subtracted from a zero base made every score <0.
Now `+60 − min(dist,100)` — verified: geo-only @BKK returns 5 ranked,
nearest 3.2 km; heading east/west both rank correctly.

## Finding 4 — Unverified "latest data" presented as fact (OPEN)

`d5f0c2ffca`: zero tool calls, yet Ada reported "จากข้อมูลล่าสุด" flood
details for Phayao/ม.พะเยา and self-contradicted Mae Sot distance
(200+ km → 70–80 km between adjacent turns). Candidate fix: instruction
to age-hedge model-memory claims ("ล่าสุดที่ผมรู้") unless a tool
confirms. Not yet shipped.

## Finding 5 — Speaker-ID still muddies identity (OPEN, known)

`ac1fe3abda`: KK enrolled mid-session; Ada then confused KK ↔ "คุณเซ" ↔
Tony across turns. Same root as memory-audit sticky-identity.

## Finding 6 — STT hallucinates languages on noise (OPEN, known)

PT/ES/KO/HI/ZH fragments logged as user turns on unclear audio. Ada
recovers gracefully; speaker-gate remains the open fix.

## Finding 7 — Silent clobbering of busy screens (FIXED, 0b15457)

`ac1fe3abda` + `30df7726fc`: Ada bounced screen 3 between God's Eye View
and the traffic wall, and flipped it to a CCTV snap — never acknowledging
she was replacing a running flow. `vcast_list` already carried the
ground truth (state, active_captures, camwall_zones) but cast_to_screen
reported it only *after* the publish.

Shipped (ada-pi 0b15457):
- `cast_to_screen` nav/play/image/audio/uplink onto a busy screen
  (capture lease, enabled camwall zone, or 'playing') returns
  `would_interrupt` + `needs_confirm` and does NOT publish; the retry
  needs `confirmed=true`, which only survives if the user's own speech
  affirmed (the confirm-stripping gate already enforced this — observed
  live blocking a self-certified `confirmed=True` on screen 2).
- Successful casts/walls that replaced something carry `replaced` —
  Ada must acknowledge aloud what was interrupted.
- Found along the way: `cctv_wall`'s declared schema lacked the
  `confirmed` param — Gemini rejected the flag so the confirm flow
  could never complete ("that tool doesn't accept it"). Fixed.
- Regression: `cast-interrupt-gate` scenario, in the casting suite —
  PASS live (gate refused, ask happened, yes → delivered + replaced,
  stop torn down).

## Environment notes

- Estate P2P (noble-a/noble-club via XMEye cloud) fully down — all panes
  "no video", snaps 503 after ~34 s; VMS restart didn't recover.
  Consistent with flood damage; honest-503 path verified.
- iTIC feed this morning: 36 live / 152 suspended of 188; of live-flagged
  only ~40% return real frames (rest are 43 B stubs / fixed 3 KB
  "No signal" jpegs). ~10–15 usable cams, all Bangkok/Nonthaburi.
- A second agent session was deploying ada-pi on idc01 during the bench
  (restarts at 07:38/07:40) — killed two scenario retries mid-run;
  deployed files verified to still match this branch afterwards.
- camwall zones seen enabled during the day: `rama9`→screen 2
  (since 09-28 13:53, leftover demo), `traffic`→screen 2 (later). The
  interrupt gate now protects these from silent clobbering.
- Screens 1 & 3 (iPads) were offline during the run — screen-1-targeted
  scenarios can't get delivered:1.

## Benchmark — casting suite (2026-09-29 07:11–08:35, idc01)

Latest per scenario — **10 pass · 3 flaky · 7 fail (score ≈ 0.61)**

| scenario | status | note |
|---|---|---|
| vms-camera-snapshot | pass | honest 503 path exercised + passed |
| camera_snapshot_offline | flaky | |
| cctv_snapshot_to_screen | pass | |
| cam-to-screen | flaky | |
| camera_cast_permission | fail | real — inspect |
| vcast-list | pass | |
| vcast-snapshot-probe | flaky | |
| vcast-screen-cast | fail | env — screen-1 iPad offline, stop→delivered:0 |
| vcast_cam_uplink | pass | |
| vcast-owner-allow | pass | |

title: Transcript audit 2026-09-29 — CCTV latency + voice-ID deadlock

docs.contentMd:
# Transcript audit — 2026-09-29 (CCTV latency + voice-ID deadlock)

## What Tony reported
"Still slow on cctv operations." Sessions: 06134715fd (wall casts), c66a8409e3 + 6b1005bb28 (voice enroll deadlock).

## Root causes found

1. **Wall start took 3 round-trips**: "send a wall" -> "which zone?" -> "confirm?" -> starts. Tony: "just go ahead, stop asking confirm." The capture-confirm gate fired even when the USER explicitly requested the wall — their ask IS the consent.
2. **Blank-wall blindness**: zone-a/noble-park walls cast fine but rendered empty (VMS P2P down -> all cams dead). Ada kept insisting "system says the wall is up" because she had no live-cam feedback. User saw "single camera and no picture", then "no table" on a traffic wall too.
3. **Voice-ID deadlock**: Tony's voice identified as KK (his print is stale/poisoned — code comment records "Tony's voice overwrote 'KK' after a borderline misidentification"). Both speaker_id guards then refused his genuine voice: contamination guard (matches KK) + own-voice check (doesn't match stale Tony print). ada_forget_speaker doesn't exist — no recovery path at all.
4. **Non-atomic wall writes**: a page fetch during puller write could read a truncated manifest/jpg -> "no manifest" / half frames.

## Fixes shipped

- **Owner-aware capture gate** (tool_runner._check_capture_confirmed): confirmed=true only required on secondary (recognized non-owner) turns. Owner explicitly asking = consent. Tool descriptions updated: "the request IS the consent — do not re-ask."
- **Wall health on start**: cctv_wall start now returns live_cams/total_cams + note_extra ("ALL cameras down — warn the user"). Ada can say "0/5 live, DVR uplink down" immediately instead of the user discovering a blank wall.
- **Enroll force path**: ada_enroll_speaker(confirmed=true) -> enroll_from_buffer(force) -> enroll(force) replaces the profile outright, skipping contamination + own-voice guards. Only allowed when target == session owner. Unlocks Tony's deadlock: say "fix my voiceprint", confirm, done.
- **Atomic writes**: manifest-*.json + thumbs write to .tmp then os.replace — page never reads half a file.
- **Wall page HUD**: when 0 cams live -> "all N cams down — showing stale/err" instead of a silent empty grid.
- **Split-screen panes** (earlier same session): layout 2-5, pane-routed casts, zoom/unzoom, per-pane stop; relay lastCast pane-keyed; registry tracks panes=N for pane-aware busy gating. split-screen scenario passed live.
- **Tool-name normalization**: c_c_t_v_wall -> cctv_wall (Gemini spells underscore names phonetically).

## Still open

- Tony's voiceprint must be re-enrolled once with the force path (then KK may need re-enroll if she still collides).
- VMS/XMEye P2P still down -> zone-a, noble-park, vms-* walls have 0 live cams.
- tony-house go2rtc returns 0B frames; chonburi HLS sources all dead.
- First-turn greeting race still occasionally eats turn 1 of scenarios.

## Report chain
transcript-audit-2026-09-28 (phantom claims, geo bug, interrupt gate) -> this.

subject: tv-action-cast-browser-20261002
title: tv_action/cast-browser — phantom clicks + WebGL outage 2026-10-02

docs.contentMd:
# tv_action / cast-browser — phantom clicks + GEV WebGL outage 2026-10-02

**Incident:** User asked Ada to click "Live Contacts" and "Don't show this
again" on GEV-on-TV. Ada claimed "clicked" x4; nothing happened. Separately,
GEV on the TV showed `Error constructing CesiumWidget`.

## Root causes (three stacked)

### 1. tv_action returned a fabricated arg-echo — phantom-write by design
`ha_client.tv_action` posted to HA `rest_command.tv_action` which is
**fire-and-forget** — the cast-browser `/cmd` response body was discarded and
the function returned `{cmd, text, ...}` regardless of outcome. A click on a
nonexistent element was indistinguishable from a successful one, so Ada
always claimed success.

**Fix:** `tv_action` now POSTs directly to cast-browser
`http://100.75.102.88:8799/cmd` (tailnet) and returns the real body; `{err}`
and `{ok:false}` raise as tool errors so the model sees failures.
`CAST_BROWSER_URL=""` falls back to the old HA path.
Commit `4f7a29c` (ada-pi), deployed to idc01.

### 2. Workspace/desktop casting dead — `set_workspace exit 1`
`cast-browser-server.mjs` (tony-omen `~/.local/bin/`, standalone — not
repo-tracked) hardcoded `DISPLAY=':1'` for xdotool/xprop/x11grab. tony-omen's
XFCE desktop runs on **`:0`** — the only X socket — so every workspace
switch failed. Hidden until fix #1 surfaced the error.

**Fix:** all 4 sites now use `X_DISPLAY` (env `CAST_X_DISPLAY`, default
`:0`). Backup: `~/.local/bin/cast-browser-server.mjs.bak-20261002`.

### 3. Cesium/WebGL dead in headless Chrome — `Error constructing CesiumWidget`
cast-browser launches Chrome `--disable-gpu` → WebGL context half-initializes
(Cesium's `powerPreference:"high-performance"` gets NULL on ANGLE-Vulkan too).
**Fix:** launch args now `['--no-sandbox','--enable-unsafe-swiftshader']` —
plain SwiftShader renders Cesium correctly (verified: globe imagery + HUD +
live flight markers after 'Contacts' click). GPU path is a dead end in
headless — tested Vulkan/ANGLE, gl-egl, ignore-gpu-blocklist.

## UX note — clicks update screenshots, not live pages
The TV shows **static PNG screenshots** (`shotAndCast` → HA `play_media` image)
— a click fires, page updates, new screenshot is cast (~15-35s). "Playing with
onscreen buttons" works but each action is a round-trip, not live interaction.

## Failure patterns to recognize

- Ada says "คลิกให้แล้ว" / claims success on click/nav but nothing changed:
  pre-fix this was invisible; post-fix the tool raises. If she still claims
  success wrongly, check the `function_call result` in `journalctl -u
  ada-ha-tony` for `tv_action` — the real error text is now in there.
- `set_workspace exit 1` → wrong DISPLAY for xdotool (desktop moved seats).
- `Error constructing CesiumWidget` / `context NULL` → headless WebGL
  regression; check launch args in `~/.local/bin/cast-browser-server.mjs`
  around `chromium.launchPersistentContext`.
- Click timeouts ~36s: `scrollIntoViewIfNeeded` + `loc.click` timeouts stack;
  the element name probably doesn't match the visible label (e.g. "Live
  Contacts" vs the DOM's "CONTACTS" — Ada now gets the real error and can
  retry with the correct text).

## Verified

- `/cmd click "Contacts"` on GEV → 200, live flights mode activated on the
  cast screenshot.
- `nav tony-omen:workspace:1` → `ok:true`, `cast-desktop@0.service` restarted
  itself, `camera.play_stream:200`.
- `tv_cast_control` scenario: PASS — Ada reports `set_workspace exit 1`-style
  failures honestly instead of claiming success.
