docs.contentMd:
# User Education — Correction Duty Policy

Status: **active** · adopted 2026-09-28 · enforced in CI

## What the policy is

Devin and Ada both carry a standing duty: **correct the operator plainly
when he asserts something factually wrong, misremembers a prior
decision, or proposes a wrong direction — accuracy over agreeableness.**
When a request rests on a misunderstanding, briefly explain the right
model instead of silently complying. Verify real state before
correcting; the duty is to be right, not contrarian.

## Where it lives (keep all three in sync)

| layer | location | mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Ada | `DEFAULT_ADA_INSTRUCTIONS` → Personality block, `backend/realtime_provider.py` (ada-pi) | system instruction injected per session |
| Devin | `AGENTS.md` → "Operator correction & education duty" (chaba) | repo rules, loaded every session |
| CI | `education_correction` scenario — `tools` suite, smoke tier | hourly regression test |

## How it is tested

`education_correction` runs in the hourly smoke suite. It feeds Ada a
**false premise** ("ada_v2 used YOLO for the cursor, right?") and a
**wrong-direction proposal** ("I'll drive the pointer from YOLO bounding
boxes"). Passing = she corrects toward MediaPipe landmarks both times
and never agrees. Failing surfaces on the `auto-report` page.

## Extending the coverage

Add a turn (or a new scenario) whenever a real correction incident
happens: phrase the trap the way the misunderstanding actually occurred,
assert the correct mechanism must be named, assert agreement phrases
must not appear. Domain sources that work well: kb-system docs, SSOT,
scenario/benchmark history — anything Ada can ground from a real
searchable fact.

## Why it exists

Sycophancy is the default failure mode of assistants — agreeing is cheap
and wrong. This policy makes correction contractual *and* continuously
verified, so it survives model updates.

_Updated by hand or by the benchmark runner; this page describes policy
state, not runtime data. Last verified: 2026-09-28 10:04._

## Document-first (spec-driven) configuration

**Umbrella terms:** *declarative* config, *spec-driven development*,
*docs-as-code*, *SSOT-driven*. The principle: the document is the
authority and machine config is generated from it — never the reverse.

### What it means for us

Chaba already does this — `ssot.mcp-tools.yml` is the doc, MCP server
configs are generated from it. The doc-first standard extends that
pattern: any config that a human might edit by hand should instead be
*derived* from a declared YAML/SSOT entry.

### Why it matters

| imperative (hand-edited) | declarative (doc-first) |
|---|---|
| config drifts from docs | doc and config can't diverge |
| "what does this box do?" needs `ps`/`ss` | read the doc |
| two sessions edit differently | one render, deterministic |
| audit = diff live vs memory | audit = diff live vs doc |

### The rule

If a setting can be declared in SSOT, it must be declared — the live
config is a generated artifact, not a second source of truth. The
`expected_exposure` tables in `ssot.security.*.yml` are already this:
they declare, `audit-security.py` diffs.

*Added 2026-09-30 — devin.*

# vcast playback failure — incident report

### Incident Report: vcast Playback Failure
**Time:** 2026-09-25 19:12
**User:** Tony
**Details:** User reported vcast screen 1 (iPad) showed black screen and
did not play video even after refresh and re-sending playback command.
System status indicated 'playing', but no visual output was observed on
the device.
**Devin Task:** Dispatched to investigate and fix playback issue, verify
with tests, and generate final report.

---

### Update — 2026-09-27

**Status: partially resolved — cast path hardened, black-screen root cause fixed in the tool layer.**

Findings and fixes since the incident:

- **Root cause class: tool-layer silent failure.** The cast *worked*
  server-side while status read 'playing' — iPad showed nothing because
  the action verb returned before the player attached. Two steering bugs
  made it look like a playback fault: `tv_action` was also answering
  lookup questions (cast instead of answer), and the HA client timed out
  at 5s while `nav`/cast takes ~6–10s.
- **Fixed**: `ha_client` per-call timeout raised to 45s (`a269fe9`) —
  the cast-complete response no longer aborts mid-flight; `tv_action` is
  now screen-display only (`b412b4a`); news lookups route to
  `web_search` (`42bc8c1`, `1f33052` for the grounding-quota revert).
- **Owner-locked casting** (`6a2ced7`, `5024c07`, `6b27155`): screens
  are speaker-gated — a guest/kid can't take over Tony's screen;
  `/pub` confirms via `ok:true` without echoing denial.
- **`cctv_snapshot`** (`f2e5951`): single-frame go2rtc peek pushed to a
  screen — gives Ada "eyes" on what a vcast screen actually shows
  (peek-per-request, no streaming overhead).
- **`/api/notify`** (`f9a5b49`): the backend can inject a system turn
  into the live voice session — cast results/ETA announcements reach
  Ada even when the action originated outside the conversation.
- **Scenario coverage**: `tv_cast_control.yaml` exercises cast verbs
  live; `cctv_snapshot_to_screen.yaml` covers the peek path.

**Still open:**

- [ ] vcast mechanics + remote-browser live verification on tony-dell
      (end-to-end play → iPad actually renders — not just status flags)
- [ ] A "did the screen show it?" post-cast check — `cctv_snapshot` of
      the target screen after cast to close the loop
- [ ] iPad black-screen device-side check (browser console) — only if it
      recurs after the tool-layer fixes

# Verified Working Routes — Ada / Home Infra

Point-in-time registry of routes proven end-to-end — not just a 200, but a device-side acknowledgement. Re-verify entries when infrastructure moves.

## Casting & displays

| Route | Path | Proof | Verified |
|---|---|---|---|
| GEV → living-room TV | `cast-browser :8799 /nav` → HA `media_player.play_media` → `media_player.tony_tv_cast` (Skyworth SKWAMX3) | TV ack: `app=Default Media Receiver`, `media_content_id`=rendered GEV frame | 2026-10-01 |
| TV power cycle | `switch.plug_tv` + `script.cast_power_on` (HA) | plug history shows 8+ programmatic cycles | 2026-09-24 |
| Ada → vcast screen 6/7 | Ada `cast_to_screen` → input-bridge relay :3010 → real browser `vcast-real@N` | `vcast-real-6/7` registered + connected; real GEV render on idc02 | 2026-09-30 |
| CCTV frame → screen | `cctv_snapshot` → `_cctv_grab` → relay `{type:image}` | still-image path; no stream needed | 2026-09-30 |
| noble-club snapshot | `vms-snap` mn01 :8377 `/snap?ch=Swimming Pool` | HTTP 200, ~571KB PNG, ~17s | 2026-09-30 |

## Voice / memory / CMS

| Route | Path | Proof | Verified |
|---|---|---|---|
| Voice turn pipeline | mic → Gemini Live (gemini-3.1-flash-live) → tool calls → audio out | 18-turn session; median reply gap 7s | 2026-10-01 |
| CMS publish | `cms_publish_page` → MDDB `ada-cms-pages` | `today-plan` + `gev-test-report-20261001` live | 2026-10-01 |
| Memory recall | `ada_memory_search` → MDDB banks | recall worked (Kaewta nickname hit) | 2026-10-01 |

## Known-broken / gated

- `media_player.tv_40c5000` (Samsung, foreign Naris network) — **disabled in HA**; cast allowlist refuses it.
- `media_player.lg_webos_tv_nano81tsa` — stale entity, removed from all registries.
- `noble-a` VMS channels — DVR offline; do not claim until a real frame returns.
- GEV flood-history layers — built+tested on branch, **not deployed**.

## Cast-target policy (new)

Only `media_player.tony_tv_cast` and `media_player.tony_tv` may be cast targets — enforced in `cast-browser-server.mjs` `CAST_ALLOWLIST`, screens.json destinations, and the disabled HA entity. Naris USB-dongle (wlx00761100125e) admin-down + `autoconnect=no` — kills neighbor-device discovery and the flap storms that starved HA's executor.

subject: vms-wall-outage-20261001
title: VMS camera-wall outage 2026-10-01 — runbook

docs.contentMd:
# VMS camera-wall outage 2026-10-01 — diagnosis & fixes

**Incident:** noble-a and noble-club walls showed 0/N live cams (all error tiles /
"black page") for ~40h while the DVRs were actually up — verified working in
XMEye Pro at the same time. Ada's `cctv_wall` calls worked; the thumbs behind the
wall were all dead.

## Root causes (three stacked bugs)

### 1. vms-snap `_has_video` threshold rejected live night video
The dead-pane check measures mean neighbor luma delta. Threshold was **60**;
real night footage (noble-a Road In, 20:26) measured **58.1** on a genuinely
streaming pane → 503 "pane shows no video". Dark scenes compress deltas.
**Fix:** threshold 60 → **45** in `stacks/services/xmeye-vms/vms-snap.py`
(dead pane ~5, mosaic dilution ~31 — margin still wide). Deployed to mn01
`~/.local/share/xmeye-vms-stack/vms-snap.py`, service restarted.

### 2. noble-a device group collapsed in the VMS tree
The DVR's cloud session flaps periodically; when it does, the `noble-a` group
**collapses** (children vanish). Every channel click then hits empty tree space
and the shim's drift check correctly 503s ("selected row y=… does not match").
**Fix/workaround:** click the group header (~1100,385) to expand; rows then sit
at the calibrated `channels.json` coords again. Recurrent — the drift check is
the right sentinel.

### 3. VMS container wedged + watchdog restart needs the 0,0 ritual
`xmeye-vms.service` was SIGKILLed at 20:06 after a wedge. After restart the Wine
app needs **click (0,0) once for login, again for draw** before streams attach —
until then every snap reports "pane shows no video". (Also risk: watchdog's
3×no-video restart loop can fire spuriously while the app is in this state.)

## Efficiency fix shipped with it

- `vms-snap.py` gained **`?zoom=0`**: skips the single-pane zoom/re-attach dance
  (12–36s/cam) — wall thumbs only need grid-res (528×273). ~15s/cam.
- `cam-wall-pull.py` calls `snap?ch=…&zoom=0` — an 8-cam zone now fits inside
  `VMS_BUDGET` (180s) in one sweep instead of starving the tail cams every cycle.

**Puller note:** the systemd unit on tony-dell runs from
`~/CascadeProjects/chaba-tony-dell/` (not `chaba/`). Edits must land in that
checkout — or better, a fast-forward pull once changes are committed on master.

## Verification

- `/snap?ch=1. Road In&zoom=0` → 200, real PNG
- Puller sweep 22:25+07: **noble-club 8/8, noble-a 5/5** thumbs live
- `wall_ops` live scenario on idc01: **PASS** (status/settings/status round-trip)
- Wall pushed to screen 3 manually via input-bridge `nav` (delivered=1)

## Runbook — "wall shows all-error/black"

1. `curl -s http://100.106.196.22:8377/health` — shim alive?
2. Snap one cam: `/snap?ch=1.%20Road%20In&zoom=0`. Read the JSON error:
   - `device tree layout drifted` → tree group collapsed or re-sorted —
     screenshot the desktop (`xwd -root` on :99), expand the group or
     recalibrate `channels.json`.
   - `pane shows no video` → check the pane really is dark (screenshot); if it
     visibly streams, suspect the `_has_video` threshold again.
   - `unknown channel` → channel name changed / DVR offline.
3. VMS app dead entirely → `systemctl --user restart xmeye-vms` on mn01, then
   **click (0,0) twice** before expecting streams.
4. Watchdog note: 3 consecutive no-video snaps auto-restart the VMS
   (`NOVIDEO_COOLDOWN_S=900`) — a collapsed tree does NOT trigger it (drift
   check raises before the video check).

## Data lost / blast radius

- Walls showed status cards instead of thumbs for ~40h (noble zones only;
  traffic/HLS zones unaffected).
- Ada correctly reported "all cams in this zone are down" — the tool contract
  worked; the data behind it was wrong.

_Generated by Devin session, 2026-10-01 — chaba commits 5af1e75f + 39c4ac9a._

# Voice Latency & Transcript Assessment — 2026-10-01

Assessment of Ada voice session `cd79bfc889` (07:20–07:25 +07, backend `ada-ha-michael` session `b567f66943`).

## Measured latency

- User→Ada reply gap (transcript timestamps, 18 turns): **median 7s, mean 6.8s, max 11s**
- Backend response durations (`duration_ms`): 10s–32.5s; first audio chunk arrives before completion
- Felt delay of "a few seconds" is real and consistent — every turn pays ~7s

## The UPS turn (what actually happened)

```
00:25:15  user: "ซ่อมเครื่อง UPS ที่บ้าน… iMac ของ KK" (81 chars)
00:25:16  tool call: get_rk600_weather   ← wrong tool
00:25:36  response completed (19.7s turn)
00:25:44  session closed — user had already left
```

Ada wasn't broken — she took ~21s because the UPS question fired `get_rk600_weather` (irrelevant) and then generated a long answer the user never heard.

## Root causes

1. **Tool-call misfire** — battery/UPS semantics near-missed a weather tool. Wrong tool = +5–8s and polluted answer context.
2. **Context bloat** — per-turn input tokens ran 29k–50k (cumulative 276k). Each Gemini Live turn resends history; larger context = slower first-audio.
3. **Memory pollution** — `ada_memory_search` returned a 43KB Devin CLI session dump (system prompts + full transcript) as a memory hit, score 0.74. Should never be in an Ada bank.
4. **mddb write storm** — `mddb update_document failed` ×27 in one second at 00:22:13 during `ada_memory_search`/remember writes. Silent in transcript but burns latency.
5. `ada_remember` self-asserted `confirmed=true` once — correctly stripped and denied by the gate.

## Recommendations

- Cap/prime conversation injection; compact history after N turns (biggest latency lever).
- Tighten tool descriptions for weather/UPS-class disambiguation ("only call weather tools when the user asks about weather").
- Purge Devin transcript dumps from `ada-*` banks; add an ingest filter (reject docs containing `<available_skills>`/system-prompt markers).
- Fix `mddb update_document` failures — 27 errors in 1s suggests a retry loop or bad doc id; check MDDB logs.
- Batch `ada_remember` calls — every "บันทึกไว้ให้แล้ว" turn does a write; queue them.

Generated by Devin session 2026-10-01 · sources: ada transcript cd79bfc889, ada-ha-michael journal, MDDB


## Fixes applied (same session, commit ada-pi@33b29d7)

- `memory_ops._doc_to_hit` — hit content capped at `ADA_HIT_MAX_CHARS` (2000): a surfaced devin session dump now injects a 2KB excerpt + key, not 50KB raw
- `memory_ops.record_use` — skips docs already `last_used`-stamped today: kills the per-search rewrite storm (the ×27 timeout burst)
- `mddb_client` — logs exception type on update failures (empty httpx timeout strings made the storm invisible)
- `get_rk600_weather` — description scoped to explicit weather queries only (the UPS misfire); `control_media_player` example now `media_player.tony_tv`

## Notes on the "pollution" finding

The `devin` bank is **by design** — a read-only handoff store (`bank=devin`, `writable=false`, 1000+ session docs from `devin-cli`). It is not stray data. The bug was recall scope + injection size, fixed above. No purge needed.

## Verification

- `tv_cast_control` scenario (5 turns, real TV): **PASS** after the cast allowlist patch
- Unit checks: `record_use` dedupe + hit cap verified; small docs unaffected
- `chaba-guest` restarted on patched code — boots clean
- idc01 backends still run pre-patch code until the checkout there is updated (separate session owns its dirty tree) — restart pending approval

title: VPS hardening + perf tuning — 2026-09-30

docs.contentMd:
# VPS Security Hardening + Performance Tuning — fleet report

Researched 2026-09-30 against Ubuntu 24.04 hardening guides (StackHarden,
PrivateDevOps, ventx) + sysctl/perf sources (RamNode, unquietwiki,
podman discussion #28320), cross-checked against our fleet state
(idc01/idc02 VPS, mn01, tailnet layout).

## Hardening — what's agreed across guides, and our state

| Practice | Consensus | Our state |
|---|---|---|
| Non-root sudo user | mandatory first step | ✅ done (tony, uid 1000) |
| SSH keys only, PasswordAuthentication no | mandatory | ⚠ deviation — key auth works; password kept on both idc01/idc02 as panel-recovery fallback |
| PermitRootLogin no (or prohibit-password) | mandatory | ⚠ root ssh allowed; key-only now works — can tighten |
| sshd hardening via drop-in (`sshd_config.d/*.conf`) | best practice — first-match wins, survives package updates | ❌ not applied |
| UFW deny-inbound | mandatory | ✅ both VPS |
| Fail2Ban | worth it for logs + non-ssh services; ssh itself is key-only so mostly noise reduction | ❌ not installed |
| unattended-upgrades (security-only) | mandatory | ❌ not verified — check `apt-cache policy unattended-upgrades` |
| auditd | recommended for post-incident | ❌ not installed |
| chrony (time sync) | cheap, prevents TLS/log drift | ❌ not verified |
| AppArmor left on | verify, don't disable | ⚠ verify |

**Key nuance (ventx):** Ubuntu 24.04 uses `ssh.socket` activation — a custom
`Port` in `sshd_config` is *silently ignored*. Any port change must go
through the socket unit, not the config file.

## Performance tuning — the worthwhile subset

| Knob | Guide value | Apply? |
|---|---|---|
| `net.core.default_qdisc=fq` + `net.ipv4.tcp_congestion_control=bbr` | everywhere; idc01 already has it in `/etc/sysctl.d/90-bbr.conf` | ✅ apply idc02 (kernel 6.8 has bbr) |
| `vm.swappiness=10` | standard on VPS | ✅ |
| zram | guides enable it on <4G; idc02 has 15G so swap file suffices | optional |
| `fs.inotify.max_user_watches=524288` | needed for mddb/watcher-heavy services | ✅ if idc02 hosts mddb replica |
| noatime in fstab | standard for SSD vda | check fstab |
| `net.core.somaxconn=8192`, `tcp_max_syn_backlog` | only if websock/bridge heavy | ✅ input-bridge/vcast pattern |
| `LimitNOFILE` per systemd unit | **the real gotcha** — systemd units ignore `limits.conf`, default 1024 bites mddb-type services | ✅ set `LimitNOFILE=65535` on mddb/ada units |
| I/O scheduler `mq-deadline` on virtio-ssd | standard | check `/sys/block/vda/queue/scheduler` |

**Container practice (podman #28320):** dedicated nologin system user per
service + `loginctl enable-linger`, not containers under your own login —
isolates escapes, survives reboots, scopes journald. Our current pattern
(`tony` user + linger) works; the hardened variant is `svc-*` users for
multi-workload hosts.

## Recommended next actions (idc02 as clean slate)

1. `sshd_config.d/10-hardening.conf` — MaxAuthTries 3, LoginGraceTime 20,
   KbdInteractiveAuthentication no, AllowAgentForwarding no, X11Forwarding no
   (keep PasswordAuthentication deviation noted in ssot.security.idc02.yml)
2. `apt install fail2ban unattended-upgrades auditd chrony` + enable
3. `/etc/sysctl.d/90-tuning.conf` — bbr+fq, swappiness, somaxconn,
   inotify watches
4. After tailnet join: `ufw allow in on tailscale0`, delete public :22,
   PermitRootLogin prohibit-password
5. Service units get `LimitNOFILE` + `MemoryMax` where relevant (we
   already use MemoryMax on open-jev)

*Sources: stackharden.com/guides/ubuntu-baseline,
privatedevops.com ubuntu-2404 checklist, ventx.de linux_hardening_basics,
ramnode sysctl tuning, unquietwiki sysctl-linux,
github.com/containers/podman/discussions/28320.*

docs.contentMd:
# Weather Station Details

Location: Michael's site (terrace installation).

## Hardware — all inside the same cabinet

- **Logger:** Rika RK600-07B
- **Sensor head:** RK900
- **HMI:** Samkoon AK070AB / AK-070MG (Android 4.2.2, app `ak_v_2.1.3_521_20190327`, SN `AKG229221907000048`), IP `192.168.31.148` (telnet :23 open, root, no password)
- **ESP32** (`esp32dev`, no PSRAM): repurposed 2026-09-25 as dedicated BLE bridge, node name `jkbms`, at `192.168.31.231`. USB-serial (CH340) cabled to the HMI's USB port.
- **Battery pack + BMS:** JK BMS, advert name **`24v20ah`**, MAC **`20:23:04:32:0D:14`** — an 8S LiFePO4 "24V 20Ah" pack powering the station. BLE service `FFE0`, protocol JK02_32S.

## Working data paths

- Weather data: Modbus-TCP `192.168.31.148:502` — e1 wind dir, e2 wind speed, e3 temp x10, e4 humidity x10, e5 rain (nonzero only when raining). e6+ unused.
- Cloud upload: HMI → `39.99.253.232:8899` (~1 row/min). Watchdog `rika-watchdog.service` on tony-omen re-adds the default route after flaps.
- Facility/device ID `22100502`, account `R22100502` (credentials in `~/.config/secrets/rikacloud.env`).
- **Battery data: ESP32 `jkbms` → BLE → JK BMS → Home Assistant.** All `sensor.terrace_weather_station_bms_*` entities live and updating every ~10 s.

## Battery/BMS — CONNECTED (2026-09-25 ~17:35)

The BMS advertises as `24v20ah` (MAC `20:23:04:32:0D:14`, RSSI -43 dBm at the ESP32 — inside the cabinet). It only started advertising after Michael power-cycled the cabinet — the BLE module appears to sleep/stop advertising while idle, which is why a 12 h+ continuous scan heard nothing.

**Live readings:**

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Pack voltage | 25.89 V (8S LiFePO4) |
| SOC | 81 % (16.27 Ah of ~20 Ah) |
| Current | -0.15 A discharging (~3.9 W station load) |
| Cell voltages | 3.232–3.241 V, delta 9 mV — well balanced |
| Temperatures | pack 26.7 °C, MOS 30.9 °C |
| Cycles / SOH | 91 / 100 % |
| BMS uptime | ~1y 344d |
| Errors | `0x00080000` "Modify password in time" (default-password nag only) |

Key detail: `protocol_version: JK02_32S` — the older JK02_24S profile produced garbage SOC/capacity on this firmware (version-2/3 frames).

## False leads (resolved)

- `SCharger-7KS-S0-NS2351395951` (`58:56:C2:C8:EE:62`) = Michael's Huawei EV wallbox, not the BMS.
- SolarAssistant dongle (`192.168.1.120`) monitors only the house Solis bank (battery_1/2/3, ~51 V) — unrelated.
- HMI serial: `ttyO1` decoded 2026-09-25 = the **RK600 weather logger's** Modbus-RTU feed (`01 03 1a` + CRC16, ~1 Hz while screen on; wind/temp/humidity float32s) — NOT the battery controller. `ttyO0` idle. No wired path to the BMS exists; BLE is the only interface.

## ESP32 recovery path (built 2026-09-25)

Remote serial through the HMI: userspace tool `espusb` (source `esp32/espusb.c` in chaba repo; binary `/data/local/tmp/espusb2`+`espusb3` on the HMI) talks CH340 over USBDEVFS ioctls — console read, DTR/RTS download-mode reset, plain EN-pulse reset, SLIP flash. Used to flash `jkbms.factory.bin` entirely remotely. OTA via SSH tunnel through michael-ha (local 3232/6053 → 192.168.31.231, script `/tmp/esp32-tunnel.sh` on tony-dell).

Wake watcher: `/root/hmi-watch.sh` on michael-ha pings .148 every 15 s → `binary_sensor.hmi_up` in HA.

## Timeline

- 2026-09-22: Cloud upload outage root-caused — HMI lost default route; fixed + watchdog installed. BLE survey from michael-ha: no BMS advert (thought to be range).
- 2026-09-23: Rain path verified end-to-end. SCharger identified as Huawei EV wallbox.
- 2026-09-24: Decided to build ESP32 JK-BMS BLE bridge (`esp32/jkbms.yaml`).
- 2026-09-25 am: Merged display+BLE firmware flashed to esp32test; board went dark — actual cause = repo wifi list lacked Michael's SSIDs (not a crash).
- 2026-09-25 ~10:36: accidental `input keyevent 26` suspended/powered off the HMI → weather + cloud stopped; needed physical power cycle.
- 2026-09-25: Remote serial path built; `jkbms` firmware flashed; node online at .231.
- 2026-09-25 ~16:29: Michael power-cycled cabinet → HMI back, route auto-restored, uploads resumed. ESP32 had hung on the power cut — revived remotely via EN-pulse over the CH340.
- 2026-09-25 ~17:35: **BMS advert `24v20ah` seen at -43 dBm on first boot after power-cycle; MAC set, JK02_32S flashed, CONNECTED. All battery entities live in michael-ha.**

## Pending

- Nothing blocking. Optional: rename device in JK app, set a real BMS password (clears the `0x00080000` nag — password lives in `~/.config/secrets/jkbms.env`), dashboard tile for the station battery.
- If the BLE link ever drops long-term, check whether the module went back to sleep — power-cycling the cabinet revives it.

subject: yomi-vs-line-bot
title: Yomi vs LINE bot

docs.contentMd:
# Yomi vs LINE bot

Two distinct LINE-related services are active in this system. Do not confuse them.

### Yomi (Message Archive)
Yomi **reads** and **analyzes** LINE chats. It pulls conversations, generates summaries, and makes them searchable.

- **Purpose:** Archiving and searching past conversations.

### LINE bot (Notifications)
The LINE bot **writes** and **sends** messages. It handles outbound alerts and notifications to the user.

- **Purpose:** Sending system notices and reminders.

---
**Rule of thumb:** Yomi reads, the bot writes.
